pages.en:
LE III. REICH...

...n'est qu'une caricature. Tous les peuples civilisés, en le regardant, sont pris d'un sentiment de dégoût, quelquefois d'une envie de rire. Il n'y a rien que les seigneurs du III. Reich détestent plus que ce rire, que les traits d'esprit, bien souvent forgés dans leur propre camps. Ils savent que le ridicule tue.

Depuis un an, nous collectionnons tous les „mots“ et toutes les caricatures ayant trait à l'hitlérisme. Aujourd'hui nous vous en présentons les meilleurs. Le cahier que nous nous permettons de vous soumettre contient plus de cent dessins, ceux-ci sont l'oeuvre de caricaturistes européens les plus renommés; très différents quant à la conception artistique, tous portent la marque d'une seule et même conviction pouvant être résumée par la formule: „Il faut sauver le monde de la barbarie brune!“

Le cahier, fort de 52 pages 35 × 25 cm est orné d'une couverture en trois couleurs. La préface a été écrite par Heinrich Mann.

Il paraîtra au début du mois d'août, en trois langues (français-allemand-anglais) aux éditions du „Simplicius“. Le prix est marqué très bas, afin de rendre l'édition accessible à tous, et pour que la lutte contre le péril brun puisse s'engager sur une base très large.

pages.zh:
第三帝国……

……不过是一幅漫画。所有文明民族在注视它时，都会产生厌恶感，有时甚至想发笑。第三帝国的老爷们最痛恨的莫过于这种笑声，以及那些往往出自他们自己阵营的妙语。他们知道， ridicule（嘲笑）能置人于死地。

一年来，我们收集了所有与希特勒主义有关的“言论”和漫画。今天，我们向您展示其中最好的部分。我们冒昧呈献给您这本小册子，内含一百多幅画作，这些作品出自欧洲最著名的漫画家之手；虽然艺术构思各不相同，但都打上了同一种信念的烙印，可概括为：“必须将世界从棕色野蛮中拯救出来！”

这本小册子共 52 页，尺寸为 35 × 25 厘米，饰有三色封面。序言由海因里希·曼 (Heinrich Mann) 撰写。

该书将于八月初由“辛普利库斯”出版社以三种语言（法语、德语、英语）出版。定价极低，以便让所有人都能买得起，并使反对棕色危险的斗争能在非常广泛的基础上展开。

pages.en:
A CONSUMMATIONA CONSUMMATION DEVOUTLY TO BE WISHED

FLASH! FLASH! FLASH!
HITLER DEAD
TYRANT OF GERMANY "EXECUTED"

Famous "Leader" Found Dead in Mountains

The dismembered body of Chancellor Adolf Hitler was found in a dripping crevice, 12 miles south of his mountain home at Berchtesgaden. The partly decomposed head lay 40 feet from the torso and arms.

Missing from the Chancellory in Berlin the past two weeks, the Fuehrer, dead, was discovered by the Black Guards, who stumbled over his corpse and ended a search which had been made in every part of Europe.

Evidently two assassins were implicated; they left a note in the coat pocket of the body indicating that their motive was revenge for the Fuehrer's countless murders and his persecution and torture of Jews and Catholics since first seizing power in 1933.
pages.zh:
求之不得的圆满结局

快讯！快讯！快讯！
希特勒已死
德国暴君被“处决”

著名“领袖”被发现死于山中

阿道夫·希特勒总理的肢解尸体在贝希特斯加登 (Berchtesgaden) 山区住所以南 12 英里处的一个滴水的裂缝中被发现。部分腐烂的头颅距离躯干和手臂 40 英尺。

过去两周在柏林总理府失踪的元首，死后被黑卫队发现，他们绊到了他的尸体，结束了在整个欧洲进行的搜寻。

显然有两名刺客涉案；他们在尸体的大衣口袋里留下了一张纸条，表明他们的动机是报复元首自 1933 年首次掌权以来犯下的无数谋杀罪以及对犹太人和天主教徒的迫害和折磨。

pages.en:
2

The remains of the Lord High Executioner, President and Chancellor of the Third German Reich lie today in two burlap sacks in the common morgue of Munich.

“What He Deserved” Verdict of Man in Street.

Though considerable surprise is felt, most people outside Germany seem to feel that Hitler’s death is a blessed relief, and his assassins have already been dubbed “deliverers”. It is not only the Jews and Catholics, who have fled to every part of the world, who hold this view. The entire public save for the immediate members of the Fuehrer’s party, his intimates and followers, are offering thanks. “Civilization is safe” is the common sentiment. In Germany, of course, it is still considered unsafe to express such views. Tension is lifting, however, particularly since it has been learned that Goering and Goebbels are in jail on the charge of conspiring to “liquidate” the Fuehrer. . . . .

* * *
pages.zh:
2

这位德意志第三帝国的最高刽子手、总统兼总理的遗骸，今天躺在慕尼黑公共停尸房的两个麻袋里。

“他罪有应得”——普通人的裁决。

尽管人们感到相当惊讶，但德国以外的大多数人似乎觉得希特勒之死是一种幸事，他的刺客已被称为“解放者”。持这种观点的不仅是逃往世界各地的犹太人和天主教徒。除了元首政党的核心成员、亲信和追随者外，全体公众都在表示感谢。“文明得救了”是普遍的情绪。当然，在德国，表达此类观点仍被认为是不安全的。然而，紧张局势正在缓解，特别是自从获悉戈林和戈培尔因涉嫌密谋“清除”元首而被捕入狱以来……

* * *

pages.en:
3
The foregoing is fictional, but not entirely imagin-
ary. A world is impatiently waiting for this news, the
biggest and best story we can hope to read in our
morning papers. In all probability we need not wait
too long, either . . . not ten years, not five, nor even
two.

IT IS PROBABLY A MATTER OF MONTHS.

A group of young men have organized for the ex-
press purpose of putting a stop to the butcheries of
Hitler and his gangsters, led by Goering and Goebbels.
They are not afraid of death. They are motivated by
shame that their beloved nation has for so long been
headed by a blood-frenzied pervert. Unless they are
martyred first, they will deliver Germany from her
humiliation.

General Hermann Goering, Minister of Prussia (not
to mention countless other offices created by himself)
and Dr. Josef Goebbels, Minister of Propaganda and
Public Enlightenment, both detest Hitler and would
gladly see him done away with —but only in the hope
that they can take his place. Each of them has the
pages.zh:
3
 foregoing 内容是虚构的，但并非完全凭空想象。整个世界正不耐烦地等待这一消息，这是我们在晨报中能读到的最大、最好的新闻。很可能我们无需等待太久……不需要十年，不需要五年，甚至不需要两年。

这可能只是几个月的事。

一群年轻人为了明确制止希特勒及其由戈林和戈培尔领导的匪帮的屠杀行为而组织起来。他们不怕死。他们的动力来自于羞耻感，因为他们热爱的国家长期以来一直由一个嗜血成性的变态者领导。除非他们先成为烈士，否则他们将把德国从耻辱中解救出来。

普鲁士部长赫尔曼·戈林将军（更不用说他自己创设的无数其他职务）和宣传与国民启蒙部长约瑟夫·戈培尔博士都憎恨希特勒，并乐意看到他被除掉——但这只是希望他们自己能取而代之。他们每个人都有

pages.en:
4
same ambition, to be first despoiler of the nation, instead
of second in command.

* * *

How did it all happen? By what unfortunate
accident following upon accident have a people with a
glorious history fallen into such hands? The Third
Reich is a plague-spot surrounded by a margin of fear:
not a nation near Germany but trembles, remembering
the fate of Czecho-Slovakia and the unwilling surrender
of the Austrians. Wherever his gangsters go, Hitler
has the satisfaction of seeing murder, rape and corrup-
tion spread with them. In Holland, in Switzerland,
decent people cannot be easy so long as this infectious
disease of Nazism feeds upon the dead
hopes of innocent victims.

We are not in medieval times, it is denied us to
comfort ourselves with a simple belief in the Devil.
Hitler is a man, not a demon: a maniac in part, it is
true, but human. What sort of man is he, really!
What possible sort of man could enjoy butchering his
pages.zh:
4
同样的野心，成为国家的头号掠夺者，而不是二号人物。

* * *

这一切是如何发生的？由于怎样的不幸事故接踵而至，使得一个拥有光荣历史的民族落入如此人之手？第三帝国是一个被恐惧边缘包围的瘟疫点：德国附近的每一个国家都在颤抖，回想起捷克斯洛伐克的命运和奥地利人的非自愿投降。无论他的匪徒走到哪里，希特勒都满意地看到谋杀、强奸和腐败随之蔓延。在荷兰，在瑞士，只要纳粹主义这种传染病还在吞噬无辜受害者的破灭希望，正派人士就无法安心。

我们不在中世纪，我们不能用对魔鬼的简单信仰来安慰自己。希特勒是人，不是恶魔：部分是疯子，这没错，但他是人。他究竟是什么样的人！什么样的人会以屠杀自己的

pages.en:
5
own countrymen and terrorizing and murdering beyond
his frontiers?

Above all, why has he such a violent hatred for the
Jews? Many ignorant people have before now held a
prejudice against Jews, a silly unreasoning one, for
who can answer for the characteristics of a whole race?
but Hitler's detestation is so violent and far-fetched
that it has frightened even his own sort. In Germany
today there live thousands of plain people who would
admit if they dared that they are nauseated by the ex-
cesses of treatment afforded the Jews in their country.
The average human being has many faults, and can at
times be swept along on the crest of blood-lust and ex-
citement, but only a madman could persist in the perse-
cution urged and carried out by Hitler, through his
bullies. Even those bullies have sometimes been sickened
by the necessity to slaughter and drive harmless men,
women and children.

The question is being asked on all sides—Why?
Why? Why? Was Hitler in his youth treated badly by
a Jew? Even so, why visit his revenge upon a whole
pages.zh:
5
同胞并在国境之外进行恐怖活动和谋杀为乐？

最重要的是，他为什么如此强烈地仇恨犹太人？许多无知的人以前曾对犹太人持有偏见，这是一种愚蠢且毫无理性的偏见，因为谁能对一个整个种族的特征负责呢？但希特勒的憎恶如此猛烈且牵强，甚至吓到了他自己的同类。今天在德国，成千上万的普通人如果敢说的话，会承认他们对国内对待犹太人的过激行为感到恶心。普通人有许多缺点，有时会被嗜血和兴奋的浪潮卷走，但只有疯子才能坚持希特勒通过其打手敦促并实施的迫害。即使是那些打手，有时也对不得不屠杀和驱赶无害的男人、妇女和儿童感到恶心。

各方都在问这个问题——为什么？为什么？为什么？希特勒年轻时是否受过某个犹太人的虐待？即便如此，为什么要向整个

pages.en:
6
race? Because he is unbalanced. Then what great
wrong could it have been, to be remembered and brood
ed over, and avenged in blood and tears for a decade?

This is the answer. Hitler was wronged by being
made to live. The unforgivable sin was committed by
the Jew who gave him life - his own grandfather or
great-grandfather.

According to Nazi tenets, Hitler is himself a Jew.
According to the ordinary way of regarding these
matters, he is not. He is perhaps a quarter-strain
Jewish; or perhaps only an eighth-strain. In any
other country the most redoubtable Jew-hater would
scarcely consider this amount of Jewish blood blame
worthy; in Germany since Hitler came into power all
such people have been treated just as shamefully as
have those of purer race.

As a child he suffered from the anti-Jewish senti
ments of his own village. The other children called
him "Jewboy" and "Jewish bastard"; they mocked him
pages.zh:
6
种族复仇？因为他精神失衡。那么，那会是多大的冤屈，值得铭记、沉思，并用十年的血泪来报复呢？

答案就在这里。希特勒受到的冤屈是被迫活着。不可饶恕的罪行是由赋予他生命的犹太人犯下的——即他自己的祖父或曾祖父。

根据纳粹信条，希特勒本人就是犹太人。按照看待这些事情的常规方式，他不是。他可能有四分之一犹太血统；或者也许只有八分之一。在任何其他国家，最可怕的反犹主义者几乎不会认为这点犹太血统值得指责；但在希特勒掌权后的德国，所有这类人都受到了与血统更纯正者同样 shameful（可耻）的对待。

小时候，他遭受了自己村庄反犹情绪的影响。其他孩子叫他“犹太小子”和“犹太杂种”；他们嘲笑他

pages.en:
7
and denied him entrance to their society. Many an
other Jewish child has suffered these small cruelties
unscathed, but the boy Hitler had an unbalanced mind
to begin with, and came of rotten stock. The strain
was too much. He nursed a hatred and a sense of
grievance which, since he could not hate himself, he
turned against what he considered the author of all his
misfortunes, his Jewish father.

“It’s his fault,” he probably argued, subconsciously.
“If he hadn’t married my mother, I wouldn’t be me
My mother’s son, if only she had married a Gentile,
would be pure-blooded. Spiritually, I am pure-blooded.
I did not ask for this Jewish taint; I choose my mother’s
people. How I hate those Jews!”

It is not at all unusual, this kind of reasoning.
How often have you met that rather pitiable creature,
the anti-Semitic Jew? By cursing and inveighing
against the Jews, he hopes to fool his audience; he
supposes that they will naturally think him non-Jewish
since he is anti-Jewish. This is a common phenomenon:
Hitler shares the delusion, only he has entertained it
so long that it is almost a belief with him that he is
pages.zh:
7
并拒绝让他进入他们的圈子。许多其他犹太儿童未受伤害地承受了这些小残酷，但男孩希特勒一开始就精神失衡，且出身腐朽。这种压力太大了。他怀抱着仇恨和委屈感，由于他不能恨自己，他便将这种仇恨转向了他认为是所有不幸根源的人，即他的犹太父亲。

“这是他的错，”他可能在潜意识里争辩道。“如果他没有娶我母亲，我就不会是我。如果我母亲嫁给了一个非犹太人，她的儿子就会是纯血统的。在精神上，我是纯血统的。我没有要求这种犹太污点；我选择我母亲的人民。我多么恨那些犹太人！”

这种推理并不罕见。你遇到过多少次那种相当可怜的生物，即反犹的犹太人？通过咒骂和抨击犹太人，他希望愚弄听众；他认为既然他是反犹的，人们自然会认为他不是犹太人。这是一种常见现象：希特勒也有这种妄想，只是他沉浸其中太久，以至于这几乎成了他的信念，即他

pages.en:
8
not a Jew. Only his conscience gives a twinge at times,
and this, too, he blames on the race which produced a
father who in turn produced him.

This is not speculation merely; it is borne out by
history. Hitler was also illegitimate. Let us see.

• • •

His father, a man with a hot temper and too much
sex-impulse, was famous for his furies. He married three
times and had seven children. He was divorced once;
at least one of the children was born out of wedlock
and two were born just after the wedding of their
mother. One of the wives was fourteen years her
husband's senior, and another, Hitler's mother, was
twenty-three years his junior.

The father's name was Alois Schicklgruber; small
wonder that Hitler chose another! His surname was
that of his mother, Hitler's grandmother, because Alois
was himself born out of wedlock, to a penniless peasant
girl. After her death he was raised by one Georg
Hietler, a miller; probably his father.
pages.zh:
8
不是犹太人。只有他的良心偶尔会感到一阵刺痛，而他也把这归咎于那个生下了他父亲、进而生下他的种族。

这不仅仅是推测；历史证实了这一点。希特勒也是私生子。让我们来看看。

• • •

他的父亲脾气暴躁，性欲过强，以暴怒闻名。他结过三次婚，有七个孩子。他离过一次婚；至少有一个孩子是婚外所生，还有两个孩子是在母亲结婚后不久出生的。其中一个妻子比丈夫大十四岁，另一个，即希特勒的母亲，比丈夫小二十三岁。

父亲的名字是阿洛伊斯·席克尔格鲁伯 (Alois Schicklgruber)；难怪希特勒选择了另一个名字！他的姓氏是他母亲（希特勒的祖母）的姓氏，因为阿洛伊斯本人是婚外所生，母亲是一个身无分文的农女。在她去世后，他由一位名叫乔治·希特勒 (Georg Hietler) 的磨坊主抚养长大；这可能是他的父亲。

pages.en:
9
By the time of his third marriage, Alois Schicklgruber had changed his name to Hitler, a variation of Hietler; this was legally done. And so the correct expression of the Nazis should not be “Heil Hitler!” but “Heil Schicklgruber!” Of such small chance is history made. The Fuehrer has actually no name of his own.

Schicklgruber-Hitler was a minor customs official. The marriage and birth records pertaining to his family, at Braunau where he lived for a time, have been blurred and erased and rewritten, evidently in an attempt to alter them. Particularly messed up is the entry pertaining to the birth of Adolf; is not it most likely that this was changed to give the impression, falsely, of Adolf’s legitimacy?

His mother, Klara Polzl, was the daughter of a truck-farmer. Her mother’s name was Hitler; and biologists know that where the stock is tainted, inbreeding makes this taint very much more intense in the progeny. No doubt Hitler’s intermittent insanity comes from his family marriage, or rather, mating. At the time she married she was working as a housemaid: peasants and others living at Braunau can still re-
pages.zh:
9
到阿洛伊斯·希克尔格鲁伯（Alois Schicklgruber）第三次结婚时，他已将自己的名字改为希特勒（Hitler），这是“Hietler”一词的变体；这一更改是合法完成的。因此，纳粹分子正确的口号不应该是“希特勒万岁！”而应该是“希克尔格鲁伯万岁！”历史就是由这样微小的偶然性构成的。这位元首实际上并没有属于自己的名字。

希克尔格鲁伯-希特勒曾是一名低级海关官员。在他一度居住过的布劳瑙（Braunau），与其家庭有关的婚姻和出生记录已被涂抹、擦除并重新书写，显然是为了篡改这些记录。特别是关于阿道夫出生的条目被弄得混乱不堪；这难道不是极有可能是为了虚假地营造阿道夫为婚生子的印象而进行的修改吗？

他的母亲克拉拉·波尔兹尔（Klara Polzl）是一名菜农的女儿。她母亲的姓氏是希特勒；生物学家知道，当血统受到污染时，近亲繁殖会使这种污染在后代中变得更为强烈。毫无疑问，希特勒间歇性的精神错乱源于其家族的婚姻，或者更确切地说，是交配关系。她结婚时是一名女佣：居住在布劳瑙的农民和其他人仍然能——

Aside from being a bastard and a Jew in the eyes
of his neighbours, Hitler suffered because he hated be-
longing to such a humble class. We know that the
most pitiless tyrants are usually those people who have
risen from the ranks: Adolf Hitler is an outstanding
example of this. He has sometimes posed as a friend
of the workers, but in reality all his actions show how
he detests manual laborers.

There is still living a former cook of the Heidler-
Hitlers who tells a story of an interview she once
overheard between young Adolf and old Alois. The
father wanted his son to follow in his footsteps as a petty
customs official: young Hitler, just past his twelfth
birthday, did not agree. This was at Linz, in Upper
Austria. Adolf screamed tearfully that he would not
spend the next six years studying for the examination
his father had once taken: Alois, enraged at his son's
crackpot hopes of becoming an artist, had recourse to
the whip. Adolf insisted that an artist could get out
of his class and hobnob with the aristocracy. When
his father became insulted at aspersions cast upon his
position in society, his son forestalled a beating by
throwing a paperweight at the old man, drawing blood.

Adolf Hitler was a stupid oaf at elementary school,
and he did not endear himself to the faculty by spitting
in the face of his history teacher, who was a woman.
Moreover, he was dirty and had a bad influence on his
schoolmates. In the end his instructors bribed the
father to take young Adolf away, by certifying falsely
that he had “passed”. This was the end of the
Fuehrer’s formal schooling.

His father died a little later, and Adolf found his
mother more easy to manage; in fact, she spoiled him.
“Suddenly,” as he writes, “an illness came to my help
and in a few weeks decided my future. The severe lung-
trouble I contracted made a doctor advise my mother
to let me off any indoors work. No school, he said, for
at least a year. My mother finally let me attend the
Academy, but her death in 1908 put a brutal end to all
these fine projects.”

"With my clothes and linen packed in a valise and
with an indomitable resolution in my heart, I left for
Vienna. I hoped to forestall fate, as my father had
done fifty years before. I was determined to become
'something'—but certainly not a civil servant."

Incredible, tragic, misshapen little monster! Even
the Greek tragedians have never offered a more heart-
breaking figure than this scrap of warped humanity,
forever spurred on by the Jewish content in his tainted
blood, forever fleeing from the acknowledgement of his
debt to that hated race. Whether he would or not, the
blood of Christ flows in his veins, and though it has been
turned to poison by other less pure elements in the
mixture, it was inevitable that his dearest wish was to
be realized. Hitler was indeed to become "somebody".

VIENNA'S DOSS-HOUSE FUEHRER

Four years Hitler lived in a doss-house in Vienna.
His own account of this period is vague and oratorical,

维也纳廉价旅馆里的元首

希特勒在维也纳的一家廉价旅馆里住了四年。
他自己对这段时期的叙述模糊且充满演说腔调，

19
but one can read between the lines how much his misery
owed to his feeling of being born for better, that is,
easier and more glorious, things. We find him admitting
to a little art work here and there, and he shamefacedly
confesses that he once actually held a job with other
manual laborers building a house. Poverty, he
observes sententiously, is a very bad thing and makes
the wrong impression on children. He traces the
misery of these people directly to the fact that they
live in Vienna, for which city he has the liveliest feel-
ings of horror. “Dazzling riches and loathsome destitu-
tion were intermingled in violent contrast.” Still, he
protests, he is very glad that he had the experience.
“ . . we argued with one another on the building pre-
mises. From day to day I was becoming better in-
formed than my companions in the subjects on which
they claimed to be experts. Then a day came when the
more redoubtable of my adversaries resorted to the
most effective weapon they had to replace the force of
reason. This was intimidation and physical force.
Some of the leaders among my adversaries ordered me
to leave the building or else get flung down the scaffold-

physical resistance; so I chose the first alternative and departed, richer however by an experience.”

The real story in detail is more interesting. In the doss-house, from which Adolf was once thrown out for being too dirty even for those surroundings, he made a friend, an etcher named Hanisch, who was sorry for the tubercular and pathetically shabby young man. Hitler’s manners were diverting, in a way; he put on such airs! “I am a painter,” he told Hanisch; “An academician and a gentleman.”

Once he asked Hanisch, “Do I look like a Jew?”

Hanisch realized the truth immediately, though he could not guess the extent of Adolf’s insanity; to tease the boy, he said, “Well, now that you mention it. . . .”

Hitler burst into tears. All that night he had hysterics.

Remorsefully, Hanisch set about finding some way for the boy to live. This was how Hitler became a bricklayer’s assistant, but the job, as we have seen, did not last long. The men, indeed, resented him, saying, “Who the hell does he think he is? Dancing around
pages.zh:
20
身体上的反抗；所以我选择了第一种方案并离开了，不过这段经历让我获益良多。”

详细来说，真实的故事更为有趣。在那家收容所里——阿道夫曾因过于肮脏，即便在那种环境下也容不下他而被赶出去——他结识了一位名叫汉尼施（Hanisch）的蚀刻画家，此人同情这位患有肺结核、衣着寒酸得令人心酸的年轻人。希特勒的举止在某种程度上颇为滑稽；他摆出那样的架子！“我是一名画家，”他告诉汉尼施；“一位学院派艺术家和绅士。”

有一次他问汉尼施：“我看起来像犹太人吗？”

汉尼施立刻意识到了真相，尽管他无法猜出阿道夫疯癫的程度；为了戏弄这个年轻人，他说：“嗯，既然你提到了……”

希特勒放声大哭。那一整夜他都歇斯底里发作。

汉尼施怀着愧疚之情，着手为这个年轻人寻找谋生之道。希特勒就这样成了一名泥瓦匠的助手，但正如我们所见，这份工作并未持续多久。工友们确实对他心生怨恨，说道：“他到底以为自己是谁？像个姑娘似的在这里扭来扭去，自以为比我们这种人高贵。哼，他不过是个乡下小犹太，连学门手艺的脑子都没有！”

After that failure the future Reich leader pan-
handled for a few days, while Hanisch wondered what
next they could do for the academician and gentleman.
Adolf himself suggested that he "fake" old masters,
baking his new pictures in an oven to make them brown
and antique-looking. He had done it before, he said, in
Linz. Hanisch had a better and safer idea; Hitler,
since he would not soil his hands with manual labour,
might as well paint post-cards. Adolf promptly borrow-
ed the savings of his sister and invested in some paints
and cards; Hanisch did the selling. After a while they
discovered it saved time and effort simply to trace the
pictures from photographs.

Today, Nazis pay as much as $375 U.S. for these
horrible things.

Without doubt Hitler would have starved without
Hanisch. But the time was coming when he was to
show of what gratitude he was made.

在那次失败之后，这位未来的帝国领袖乞讨了几天，而汉尼施则在琢磨接下来还能为这位“学院派艺术家和绅士”做些什么。阿道夫自己建议“伪造”古代大师的作品，将新画的画作放入烤箱烘烤，使其呈现褐色和古旧的外观。他说以前在林茨（Linz）就做过这种事。汉尼施有一个更好且更稳妥的主意；既然希特勒不愿弄脏双手从事体力劳动，不如画明信片。阿道夫随即借用了他姐姐的积蓄，购买了一些颜料和卡片；由汉尼施负责销售。过了一段时间，他们发现直接从照片上描摹图画更省时省力。

如今，纳粹分子为这些糟糕的东西支付高达375美元。

毫无疑问，如果没有汉尼施，希特勒早就饿死了。但展示其感恩之心的时刻即将到来。

One day, having decided privately that he could
now get along better alone, he deliberately picked a
quarrel with Hanisch, accusing him of cheating, holding
out on money they had both earned. He flew into a
rage, was the first of many such fits which were
later to become famous. Assuming an expression of
infuriated injury and pop-eyed disbelief, he screamed
at Hanisch:

“You dirty crook! You swindler! Grabbing all
the profit from my work. . . . You Jew bastard, get
out of here!”

They never saw each other again. Once Hitler
had decided for himself that a man was a “Jew bastard”
—i.e., once he had insulted a person by applying the
epithet which he knew himself, secretly, to deserve—
that man was marked; he was doomed.

“It’s for me to decide,” as he once snarled,
“whether a man’s a Jew.”

有一天，他在私下认定现在独自生活会更好后，故意与汉尼施挑起争端，指责他欺诈，私吞了两人共同赚得的钱。他勃然大怒，这是后来闻名遐迩的多次此类发作中的第一次。他摆出一副愤怒受辱和瞪眼不信的神情，对汉尼施尖叫道：

“你这肮脏的骗子！你这欺诈犯！攫取我劳动的所有利润……你这犹太杂种，滚出去！”

他们从此再未相见。一旦希特勒自行认定某人是“犹太杂种”——即一旦他用自己内心深处知道才配得上的侮辱性称呼去辱骂某人——那人就被标记了；那人便注定毁灭。

“由我来决定，”他曾咆哮道，“一个人是不是犹太人。”

THE FIRST LOVE AFFAIR

At the age of twenty, Hitler hung about the cafés
of Vienna, now and then trying to make a speech against
the Social Democrats and the Jews. Usually he was
pelted with beer and stale pretzels, and thrown out.
One evening a young woman was attracted by him.
Feeling that in his misguided way he was seriously
trying to understand the fabric of society, she walked
out with him and wiped the beer from his face.

Fraulein Reinhart was a Jewess, but Hitler became
attached to her nevertheless. Her father, however, had
heard of the young man's anti-Semitism, and refused
him the house. One night Hitler walked home with her,
and at the door he promised to sing a Schubert serenade
for her if she would blow him a kiss from her window,
three stories up.

He waited beneath the window, singing. Slowly the
window opened. Hitler peered up hopefully for the pro-
mised kiss—and received, instead, a chamber-pot flung
by the irate father. The chamber-pot was not empty.
Perhaps Adolf dodged in time, perhaps not. But the

初恋

二十岁时，希特勒在维也纳的咖啡馆里游荡，不时试图发表反对社会民主党和犹太人的演讲。通常他会遭到啤酒和 stale pretzels（陈椒盐卷饼）的投掷，并被赶出去。一天晚上，一位年轻女子被他吸引。她觉得他以一种误入歧途的方式认真试图理解社会结构，便与他一同走出咖啡馆，擦去他脸上的啤酒。

莱因哈特小姐（Fraulein Reinhart）是一位犹太女性，但希特勒还是对她产生了依恋。然而，她的父亲听闻了这位年轻人的反犹主义言论，拒绝让他进门。一天晚上，希特勒送她回家，在门口他承诺，如果她从三楼的窗口向他飞吻，他就为她演唱一首舒伯特的小夜曲。

他在窗下等待，歌唱着。窗户缓缓打开。希特勒满怀希望地向上窥视，期待那个承诺的吻——结果得到的却是愤怒的父亲扔出的一个夜壶。夜壶并不是空的。也许阿道夫及时躲开了，也许没有。但这

pages.en:
24
incident was scarcely likely to make him any fonder of
the Jews.
“In standing guard against the Jew,” as he says
in ‘My Struggle’, “I am defending the handiwork of
the Lord.”
Or, in other words, defending his own dignity,
forever armoured against the attacks of his hidden
Jewish nature.
• • •
“This Judaizing of our spiritual life and mam-
monizing of our natural instinct for procreation will
sooner or later work havoc with our whole posterity.
For instead of strong healthy children, blessed with
natural feelings, we shall see miserable specimens of
humanity. . . . One may defy Nature for a certain
period of time, but sooner or later she will take her in-
exorable revenge. . . . All this (prostitution, blamed
on the Jews) leads to absolute degeneration. . . .”

件事几乎不可能让他对犹太人产生更多好感。
“在警惕犹太人方面，”正如他在《我的奋斗》中所说，“我是在捍卫上帝的杰作。”
或者，换句话说，是在捍卫他自己的尊严，永远武装起来以抵御其隐藏的犹太本性的攻击。
• • •
“这种对我们精神生活的‘犹太化’以及对我们自然繁衍本能的‘金钱化’，迟早会给我们整个后代带来灾难。因为我们将看到的不是拥有自然情感、强壮健康的孩子，而是可怜的人类标本……人可以在一定时期内违抗自然，但迟早自然会进行无情的报复……所有这一切（归咎于犹太人的卖淫）导致绝对的退化……”

“The blackhaired Jew-boy, his face twisted with
devilish joy, lies in wait, hour after hour, for the un-
suspecting girl whom he pollutes with his blood!”

Time after time in “Mein Kampf” we find similar
visions and ideas, all centering about the imagined situa-
tion in which a Jewish man seduces, violates, rapes or
at the very best marries a golden-haired Christian girl.
Hitler’s hidden fears are very easy to see here; they
are hidden only from himself. Useless to protest in the
next paragraph that “at home I never heard the word
‘Jew’. Had it been mentioned to my father, the old
gentleman would in all probability have regarded it
with his usual broadminded and cosmopolitan
attitude—” etc. etc.

No, it is quite evident that Hitler is still nursing the
fancied grievance against his father for having lain
with his mother—the hideous Jew-boy of his terrified
imagination, forcing the spotless, blameless Aryan girl
who is the mother of his idealization, and giving birth
to Adolf himself. Oh crime, oh tragedy, thus to treat
the mother of such a great man! He, Hitler, is his
mother’s son, the pure Aryan child of that golden-
pages.zh:
25

“那个黑发犹太男孩，脸上扭曲着恶魔般的喜悦， hour after hour（ hour after hour 此处保留原文或译为‘时时刻刻’，根据语境译为‘时刻’）潜伏着，等待那些 unsuspecting（ unsuspecting 译为‘毫无防备’）的女孩，用他的血液污染她们！”

在《我的奋斗》中，我们一次次发现类似的幻象和观念，全都围绕着一个想象的情境：一个犹太男人引诱、侵犯、强奸，或者往好里说，娶了一位金发基督教女孩。希特勒隐藏的恐惧在此处显而易见；这些恐惧只是对他自己隐藏而已。在下一段中抗议说“在家里我从未听过‘犹太’这个词。如果向我父亲提起，那位老先生很可能会以他一贯的开明和世界主义态度看待它——”等等，是无济于事的。

不，很明显，希特勒仍在滋养对他父亲的虚构怨愤，因为他父亲曾与他的母亲同床——在他惊恐的想象中，那个可怕的犹太男孩强迫了他理想化中纯洁无瑕、无可指责的雅利安女孩（即他的母亲），并生下了阿道夫本人。哦，罪行，哦，悲剧，竟如此对待这样一位伟人的母亲！他，希特勒，是他母亲的儿子，是那位金发

pages.en:
26
haired virgin, and mentally he has banished his criminal
Jewish father to the outside hell where he belongs for
so polluting the blood and ruining the life of the
Fuehrer. Again and again Hitler takes this mental
revenge and comforts himself with these imaginings.

Prostitutes? All the victims of Jews. Therefore
who can blame his mother for having allowed herself
to bear an illegitimate child? Nobody is to blame but
that unspeakable monster, that JEW, who violated her.

All the other crimes of which he accuses Judaism,
treason and corruption in politics and the rest, are
secondary to the original outrage, the seduction of
Klara Poelzl, and the fathering of Adolf Hitler.

Hitler left Vienna in 1912, at the age of twenty-
three. He was a skinny, sickly youth with only one
sound lung and a disabled stomach, the result of years
of malnutrition. He still wore his father's ancient black
coat, unbelievably filthy by this time. He affected a
bushy mustache, and his hair hung over his collar in
pages.zh:
26
处女的纯雅利安孩子，而在精神上，他已将那犯罪的犹太父亲放逐到属于他的外部地狱，因为后者污染了血统并毁了元首（Fuehrer）的生活。希特勒一次又一次地进行这种精神复仇，并通过这些想象来自我安慰。

妓女？都是犹太人的受害者。因此，谁能责怪他的母亲允许自己生下私生子呢？除了那个不可言说的怪物，那个强奸了她的犹太人之外，没有人应受责备。

他指控犹太教的其他所有罪行，政治上的叛国和腐败等等，都次于最初的暴行，即对克拉拉·波尔兹尔（Klara Poelzl）的引诱以及阿道夫·希特勒的出生。

希特勒于1912年离开维也纳，时年二十三岁。他是一个瘦弱、多病的青年，只有一侧肺部健康，胃部受损，这是多年营养不良的结果。他仍然穿着父亲的那件古老黑外套，此时已肮脏得令人难以置信。他蓄起浓密的胡须，头发垂在衣领后面。

pages.en:
27
back. (Somehow he always managed to have a collar.
He could not bear to be classed as a common labourer,
"a creature corrupted by the Jew bastard Karl Marx".)

According to his few acquaintances at the time,
he was still a virgin. Adolf's sexual life has always
been at once irregular and undemanding. Like many
nearly impotent men, he must search for the less normal
forms of indulgence before he can feel excitement.
"These children of mixed parentage," as he naively
confesses, "seldom breed well." Another black mark
to be chalked up against the sinner Alois!

He suddenly enlisted in the army, and was presently
made corporal. As orderly to Captain Schweinbolde in
the List regiment, he was an object of mirth in his
passion for whatever beauty he could create in an army
tent. In short, he polished and polished and polished
the captain's boots until that officer would kick him out.
Hitler was completely slavish at this period, glorying
and wallowing in servility. The captain's brother
officers jokingly accused him of having an affair with the
unappetizing corporal—homosexuality was then quite
pages.zh:
27
（不知何故，他总是能弄到有领子的衣服。他无法忍受被归类为普通劳工，“一个被犹太杂种卡尔·马克思腐蚀的生物”。）

据当时少数认识他的人说，他仍然是处男。阿道夫的性生活一直既不规则又缺乏需求。像许多近乎阳痿的男人一样，他必须寻求不太正常的放纵形式才能感到兴奋。“这些混血子女，”他天真地承认，“很少繁殖良好。”这又是罪人阿洛伊斯（Alois）的一笔黑账！

他突然参军，不久后被提拔为下士。作为李斯特团（List regiment）施温博尔德队长（Captain Schweinbolde）的勤务兵，他因热衷于在军营帐篷中创造任何可能的美感而成为笑柄。简而言之，他把队长的靴子擦了又擦，直到那位军官把他踢开。这一时期的希特勒完全奴性十足，在卑躬屈膝中自得其乐、沉溺其中。队长的其他军官同事开玩笑地指责他与这位令人倒胃口的下士有染——当时同性恋在德国军队中相当

pages.en:
28
the fad in the German army. It was a splendid joke,
good for days!
“A good soldier,” they said, more seriously, “but
he must never be given a commission. He’s at once
too hysterical and too servile.”
It is interesting to note that the German army
at this time was in such need of officers that it was
really an effort for a non-com. not to gain his commis-
sion. The fact that Hitler did not is more significant
than are most negative arguments. Nevertheless he
was happy as a soldier. Before enlisting he had spent
two dreary years in Munich, eking out a living with his
painted post-cards, and now and then shamefacedly
painting a house. There were no women with enough
perversity to take an interest in the dirty half-starved
academician and gentleman. What riches of resent-
ment did he store up for future use! How many
thwarted hopes and hungers turned to poison in his
mind! Adolf the house-painter seems to me the most
pitiable figure of all the pitiable Adolfs of Hitler’s
career. That insane spark glowed in his tortured mind
and carried him through despair and squalor. If only
pages.zh:
28
流行。这是一个精彩的笑话，够大家乐上好几天！
“是个好士兵，”他们更严肃地说，“但绝不能授予他军官委任状。他既太歇斯底里，又太奴性。”
值得注意的是，当时德国军队极度缺乏军官，士官未能获得委任状实际上是很困难的。希特勒未能获得委任状这一事实，比大多数反面论据更具意义。尽管如此，他作为一名士兵是快乐的。入伍前，他在慕尼黑度过了两年沉闷的时光，靠画明信片勉强维持生计，偶尔还羞怯地粉刷房屋。没有足够变态的女人会对这位肮脏、半饥饿的“学院派艺术家和绅士”感兴趣。他为未来储备了多少怨恨的财富！有多少受挫的希望和渴望在他的脑海中变成了毒药！在我看来，作为房屋油漆工的阿道夫，是希特勒生涯中所有可怜的阿道夫形象里最令人心酸的一个。那疯狂的火花在他受折磨的脑海中闪烁，支撑他度过绝望和肮脏。要是

pages.en:
29
he had not been warped!

Better times were coming; the World War was the turning-point for Hitler. In the riot of bloodshed and cruelty the boy at last found an outlet for his sex impulse, such as it was; the sight of torture and death excited and satisfied him. Besides, he was happy as a boot-licker and boot-polisher. He never joined the other men in criticising their officers for bribery, corruption, and debauchery—“My ideal was blind respect of my superior officers; complete submission.”

There is a story told in varying forms by dozens of Nazi historians, that Hitler in 1916, single-handed, captured fifteen Frenchmen and handed them over to his commander. Sometimes the story is that he captured a tank. As a matter of fact, neither the commander, who wrote his memoirs, nor Hitler himself has ever mentioned this daring feat of arms; nevertheless the story is in all German textbooks for children which deal with the World War. He did receive the following rewards; a regimental diploma for bravery, Military Cross for distinguished services, third class, the Black Badge for wounds (in 1916 he was wounded by a shell)
pages.zh:
29
他没有被扭曲该多好！

更好的时代即将来临；世界大战是希特勒的转折点。在血腥和残酷的骚乱中，这个男孩终于为其性欲冲动找到了宣泄口，尽管这种冲动本身就很微弱；酷刑和死亡的景象使他兴奋并得到满足。此外，他乐于做一个拍马屁者和擦鞋匠。他从不与其他人一起批评军官们的贿赂、腐败和放荡行为——“我的理想是对上级军官的盲目尊重；完全服从。”

数十位纳粹历史学家以不同形式讲述着一个故事，称希特勒在1916年单枪匹马俘虏了十五名法国人，并将他们移交给他的指挥官。有时这个故事版本是他俘虏了一辆坦克。事实上，无论是写了回忆录的指挥官，还是希特勒本人，都从未提及这一大胆的军事壮举；尽管如此，这个故事却出现在所有涉及世界大战的德国儿童教科书中。他确实获得了以下奖励：一枚团级勇敢证书，三等功绩军事十字勋章，负伤黑章（1916年他被炮弹炸伤）

pages.en:
and a first class Iron Cross. Such trophies came to
most men in the army if they survived the war, save the
Iron Cross, which remains a bit of a mystery. Hitler
seems to have forgotten why and where he got it.
Perhaps this is modesty; there seems little doubt that
he conferred it upon himself

THE INFORMER

It was about the time of the war and afterward
that Hitler began to hear voices, after the manner
of Jeanne d'Arc. He describes her intensely: "She has
no woman-stench", as he so gracefully puts it. These
voices, of course, urged Hitler to deliver Germany
from the menace of the Jews.

Another moment, he says, were the
returned soldiers. The voices
urged him to be serious. His sym-
pathies were Prussian. Germany was in revolt and
his voice knew only to side with the loser.
Since he had no trade, he stayed in the
army since the Armistice. During

以及一枚一级铁十字勋章。这样的荣誉只要能在战争中幸存下来，大多数军人都能获得，除了铁十字勋章，这仍然有点神秘。希特勒似乎忘记了他是为何以及在何处获得它的。也许这是谦虚；毫无疑问，这枚勋章是他自封的。

告密者

大约在战争期间及战后，希特勒开始听到声音，就像圣女贞德那样。他生动地描述她：“她没有女人味”，他如此优雅地说道。当然，这些声音敦促希特勒将德国从犹太人的威胁中解救出来。

他说，另一个关键时刻是退伍士兵归来。声音敦促他严肃起来。他的同情心倾向于普鲁士。德国处于叛乱之中，而他的声音只知道站在失败者一边。
由于没有手艺，他在停战协定签署后仍留在军队中。在此期间

pages.en:
31
this time he was sent about Bavaria and other parts
of Germany, hunting “Reds” with his brother-soldiers.
In Munich he met Captain Roehm, who was to help him
thirteen years later.

In 1920 Hitler was demobilized; he immediately
joined the Workers’ party, which was a very clever
thing to do. He hated manual labour and its priests,
but the world was swinging in the direction of labour;
he recognized the bandwagon, and climbed aboard.
The German National Socialist party—“Nazi”—was
named by Hitler, who put in the word “Socialist” to
attract the radicals, and the word “National” for the
Old Guard. The fact that it means nothing, being as
contradictory as “Republican-Communist” or “Radical-
Conservative” did not worry either the future party
leader nor his followers.

It came about as follows: Hitler was fairly
happy, back at his old game of bawling speeches from
café tables. One night a drunken poet, an ex-news-
paperman named Eckart, heard the future Chancellor
screaming his catchy nonsense in the Café Fahrig.
With Captain Roehm, he decided that this strange
pages.zh:
31
这一次，他被派往巴伐利亚和德国其他地区，与他的战友一起搜捕“赤色分子”。在慕尼黑，他遇到了罗姆上尉（Captain Roehm），此人在十三年后曾助他一臂之力。

1920年，希特勒退役；他随即加入了工人党，这是一个非常聪明的举动。他厌恶体力劳动及其拥护者，但世界正朝着劳工的方向发展；他认清了大势，并顺势而上。德国国家社会主义党——即“纳粹”——由希特勒命名，他在其中加入“社会主义”一词以吸引激进派，加入“国家”一词以迎合保守派老卫兵。尽管该名称毫无实质意义，其矛盾程度如同“共和-共产主义”或“激进-保守主义”，但这并未让这位未来的党魁或其追随者感到困扰。

事情是这样发生的：希特勒相当快乐，重操旧业，站在咖啡馆的桌子上大声发表演讲。一天晚上，一位醉醺醺的诗人、前报人埃卡特（Eckart）在法里格咖啡馆（Café Fahrig）听到这位未来的总理尖叫着他那朗朗上口却荒谬不经的言论。他与罗姆上尉决定，这只奇怪而粗野的野兽可能对德国工人党有用。他正是他们急需的人选。他们需要一名有勇气的人，一个能相信自己必须宣讲的那些胡言乱语的人；他们需要一名工人、一名退伍士兵，以用于宣传和博取人气；他们需要一名单身汉来吸引女性。受到灵感的启发，他们从某位疯狂的教授那里抄袭并采用了“雅利安”理论，这注定会迎合无知的公众，并且日后在纳粹关于其殖民地的外交政策中也会派上用场。每个人都喜欢感觉自己优于他人。

uncouth beast could be useful to the German Workers'
Party. He was just what the doctor ordered. They
wanted a man with courage, who could believe in the
bunkum he must talk; they wanted a workman, an ex-
soldier, for publicity and popularity; they wanted a
bachelor to catch the women. Still inspired, they copied
from some crazy Professor and adopted the "Aryan"
theory, which was bound to appeal to the ignorant
public, and also was to come in handy in the foreign
policy of the Nazis, in regard to their Colonies. Every-
body likes to feel superior to others.

Roehm then organized the "Iron Fist", a group
of young officers and former non-commissioned men.
With the regular army, the Reichswehr, they suppressed
Bavarian uprisings with machine-guns. Hitler enjoyed
shooting defenseless citizens. While working the
gun, he said to his assistant: "This'll teach the
Christ-killers a lesson." And really, you see, any
enemy of his became a Jew.

He began to have a reputation in Munich; they said
it was better to keep Hitler than to watch a three-ringed
circus. One night S... went slumming

32
随后，罗姆组织了“铁拳”（Iron Fist），这是一个由年轻军官和前士官组成的团体。他们与正规军——国防军（Reichswehr）一起，用机枪镇压了巴伐利亚的起义。希特勒乐于射杀手无寸铁的平民。在操作机枪时，他对助手说：“这将给那些杀害基督的人一个教训。”事实上，你看，任何他的敌人都成了犹太人。

他在慕尼黑开始有了名声；人们说，看希特勒比看三圈马戏团表演更有趣。一天晚上，S...女士去贫民窟

pages.en:
33
to hear him speak. She was a woman of forty in 1920-
21, and Hitler somehow attracted the favour of the
sophisticated, perverse woman. She was a divorcée, tall,
blonde and brilliant.

Hitler was overcome with flattery. An aristocrat!
At last he was coming into his own; at last he would
show those damned Jewish peasants what he really
was. Moreover, the Countess' caresses simply stagger-
ed him; he realized what he had been missing all these
years. Last but far from least, she was rich and—
generous.

Among other more sensual lessons, she taught him
something of spiritualism and other mystic claptrap.
Hitler attended séances at which he heard those old
friends of his, the voices. They were now discovered,
by a coincidence, to belong to German heroes such as
Frederick the Great, who warned him, naturally, against
Communists and Jews, for the sake of Germany. And
Napoleon told him to assassinate the Reichspresident,
Fritz Ebert.

Meantime the living authorities also began to
notice him; and he was ordered back to the army as a

听他演讲。她在1920-21年间是一位四十岁的女性，不知何故，希特勒吸引了这位世故、乖张的女性的青睐。她是一位离异女性，身材高挑，金发碧眼，才华横溢。

希特勒被奉承冲昏了头脑。一位贵族！他终于要崭露头角了；终于可以向那些该死的犹太农民展示他的真实面目了。此外，伯爵夫人的爱抚简直让他神魂颠倒；他意识到自己这些年来错过了什么。最后但同样重要的是，她富有且——慷慨。

除了其他更感官的课程外，她还教了他一些招魂术和其他神秘的废话。希特勒参加了降神会，在那里他听到了他的那些老朋友——声音。巧合的是，这些声音现在被发现属于德国的英雄人物，如腓特烈大帝（Frederick the Great），他自然地警告希特勒要提防共产主义者和犹太人，这是为了德国的利益。拿破仑则告诉他去刺杀帝国总统弗里茨·艾伯特（Fritz Ebert）。

与此同时，在世当局也开始注意到他；他被命令以预备役成员的身份返回军队。

member of the reserves. The new assignment paid
well and was congenial work. In plain terms, Hitler
was a stool pigeon for the government. Under the
guise of “education officer”, supposed to train troops
in political propaganda, this highly educated young
professor snooped about Bavaria and reported all signs
of revolution which he could discover. A brother stool
pigeon, Feder, inspired him with imitative admiration:
Hitler shaved his bushy mustache and imitated Feder’s
tiny toothbrush on the upper lip. Feder had a well
developed anti-Semitic doctrine, also. They became
excellent friends.

When he was released from this work, Hitler re-
joined the party, now the National Socialist German
Workers. Feder was no fool, but as soon as he began
to attract too many people with his oratory, Hitler got
rid of him. At the same time he dispensed with the
countess, because of whispers about such goings-on on
the part of a “worker”. Hitler didn’t need her money
any more, anyway. Soon after this she died in a fire
in her apartment. Nobody has ever found out how that
fire started.

The Countess had served her purpose. Hitler now
pages.zh:
34
这项新任务报酬丰厚，且工作性质合意。简而言之，希特勒是政府的线人。在这位受过高等教育的年轻教授伪装成“教育官员”、 supposedly 负责训练部队进行政治宣传的幌子下，他在巴伐利亚四处窥探，并报告他发现的所有革命迹象。另一位线人费德尔（Feder）以模仿式的崇拜激励了他：希特勒剃掉了浓密的胡子，模仿费德尔在上唇留的小牙刷式胡须。费德尔也有一套发展完善的反犹主义学说。他们成为了极好的朋友。

当希特勒结束这项工作时，他重新加入了政党，此时该党已更名为德国国家社会主义工人党。费德尔并不愚蠢，但一旦他开始凭借口才吸引太多人，希特勒便摆脱了他。同时，他也甩掉了那位伯爵夫人，因为有关于一名“工人”如此行径的流言蜚语。反正希特勒也不再需要她的钱了。不久之后，她在公寓的一场火灾中丧生。从未有人查明那场火灾是如何引起的。

伯爵夫人已经完成了她的使命。希特勒现在

knew just how persuasive was his hysterical high-
pitched treble voice. He promised violence to his public,
and they were so pleased at the prospect that they
forgot to ask for a constructive program. The male
members of the party organized into a political army;
this was treason, but the government was frightened
and did not object.

“Democracy stinks!” he would roar, “Democracy
is the refuge of cowards! The Jewish Communists are
at our throats, they must be exterminated.”

He was now living on party dues. As a matter of
record, from the time he met the Countess until today
he has not been forced to work for a living, which must
have been a great relief to his feelings. The necessity
of working now and then, before the happy day when
he lost his independence and his virginity to the
Swedish lady, had horrified his gentlemanly soul: “I
only worked,” as he says, “to keep from starving.”
History has forgiven him this lapse from good taste.
Roehm confided to Franz von Papen that the party
dues, though as yet they did not amount to very much,
were enough “for parties in Munich almost every night,

清楚地知道他那歇斯底里的高音假声具有多大的说服力。他向公众许诺暴力，而公众对这一前景如此满意，以至于忘记了要求建设性的纲领。党的男性成员组织成了一支政治军队；这是叛国行为，但政府感到恐惧，并未反对。

“民主臭不可闻！”他会咆哮道，“民主是懦夫的避难所！犹太共产主义者正掐住我们的喉咙，必须将他们灭绝。”

他现在靠党费生活。据记录，从他遇到伯爵夫人直到今天，他从未被迫为生计而工作，这对他的情感来说一定是一种巨大的解脱。在他失去独立性和童贞给那位瑞典女士的幸福日子到来之前，偶尔需要工作的必要性曾让他那绅士般的灵魂感到惊恐：“我工作，”他说，“只是为了避免饿死。”历史已原谅了他这一有失品味的过失。罗姆曾向弗朗茨·冯·帕彭（Franz von Papen）透露，党费虽然当时数额不大，但足以“几乎每晚在慕尼黑举办派对，

with young boys. In those days we never lacked cham-
pions or good-looking lads dressed as women."

It was the gossip of the day that Hitler was especial-
ly fond of his chauffeur, Julius Schreck, a handsome
boy. Röhm used to say that the future Führer liked
to ruffle the boy's cheeks and hair. Schreck, who had
been operated on for a brain tumour, was shot and
killed in 1936 by an unknown assassin who thought he
was firing at Hitler.

The party funds also went to support the SA men,
who must be fed and housed and clothed and given
parades and flags and bands. The Bavarians, over-
joyed at finding something that looked like authority,
willingly contributed their two or three marks. When
the Nazis could announce that they were now supported
by Marshal Erich von Ludendorff, the money rolled in.
True, Ludendorff was insane ever since the end of the
war, but he was sane enough to know the drawing
power of Hitler.

Hitler also met Goering at this stage. Hermann
Goering during the war was an aviator and a morphine-
addict, which latter habit helped him in his aerial dog-

和年轻男孩一起。在那段日子里，我们从不缺乏支持者或打扮成女人的漂亮小伙子。”

当时的流言称，希特勒特别喜欢他的司机朱利叶斯·施雷克（Julius Schreck），一个英俊的小伙子。罗姆常说，这位未来的元首喜欢抚摸那男孩的脸颊和头发。施雷克曾因脑肿瘤接受过手术，于1936年被一名不明刺客枪杀，该刺客以为自己在向希特勒开枪。

党的资金也用于支持冲锋队（SA）成员，必须为他们提供食宿、服装，并组织游行、旗帜和乐队。巴伐利亚人因找到某种看似权威的东西而欣喜若狂， willingly 贡献出他们的两三马克。当纳粹宣布他们现在得到埃里希·冯·鲁登道夫元帅（Marshal Erich von Ludendorff）的支持时，资金滚滚而来。诚然，鲁登道夫自战争结束以来一直精神失常，但他还清醒地知道希特勒的号召力。

希特勒也在这一阶段结识了戈林（Goering）。赫尔曼·戈林在战争期间是一名飞行员和吗啡成瘾者，后者习惯帮助他在空中狗斗中

fights. A gross, ungainly creature, he has an insane
vanity and a childish love of uniforms. The Langbro
Lunatic Asylum in Sweden once kept him under control
for a time, though private asylums refused to accept
him as a patient because of his insane violence. There
is on record a certificate signed by Dr. Karl A. Lund-
berg which reads: “Captain Goering suffers from
morphine addiction, and his wife Baroness Goering,
née Frikkerina Fock, suffers from epilepsy, and that is
why their home does not seem a fit place for her son,
Thomas Kantzau.” Goering seemed very rich at this
time, because he was backed by Herr Hannussen, a
millionaire eccentric whom Goering later assassinated
for fear of the stories he might tell.
Captain Roehm also introduced Hitler to Ernst
Hanfstaengl, a rich man who said he was passionately
interested in the German Workers. The four of them
staged wild parties at the Platterhof Inn near Berches-
gaden, until some of the more conservative party-
members, meeting at the East Railway Station in
Munich, sent him the following message:
“We realize that the Fuehrer is an artist who
cannot be judged by ordinary standards, and he

保持状态。他是一个粗俗、笨拙的生物，有着疯狂的虚荣心和孩子气地对制服的喜爱。瑞典的兰布罗精神病院（Langbro Lunatic Asylum）曾一度控制过他，尽管私人精神病院因他疯狂的暴力倾向而拒绝接收他为病人。有一份由卡尔·A·伦德伯格博士（Dr. Karl A. Lundberg）签署的证明书记录在案，上面写道：“戈林上尉患有吗啡成瘾症，其妻子戈林男爵夫人，娘家姓弗里克里娜·福克（Frikkerina Fock），患有癫痫症，因此他们的家似乎不适合她的儿子托马斯·坎察乌（Thomas Kantzau）居住。”戈林当时显得很富有，因为他得到了汉努森先生（Herr Hannussen）的支持，这是一位百万富翁怪人，戈林后来因害怕他可能讲出的故事而将其暗杀。
罗姆上尉还将希特勒介绍给了恩斯特·汉夫施滕格尔（Ernst Hanfstaengl），一位富人说他对德国工人充满热情。这四个人在贝希特斯加登附近的普拉特霍夫旅馆（Platterhof Inn）举办狂野的派对，直到一些较保守的党员在慕尼黑东火车站集会，向他发送了以下信息：
“我们认识到元首是一位艺术家，不能用普通标准来评判，而且

pages.en:
should not be judged for his conduct in the
company of beautiful women. But the Fuehrer
must realize that all he does or leaves undone is
exposed to the glare of publicity, and that the
moral value of the party will be judged by this
behavior."

Hitler was furious when he got this note, and he
never forgot who was responsible. Later, he "liquidat-
ed" many of the older conservatives who had dared
criticize him. Indeed, the Fuehrer seldom forgets an
offense, although he is willing to release himself from
many promises of gratitude. Typical of this trait in
his character is the story of the Jewish manufacturer, an
unimportant fellow with bad judgment but a soft heart,
who once saved Hitler's life. Hitler at the time said
he would never forget this service. Later, when the
Jews were being persecuted and this particular Jew's
business was "Aryanized", he wrote to Hitler and
reminded him of the promise. For a long time there
was no reply, but at last Hitler did answer. He said
he could do nothing for his former benefactor, as the
policy of the State came first and was paramount!

不应因其在美女陪伴下的行为而受到评判。但元首必须意识到，他所做或未做的一切都暴露在公众关注的强光之下，党的道德价值将根据这种行为来评判。”

希特勒收到这张纸条时勃然大怒，他从未忘记是谁对此负责。后来，他“清算”了许多敢于批评他的老保守派。的确，元首很少忘记冒犯，尽管他愿意让自己摆脱许多感恩的承诺。他性格中这一特征的典型例子是关于一位犹太制造商的故事，这是一个判断力差但心肠软的不重要人物，他曾救过希特勒的命。希特勒当时说他永远不会忘记这份恩情。后来，当犹太人受到迫害，这位特定犹太人的生意被“雅利安化”时，他写信给希特勒，提醒他当年的承诺。很长一段时间没有回复，但最后希特勒确实回答了。他说他无法为以前的恩人做任何事，因为国家政策优先且至高无上！

pages.en:
39

The parties at the Platterhof were not always as feminine as they looked. Most of the “beautiful women” were young boys dressed up by Goering. But one lady, Frau Esser, used to attend these brawls dressed in silk breeches, and found special favour with Hitler. Since at this time thousands of workers were literally starving in Germany, some party-members naturally resented these “innocent” pastimes.

All of this was amusing enough for the son of Alois Schicklgruber, but he wasn’t getting very much for-rader. Hanussen, for instance, would join in Bohemian revels with him, but would not introduce him into the Munich drawing-rooms. “He looks like a country barber or a bad waiter,” he explained to Goering. Hitler felt this criticism keenly. He said one day to a young Cologne journalist he had recently met, one Goebbels: “What have they got against me? Is it because I haven’t a title or a PhD? Or because I’m a non-com?”

Goebbels kept a straight face and told him to bide his time. Hitler was able to get along socially with the Hanfstaengls, anyway. Ernst Hanfstaengl’s mother,
pages.zh:

普拉特霍夫的派对并不总是像看起来那样充满女性气息。大多数“美丽的女人”都是戈林打扮的年轻男孩。但有一位女士，埃瑟尔夫人（Frau Esser），常穿着丝绸马裤参加这些喧闹活动，并特别受到希特勒的青睐。鉴于当时德国有成千上万的工人在字面上挨饿，一些党员自然对这些“无辜”的消遣感到不满。

对于阿洛伊斯·希克尔格鲁伯（Alois Schicklgruber）的儿子来说，这一切都足够有趣，但他并没有取得太大进展。例如，汉努森会和他一起参加波西米亚式的狂欢，但不会将他引入慕尼黑的客厅。“他看起来像个乡村理发师或糟糕的服务员，”他向戈林解释道。希特勒敏锐地感受到了这种批评。有一天，他对最近结识的一位年轻的科隆记者戈培尔（Goebbels）说：“他们对我有什么意见？是因为我没有头衔或博士学位吗？还是因为我只是个士官？”

戈培尔板着脸，告诉他等待时机。无论如何，希特勒在社交上能够与汉夫施滕格尔一家相处。恩斯特·汉夫施滕格尔的母亲，

born an American, was an important publisher, and she
saw possibilities in Hitler. She introduced him to rich
people who saw that they might keep labour quiet by
supporting his party. Nevertheless they fully realized
how grotesque he was. A fellow-guest at a Munich
party in 1923 wrote his impressions:

"While he (Hitler) was being introduced he wore
the expression of a public prosecutor at an execution.
I was struck by his voice when he asked the hostess for
tea and cakes, of which he ate enormously. He sat
silent for half an hour. Then the hostess happened to
mention the Jews, defending them jokingly, and he
began to speak without stopping for breath. After a
while he thrust back his chair and stood up, still speak-
ing, or rather yelling in such a powerful and penetrat-
ing voice as I have never heard before or since. In the
next room a child woke up and began to cry."

Roehm bought a Munich paper, the Volkischer
Beobachter, with funds obtained from industrialists who
supported the Reichswehr. Hitler now used it to
appeal to a much larger public, and the paper's tone
became very anti-Semitic. He organized the Storm
pages.zh:
40
出生在美国，是一位重要的出版商，她看到了希特勒的潜力。她将他介绍给富人，这些人认为通过支持他的政党可以让劳工保持安静。尽管如此，他们充分意识到他是多么怪异。1923年慕尼黑派对上的一位同伴写下了他的印象：

“当他（希特勒）被介绍时，他脸上带着行刑场上公诉人的表情。当他向女主人索要茶和蛋糕时，他的声音让我印象深刻，他吃了大量的茶点。他沉默地坐了半个小时。然后女主人偶然提到犹太人，开玩笑地为它们辩护，他开始说话，中间都不换气。过了一会儿，他把椅子往后一推，站了起来，继续说话，或者更确切地说是在吼叫，声音如此有力且穿透人心，是我以前或以后从未听到过的。隔壁房间的一个孩子醒了，开始哭泣。”

罗姆用从支持国防军的工业家那里获得的资金购买了一份慕尼黑报纸，《人民观察家报》（Volkischer Beobachter）。希特勒现在利用它向更广泛的公众发出呼吁，报纸的语气变得非常反犹。他组织了风暴

pages.en:
41
Troopers to throw out from his meetings all hecklers,
whom they thrashed in the streets. “Again and again
my Storm Troopers,” he writes, “would come to the
attack. Again and again they flung themselves like
wolves in packs of eight or ten men on their opponents.
After five minutes I could see scarcely a single man
who did not stream with blood. We never gave ground
till our opponents fell, their heads bathed in blood. . . .
One’s heart was gladdened in this revival of my wartime
experiences.”

In another year these meetings were being held in
other cities. First the Storm Troopers came and pasted
up huge red playcards which bore inflammatory slogans,
while other SA men tore through the streets in trucks,
dumping handbills. When the curious arrived at the
meeting they found tall young bullies posted at all the
doors; armed with truncheons. Then Hitler appeared,
with a bodyguard of his tallest toughs. If nobody in
the hall made a genuine protest, the Nazis would
fabricate one, so that they might terrorize the public.
If they couldn’t create a disturbance in the hall itself
they let fly with chair-legs and truncheons in the streets.
pages.zh:
41
冲锋队员将其集会中的所有起哄者驱逐出去，并在街头对他们进行殴打。“我的冲锋队员，”他写道，“一次又一次地发起攻击。他们一次又一次地像狼群一样，以八到十人为一组扑向对手。五分钟后，我几乎看不到一个不血流满面的人。直到我们的对手倒下、头部浸在血泊中，我们才停止进攻……这种战时经历的复苏令人心旷神怡。”

又过了一年，这些集会在其他城市举行。首先是冲锋队员到来，张贴印有煽动性口号的巨大红色海报，而其他纳粹突击队员（SA）则驾驶卡车穿梭于街道，抛撒传单。当好奇的民众到达会场时，发现所有门口都站着高大的年轻暴徒，手持警棍。随后希特勒出现，身边护卫着他最高大的打手。如果大厅内没有人提出真正的抗议，纳粹分子就会制造一起抗议，以便恐吓公众。如果他们无法在大厅内部制造骚乱，他们就在街道上挥舞椅腿和警棍大闹。

Hitler's words at first were sometimes wild;
he denounced the Jews and various "defined classes".
But he attracted the masses. They were drawn by his
eloquence, and they liked the idea of using the Jews as
a target for their anger under existing conditions.
After a while they began to demand that he do some-
thing definite. In 1923 he was not rich and
contented, and would willingly have kept "working",
but his public wouldn't let him. Thus the Beer-
hall Putsch came about.

希特勒最初的言论有时十分狂野；他谴责犹太人以及各种“特定阶级”。但他吸引了大众。他们被他的口才所吸引，并且喜欢在当时条件下将犹太人作为愤怒发泄目标的想法。过了一会儿，他们开始要求他采取一些具体行动。1923年，他并不富有且安于现状，本愿意继续“工作”，但他的追随者不允许他这样做。于是发生了啤酒馆暴动。

43
the Reich, “those criminal Jews.” Ludendorff wanted
to wait until the Nazis could serve an ultimatum on the
Ebert Government at Berlin, but Hitler and Goering
decided to jump the gun.

On November 8, 1923, the Bavarian General State
Commissioner von Kahr was to give an address at the
Burgerbrauhaus. Kahr believed with Ludendorff that
the time was too early for an uprising. Later he was
to be “liquidated”. He began his speech.

At 8:00 P.M. there was a commotion at the door.
In walked a butcher named Graf, carrying the Nazi
swastika banner. Then came Goering. Then came
Hitler, in a black morning-coat. All carried revolvers.
Hitler jumped on a chair and shot at the ceiling, shout-
ing “Silence!”

Goering was full of dope, and his finger twitched
at the trigger.

“Silence!” bawled Hitler. “The national revolution
has broken out! This hall holds 600 heavily armed
men (actually there were 60). If there is not silence,
we will shoot a machine-gun from the gallery.” He
was bathed in perspiration. He addressed Kahr, who
was simply paralyzed: “Nobody is to leave this hall
pages.zh:
43
帝国的那些人，“那些犯罪的犹太人。”鲁登道夫想等到纳粹能够向柏林的艾伯特政府发出最后通牒时再行动，但希特勒和戈林决定抢先行动。

1923年11月8日，巴伐利亚州总专员冯·卡尔将在贝格勃劳凯勒啤酒馆发表演讲。卡尔与鲁登道夫一样，认为起义的时机尚早。后来他被“清除”。他开始发表演讲。

晚上8点，门口发生了一阵骚动。一个叫格拉夫的屠夫走了进来，举着纳粹卐字旗。接着是戈林。然后是身穿黑色晨礼服的希特勒。所有人都携带左轮手枪。希特勒跳上一把椅子，朝天花板开枪，大喊“安静！”

戈林吸毒成瘾，手指在扳机上抽搐。

“安静！”希特勒吼道。“民族革命已经爆发！这个大厅里有600名全副武装的人（实际上只有60人）。如果不保持安静，我们就从楼座上架起机枪射击。”他浑身大汗淋漓。他对完全吓呆的卡尔说道：“未经我允许，任何人不得离开这个大厅

pages.en:
44
without my permission. I proclaim that the new Reich
government is formed. The Bavarian government is
deposed. The Reich government goes to me."
And so forth. The police captain, Chief Constable
von Seisser, to whom Hitler had only a few days before
pledged not to attempt such a coup, screamed at him,
"You Judas!"
"Yes," admitted Hitler. "I have broken my
promise. But I did it in the interests of the Father-
land. Forgive me. General von Lossow, Ludendorff
is holding himself in readiness. He will be here in a
minute."
After a while, during which the multitude was quiet-
ed by the show of arms and machine-guns, Ludendorff
arrived. He was as surprised as anybody, and he
growled to Hitler. "You should have warned us. It
isn't right to hold us □□ □□ □□. You should have
waited. . . . Nevertheless I □□ □□ the movement—but
not as a corporal's assistant!"
Meantime Rochu, □□ □□ Nazi meeting nearby, an-
nounced that the Nazi re□ □□op had begun. His young
hearers helped him take □□□□ion of the Reichswehr
pages.zh:
44
我宣布新帝国政府成立。巴伐利亚政府被废黜。帝国政府归我掌管。”
等等。警察局长、首席警司冯·赛瑟尔几天前曾向希特勒保证不会尝试此类政变，此时对他尖叫道：“你这个犹大！”
“是的，”希特勒承认。“我违背了诺言。但我是为了祖国的利益。请原谅我。冯·洛索夫将军，鲁登道夫已做好准备。他马上就到。”

过了一会儿，在武器和机枪的展示使人群安静下来之后，鲁登道夫到达了。他和其他人一样惊讶，并对希特勒咆哮道。“你应该警告我们。把我们 □□ □□ □□ 是不对的。你应该等待……尽管如此，我 □□ □□ 这场运动——但不是作为一个下士的助手！”
与此同时，罗姆，□□ □□ 附近的一次纳粹集会，宣布纳粹夺 □□ 权已经开始。他的年轻听众帮助他接管了国防军

pages.en:
45
headquarters in Munich. Nazi party members and SA
men came hurrying from the outskirts of Munich, ready
to make trouble. Ludendorff hurried to the Reichswehr
headquarters. Hitler suddenly disappeared, just when
he should have directed the plan to seize the government
buildings.

The Constable and the Commissioner managed to
send word that they were being detained by force.
Ludendorff grew nervous and sent messengers to find
what had happened to Hitler and Goering; these
messengers were shot by the Bavarian police. Later,
Ludendorff went home; nobody dared arrest him.

Meanwhile Hitler returned to the beer-hall and
learned that the officials in the government buildings
refused to give them up. Reichswehr officers who
remained loyal to the Reich had broadcast orders for
outlying detachments to come to their aid. Ludendorff
went back to the beer-hall and they devised a plan to
march into the center of Munich. He and Hitler were
certain that the police and the loyal Reichswehr men
wouldn't fire on Nazis. They marched into the
Ludwigstrasse just before noon on the 9th, and saw
pages.zh:
45
在慕尼黑的总部。纳粹党成员和冲锋队员从慕尼黑郊区匆匆赶来，准备制造麻烦。鲁登道夫急忙赶往国防军总部。希特勒突然消失了，就在他应该指挥夺取政府大楼的计划时。

警司和专员设法传出消息，称他们被强行扣押。鲁登道夫变得紧张起来，派出信使去查明希特勒和戈林的下落；这些信使被巴伐利亚警察击毙。后来，鲁登道夫回家了；没人敢逮捕他。

与此同时，希特勒回到啤酒馆，得知政府大楼里的官员拒绝交出权力。忠于帝国的国防军军官已广播命令，要求外围分队前来支援。鲁登道夫回到啤酒馆，他们制定了一个进军慕尼黑市中心的计划。他和希特勒确信，警察和忠于帝国的国防军人员不会向纳粹分子开火。他们在9日中午前不久行进至路德维希大街，看到

pages.en:
46
police throwing down their arms, refusing to fire on
war-veterans.

Another detachment, however, fired a volley, and
eleven Nazis went down. Hitler threw himself to the
ground in panic; his shoulder was dislocated. He fled
in his car. Goering fled. Roehm, still at the Reich-
swehr headquarters, surrendered when he believed he
was simply subjecting his men to mass murder.
Ludendorff, saved by his valet's sacrifice of life, was
arrested, but soon afterwards released.

Hitler, having deserted his men, as had Goering,
was by this time being driven at top speed to the home
of "Putzi" Hanfstaengl at Uffing. "Putzi" was not
there, but his sister Erna let Hitler in.

He staggered into the hall and pulled out his gun
hysterically, attempting without sincerity to kill him-
self. Erna got the gun away from him. Two days
later he was arrested there, hiding behind her skirts,
by Reichswehr officers who broke into the house.

The Bavarian government ordered the Nazis dis-
solved, suppressed the paper, and ordered the SA men
into the Reichswehr. Nazis found bearing arms were
pages.zh:
46
警察放下武器，拒绝向退伍军人开火。

然而，另一支分队发射了一排子弹，十一名纳粹分子倒地。希特勒惊慌失措地扑倒在地；他的肩膀脱臼了。他乘车逃跑了。戈林也逃跑了。罗姆当时仍在国防军总部，当他认为自己只是让手下遭受大规模屠杀时，便投降了。鲁登道夫因其仆人的牺牲生命而得救，被捕后不久即获释。

希特勒像戈林一样抛弃了他的手下，此时正被高速驾车送往乌芬的“普齐”汉夫施坦格尔家中。“普齐”不在家，但他的姐姐埃尔娜让希特勒进了屋。

他踉跄着走进大厅，歇斯底里地拔出手枪，试图假装自杀。埃尔娜从他手中夺下了枪。两天后，闯入房屋的国防军军官在那里逮捕了他，当时他正躲在她的裙子后面。

巴伐利亚政府下令解散纳粹党，查封报纸，并命令冲锋队员加入国防军。被发现携带武器的纳粹分子

pages.en:
47
shot on sight. The movement was driven underground,
because Hitler and Goering, the minute they saw signs
of opposition, had run away.
In the following February and March, Hitler,
Ludendorff and eight others were tried for high
treason. Goering was in hiding abroad. Hitler denied
that he had launched the putsch prematurely to make
certain of becoming Reich dictator himself rather than
Goering or somebody else. He insisted that Ludendorff
was his choice for “first officer of the Reich”,
although the old general indignantly denied having
been in on the putsch.
“I only wanted to prepare the field,” he insisted.
Hitler received sentence of five years, although he
served only six months of it. They led him off to the
fortress of Landsberg, hysterically screaming revenge.
There he tried suicide again, by hunger-striking,
but his attention was quickly diverted when Rudolf
Hess, another prisoner who was later to be one of his
ministers, suggested that he dictate his autobiography.
Besides, he had all sorts of special privileges—good
pages.zh:
47
一经发现立即枪决。该运动转入地下，因为希特勒和戈林一看到反对的迹象就逃跑了。
在接下来的二月和三月，希特勒、鲁登道夫和其他八人因叛国罪受审。戈林在国外藏匿。希特勒否认他过早发动政变是为了确保自己而不是戈林或其他人成为帝国独裁者。他坚持说鲁登道夫是他选定的“帝国第一官员”，尽管这位老将军愤怒地否认参与了政变。
“我只是想铺平道路，”他坚持说。
希特勒被判处五年徒刑，但他只服刑了六个月。他们把他带到兰茨贝格要塞，他歇斯底里地叫嚣着复仇。在那里，他再次尝试通过绝食自杀，但当另一名囚犯鲁道夫·赫斯（后来成为他的部长之一）建议他口述自传时，他的注意力很快被转移了。此外，他享有各种特殊待遇——良好的

pages.en:
food, easy hours, and practically as much liberty as a
non-prisoner. Society ladies flocked to visit him, but
it is a matter of record that he paid no attention to
them. He wrote eight hundred pages of "Mein Kampf",
pouring out his hatred of the Jews. Certainly at times
during his imprisonment he was almost completely mad.
He would rant that the putsch had failed be-
cause of "Jewish machinations", and at other times
he would shout for his mother. He also screamed
curses at Goering for having escaped jail.

One woman at least attracted his wandering mind;
a princess who brought him comforting reports that he
was very popular in Bavaria. She said he was a martyr,
and that she and other women were working night and
day for his reputation... the man who had run
away, leaving fourteen of his friends to be killed be-
cause of his own activities.

In prison he was tortured by sexual repression,
which gave him nightmares. This was when he wrote
about "innocent young blonde girls" being raped by
"black-haired Jewboys"; he urged his women readers
to think of his fine young Nazi supporters, "fine up-
pages.zh:
食物、轻松的时间安排，以及几乎与非囚犯一样的自由。社交界的女士们蜂拥而至探望他，但有记录显示他对她们毫不在意。他写了八百页的《我的奋斗》，倾吐他对犹太人的仇恨。毫无疑问，在监禁期间，他有时几乎完全疯了。他会咆哮说政变失败是因为“犹太人的阴谋”，有时又会呼喊他的母亲。他还咒骂戈林逃脱了牢狱之灾。

至少有一位女性吸引了他游移不定的心思；一位公主给他带来了令人欣慰的消息，说他在巴伐利亚非常受欢迎。她说他是烈士，她和其他女性日夜为他的声誉而努力……这个人逃跑了，留下十四位朋友因他的活动而被杀。

在监狱里，他受到性压抑的折磨，这让他做噩梦。就在这个时候，他写道“无辜的金发少女”被“黑头发的犹太男孩”强奸；他敦促他的女性读者想想他优秀的年轻纳粹支持者，“优秀的、

pages.en:
49
standing young men wearing only trousers, stripped to
the waist." It is questionable which person, the author
or the reader, got more pleasure out of this mental
picture!

While he was in prison he appointed Roehm as
his deputy leader, because Roehm as an army officer
had to serve only one day in jail, and Alfred Rosenberg
was to help him. Hitler now began to fret with
jealousy, and actually resigned as Fuehrer on one
occasion. He began to hate Roehm as much as he did
Goering, fearing that the captain would supplant him
in power while he was helpless. Later he wouldn't
appoint Roehm to a party post, after he had been re-
leased and the captain was defeated in election; Roehm
said goodbye and went out to Bolivia as military in-
structor. He was to return later, however.

When Hitler did get out he had no more SA men
to help him. They had been dissolved. He joined
forces with Julius Streicher, who had been with him
in the beer-hall putsch. Streicher, a totally uneducated
man, had brought his Socialist supporters to join the
Nazis in '23. He hated Jews and Catholics even more
pages.zh:
49
只穿裤子、上半身赤裸的年轻男子。”很难说是作者还是读者从这种心理画面中获得了更多的快感！

在狱中期间，他任命罗姆为他的副领袖，因为罗姆作为军官只需在监狱服刑一天，阿尔弗雷德·罗森堡协助他。希特勒现在开始因嫉妒而烦躁，甚至有一次真的辞去了元首职务。他开始像恨戈林一样恨罗姆，担心在他无能为力时，这位上尉会取代他的权力。后来，在罗姆获释并在选举中失利后，他没有任命罗姆担任党内职务；罗姆告别后前往玻利维亚担任军事教官。不过，他后来回来了。

当希特勒出狱时，他再也没有冲锋队员来帮助他。他们已被解散。他与尤利乌斯·施特莱歇尔联手，后者曾与他一起参与啤酒馆暴动。施特莱歇尔是一个完全未受教育的人，他在1923年带领他的社会主义支持者加入了纳粹。他比希特勒更憎恨犹太人和天主教徒，因此在“犹太人性侵犯”问题上也是个疯子。这两人共同创办了一份周刊《冲锋报》，专门刊登犹太人与其非犹太人受害者之间性关系的故事。这是希特勒唯一从头到尾阅读的报纸。

pages.en:
50
than Hitler did so too is a maniac on the subject of
"Jewish sexual outrage". Between them this pair
started a weekly journal, Der Sturmer, which is devoted
to stories of sex-relations between Jews and their
Gentile victims. It is the only newspaper which Hitler
reads from cover to cover.

Today Der Sturmer is distributed throughout
Germany. Its contents are almost completely por-
nographic, cartoons of horrible Jews having sexual
relations with German girls and false stories of sexual
excesses of the same sort, told as if they were true.
Actual names and addresses are given: Streicher is
always being brought into court on libel charges.
Besides this, Streicher sends his SA men to lead Jews
and non-Jewesses through the streets with signs on
their backs—"I have defiled a German girl"—"I have
allowed myself to be defiled by a Jew." Such little
games often result in insanity or suicide of the victims.

On Streicher's birthday Hitler always comes to
see him and to be delighted with such parades through
the streets of Nuremburg. Such placards as this "I
am the biggest sow in town: I never on the Jewboys

50

如今，《冲锋报》发行遍及德国。其内容几乎完全是色情的，包括描绘可怕的犹太人与德国女孩发生性关系的漫画，以及编造的同类性放纵虚假故事，并当作真事讲述。文中列出了真实的姓名和地址：施特莱歇尔经常因诽谤罪被带上法庭。除此之外，施特莱歇尔还派遣他的冲锋队员带领犹太人和非犹太女性游街，背上挂着牌子——“我玷污了一名德国女孩”——“我允许自己被犹太人玷污。”这类小把戏往往导致受害者精神失常或自杀。

在施特莱歇尔的生日，希特勒总是来看望他，并对纽伦堡街头的这类游行感到高兴。诸如“我是镇上最大的母猪：我从不皱眉看犹太男孩”这样的标语让他笑得前仰后合。希特勒、施特莱歇尔、戈培尔和戈林这四人都觉得这些事情极其可笑。

该报定期刊登此类“方框”内容：
“德国同胞们！
你们知道犹太人强奸你们的孩子，玷污你们的妻子，玷污你们的姐妹，玷污你们的情人，谋杀你们的父母，偷窃你们的财物，侮辱你们的荣誉，嘲笑你们的习俗，毁坏你们的教堂，腐蚀你们的文化，污染你们的种族吗！
德国同胞们，因此要求：
对于与非雅利安人发生性关系的德国人，处以苦役、剥夺公民权、没收财产并驱逐出境。对于重犯，处以死刑。后代予以绝育。
对于诱奸，处以长期苦役。”

希特勒以这种方式忙碌，直到他能够重新确立自己的领导地位。最后，他去见海因里希·赫尔德博士，试图达成一项解除对纳粹禁令的交易。他说他永远不会像啤酒馆暴动那样袭击赫尔德的政党，

pages.en:
51
frown" send him into fits of merry laughter. All four,
Hitler, Streicher, Goebbels and Goering, find these
things uproariously funny.
The newspaper regularly publishes this sort of
"box":
"Fellow Germans!
Do you know that the Jew ravishes your child,
defiles your wife, defiles your sister, defiles your
sweetheart, murders your parents, steals your goods,
insults your honour, ridicules your customs, ruins your
church, corrupts your culture, contaminates your race!
Fellow Germans, demand therefore that:
For Germans who have sexual relations with non-
Aryans, penal servitude, deprivation of citizenship
rights, forfeiture of property and expulsion. For back-
sliders, the death penalty. The progeny to be sterilized.
For seduction, long terms of penal servitude."
Hitler kept himself busy in this way until he could
re-establish his leadership. Finally he went to Dr.
Heinrich Held and tried to make a bargain to remove
the ban on Nazis. He said he would never launch an
attack, like the beer-hall putsch on Held's party, the
pages.zh:
51
皱眉”会让他笑得前仰后合。希特勒、施特赖歇尔、戈培尔和戈林这四人都觉得这些事滑稽至极。

该报定期刊登此类“方框”内容：
“德国同胞们！
你们可知，犹太人强奸你们的子女，玷污你们的妻子，玷污你们的姐妹，玷污你们的恋人，谋杀你们的父母，偷窃你们的财物，侮辱你们的荣誉，嘲笑你们的习俗，毁坏你们的教堂，腐蚀你们的文化，污染你们的种族！
德国同胞们，因此要求：
凡与非雅利安人发生性关系的德国人，处以苦役、剥夺公民权、没收财产并驱逐出境。对于悔过自新者，处以死刑。所生子女予以绝育。
对于诱奸行为，判处长期苦役。”

希特勒以这种方式忙碌不已，直至他能够重新确立其领导地位。最后，他去找海因里希·赫尔德博士（Dr. Heinrich Held），试图达成一项交易，以解除对纳粹党的禁令。他说他绝不会像啤酒馆暴动那样攻击赫尔德的政党，

pages.en:
32
Catholic Bavarian People's party He assured Held
that he was only against the Jew Marxists. The Putsch
was a mistake, he admitted, fawning on the Doctor.

Held, minister president of Bavaria, though he dis-
liked the creature, reasoned that he could use him. In
return for the pledge he removed the ban. He might
have known Hitler's pledge was worth nothing; even at
that time, in '25 Hitler had broken many promises, but
he felt it would be better to have him on his side than
against him.

In February Hitler came back and staged a meet-
ing in the same beer-hall that had witnessed the putsch.
He was so fat that nobody recognized him until he started
to shout. He jumped on a table and harangued the
audience; he won back nearly 4000 people by offering
to resign at their command. Next day the outlawed
Volkischer-Beobachter appears again, announcing the
re-establishment of the National Socialist party. Once
again he was started.

HITLER. POLITICAL PROSTITUTE

About this time Hitler's fears of assassination grew
pages.zh:
32
天主教巴伐利亚人民党。他向赫尔德（Held）保证，他只反对犹太马克思主义者。他承认政变是一个错误，并对这位博士阿谀奉承。

巴伐利亚州总理赫尔德虽然讨厌这个家伙，但认为可以利用他。作为对其承诺的回报，他解除了禁令。他本该知道希特勒的承诺一文不值；即便在那时，即1925年，希特勒已经违背了许多诺言，但他觉得让希特勒站在自己这边总比与他为敌要好。

二月，希特勒归来，并在见证过那次政变的同一家啤酒馆举行了一场集会。他胖得没人认出他来，直到他开始大喊大叫。他跳上一张桌子，向听众发表煽动性演讲；他提出听从众人命令辞职，从而赢回了近4000人的支持。次日，被禁的《人民观察家报》（Volkischer-Beobachter）再次出版，宣布重建国家社会主义党。他又一次开始了行动。

希特勒。政治妓女

大约在这个时候，希特勒对暗杀的恐惧变得

pages.en:
53.
extreme. Streicher and Goering, especially the latter,
who by this time had been permitted to return to
Germany, scoffed at him, but he could not be laughed
out of his terrors. He had a bodyguard watching over
him day and night. He insisted upon having an
official “food-taster” for fear of poison. He would not
travel by train for fear somebody would wreck it; he
went by motor on his speaking-tours, with at least two
cars ahead of him, two behind, and his SS Elite Guard
standing on the running-board all around him. Lesser
Nazi leaders called him “Madame Hitler”. He began
to have the fits of hysterical weeping for which he is now
well known. Doctors he visited at that time regarded
him as a “dual personality”, or schizophrenic case.
He had moods of despair, convinced that his post as
leader was being sought by Roehm, Rosenberg, Hess,
Goebbels and Goering, all men nearest to him.

Three American psychiatrists have given their
diagnoses as to his insanity. Karl Menninger seems to
think he is a megalomaniac—“delusions of grandeur”.
Dr. Raeder says “Hitler is an infantile personality.
His temper tantrums, his weeping . . . are childhood
pages.zh:
53.
极度严重。施特莱歇尔（Streicher）和戈林（Goering），尤其是后者，此时已被允许返回德国，对他嗤之以鼻，但他无法因嘲笑而消除恐惧。他有一名保镖日夜守护着他。出于对中毒的恐惧，他坚持要有一名官方的“试食员”。出于担心有人破坏火车，他不乘火车旅行；他在巡回演讲时乘坐汽车，前面至少有两辆车开道，后面有两辆车跟随，他的党卫队精英护卫队（SS Elite Guard）站在他周围的踏板上。地位较低的纳粹领导人称他为“希特勒夫人”。他开始出现如今众所周知的歇斯底里哭泣发作。当时为他诊治的医生认为他是“双重人格”或精神分裂症病例。他陷入绝望的情绪，确信罗姆（Roehm）、罗森伯格（Rosenberg）、赫斯（Hess）、戈培尔（Goebbels）和戈林——这些离他最近的人——都在觊觎他的领袖职位。

三位美国精神病学家对他的精神失常给出了诊断。卡尔·门宁格（Karl Menninger）似乎认为他是一个妄想狂——“夸大妄想”。雷德尔（Raeder）博士说：“希特勒是一个幼稚型人格。他的脾气爆发、他的哭泣……是童年

pages.en:
64
fixations. He is amoral and probably sadistic.” Dr.
Brill says “Hitler is a psychoparanoid personality
whose sole need is hatred. All his actions are dominat-
ed by this sadistic leitmotif. His hatred for Jews and
his love for Germans are mere excuses for his algolagnia
—that is, for his pleasure in pain. But such lust for
destruction always carries with it self-destruction.”

Whether you understand all those big words or not,
the sum of these statements is simple fact—Hitler is a
lunatic.

His fine friends of former days realized it, and
dropped him. Putzi Hanfstaengl said “I think the
man’s insane.” The Princess and other feminine friends
from the upper class in Munich were afraid of a party
leader who had periods of insanity. One of his North-
Germany Nazi supporters writes: “At this time he
was sickeningly moody. His temper changes by fits
and starts. He can ring all the changes; at one moment
he is the ‘good boy’, clumsily kissing the hand of his
motherly friend, Bechstein, and at the next he can be
the highly strung artist and find life ‘exquisitely
painful’. At one moment he is full of disdain and fury,
pages.zh:
64
固着。他是非道德的，可能是施虐狂。”布里尔（Brill）博士说：“希特勒是一个心理偏执型人格，其唯一的需求就是仇恨。他所有的行为都受这种施虐主导动机的支配。他对犹太人的仇恨和对德国人的爱仅仅是为了掩饰他的痛感快乐症（algolagnia）——即他从痛苦中获得快感。但这种毁灭欲总是伴随着自我毁灭。”

无论你是否理解那些大词，这些陈述的总结是一个简单的事实——希特勒是个疯子。

他昔日的良朋好友意识到了这一点，并抛弃了他。普齐·汉夫施滕格尔（Putzi Hanfstaengl）说：“我认为这个人疯了。”慕尼黑的公主和其他上层社会的女性朋友害怕这位有精神失常时期的政党领袖。他的一位北德纳粹支持者写道：“在这段时间里，他的情绪令人作呕地多变。他的脾气阵发性地改变。他能表现出各种面貌；一会儿他是‘乖孩子’，笨拙地亲吻他母亲般的朋友贝希斯坦（Bechstein）的手，下一刻他又变成高度紧张的艺术家，觉得生活‘极其痛苦’。一会儿他充满蔑视和愤怒，

pages.en:
55
at the next he is all smiles and tenderness. And to
soften up his stubborn friends, when necessary he
breaks down in tears like a baby girl."

Probably, as a matter of fact, he was play-acting
a good deal of the time. His actions were cool and
calculating enough. He made friends with Alfred
Hugenberg, a great industrialist, who told him flatly
that he had no sympathy for the Fuehrer's self or his
party and friends. But they had been able to dupe many
of the labour-leaders, and that was what the financier
wanted then to keep on doing; he promised support.
"Our aims are the same," he admitted; "we want to
destroy the Republic, tear up the Versailles treaty,
destroy the trade-unions, wipe out the Social Democrats,
and exterminate the Communists."

Hitler sold himself to Hugenberg because the in-
dustrialist controlled scores of newspapers and had
plenty of money. He told Goebbels and others that he
intended to play along with the financier until they had
all they needed, and could crowd their benefactor out.
With Hugenberg's support he regained a lot of the
confidence of his acquaintances and lost some of his
pages.zh:
55
下一刻他又满脸笑容和温柔。为了软化他那些固执的朋友，必要时他会像小女孩一样崩溃大哭。”

事实上，他很可能大部分时间都在演戏。他的行为足够冷静和算计。他与大工业家阿尔弗雷德·胡根贝格（Alfred Hugenberg）交上了朋友，后者直截了当地告诉他，他对元首本人及其党派和朋友毫无同情。但他们已经能够欺骗许多工会领导人，而这正是这位金融家当时想要继续做的事情；他承诺提供支持。“我们的目标是一致的，”他承认；“我们要摧毁共和国，撕毁《凡尔赛条约》，摧毁工会，消灭社会民主党人，并灭绝共产党人。”

希特勒将自己出卖给胡根贝格，因为这位工业家控制着数十家报纸并拥有大量资金。他告诉戈培尔和其他人，他打算与这位金融家周旋，直到他们获得所需的一切，然后将他们的恩人排挤出去。在胡根贝格的支持下，他重新赢得了熟人们的许多信任，并失去了一些

pages.en:
56
hysteria. He increased his personal bodyguard as
soon as he could afford to. And now that he had
so much control of the press, anti-Semitism spread by
leaps and bounds. All the ills of Germany were blamed
on Jewish capitalists.

Posters appeared overnight on Berlin department
stores which were owned by Jews, advertising the fact
with much accompanying abuse. Lawyers and doctors
found their offices decorated with the “yellow spot”,
that dread insignia of the Middle Ages.

Hugenberg also owned or controlled several broad-
casting stations; Hitler screamed and Goebbels scream-
ed through these networks until hundreds and thousands
of ignorant young Germans began to believe that the
only thing that stood between them and the pre-war
conditions in Germany were half a million Jews. It
began to be fashionable to spit at Jews in the street.
Assaults on Jews were condoned by the government.
Of course many people were disgusted by these develop-
ments, but the SS and SA men now numbered hundreds
of thousands, many more than the municipal police in
pages.zh:
56
歇斯底里。一旦负担得起，他就增加了个人保镖的数量。既然他现在控制了如此多的媒体，反犹主义便迅速蔓延。德国的所有弊病都被归咎于犹太资本家。

一夜之间，柏林由犹太人拥有的百货公司出现了海报，大肆宣扬这一事实并伴有大量的辱骂。律师和医生发现他们的办公室被装饰上了“黄点”，那是中世纪可怕的标志。

胡根贝格还拥有或控制着几家广播电台；希特勒和戈培尔通过这些网络大声叫喊，直到成千上万无知的年轻德国人开始相信，阻碍他们回到战前德国状况的只有五十万犹太人。在街上朝犹太人吐口水开始成为一种时尚。政府对袭击犹太人的行为予以纵容。当然，许多人对这些发展感到厌恶，但此时党卫队（SS）和冲锋队（SA）的人数已达数十万，比大多数城镇的市政警察还要多，是正规军国防军（Reichswehr）规模的三到四倍。

pages.en:
57
most towns, and three or four times the size of the
Reichswehr, the regular army.

By 1930 the press attacked not only “Jew bastards
and Jewish sows” but anybody who wasn’t a Nazi.
Hindenberg, who detested the upstart corporal, began to
fear it would be necessary to summon him to head the
government at the next election.

As the Nazi party grew in vogue, so did sexual
abnormality. Hitler, if not an active homosexual
himself, was tolerant of homosexuality and more than
tolerant. He was constantly surrounded by homosexual
men and women, particularly Captain Roehm, who was
fond of saying, “It is the inalienable right of every
German to be homosexual!” Thousands of young
people took up this perversion: it became the fashion, a
sort of symbol of the party. Berlin was famous
throughout the world for “pansy” and “Lesbian”
cafés, and girls and women embracing, and rouged men
dancing together, were common sights in Berlin’s
Broadway, the Kurfurstendamm. Hitler constantly
urged larger families, but he himself never married, and
once he began forging ahead with Hugenberg’s help he
pages.zh:
57
到1930年，媒体不仅攻击“犹太杂种和犹太母猪”，还攻击任何非纳粹分子。兴登堡（Hindenberg）憎恨这个暴发户下士，开始担心在下一次选举中不得不召见他来领导政府。

随着纳粹党的流行，性变态也随之增加。即使希特勒本人不是活跃的同性恋者，他也容忍同性恋，甚至不止是容忍。他周围 constantly 围绕着同性恋男女，特别是罗姆上尉，他喜欢说：“每个德国人都有不可剥夺的权利成为同性恋！”成千上万的年轻人染上了这种变态行为：它成为一种时尚，一种党派的象征。柏林以“男娘”和“女同性恋”咖啡馆闻名于世，在柏林的百老汇——库弗斯坦达姆大街（Kurfurstendamm），女孩和女人拥抱、涂脂抹粉的男人一起跳舞是常见的景象。希特勒不断鼓励多生孩子，但他自己从未结婚，而且一旦在胡根贝格的帮助下开始突飞猛进，他就

pages.en:
36
avoided women completely. Only one person received
his affections, and that was a boy named Schiller to
whom it was said he wrote a number of erotic letters.
Schiller became frightened of Hitler as he realized that
the Fuehrer was violent and sometimes insane; he ran
away to Switzerland and put the letters into a safe-
deposit. He only just got away with his life; Hitler
was about to "liquidate" him, for fear the letters would
be given to his enemies. Even though it was the vogue
to be "homo", to have a pansy leader would be too
much for German public opinion.

One of the most erotic chapters in "Mein Kampf"
deals with syphilis: Hitler says the Jews have given
this disease to Germany. He grows unnaturally excited
in this part of the book: one can imagine him rolling
the words over in his mouth as he inveighs against
sensuality and lasciviousness. He forgets that he is
discussing syphilis, and runs riot on the entire subject
of sex. Such an attitude is typical of the impotent,
warped, abnormal human.

He was blackmailed more than once, though the
Nazi party treasurer, Franz Schwarz, usually rescued
pages.zh:
36
完全避开女性。只有一个人得到了他的 affection，那是一个名叫席勒（Schiller）的男孩，据说他给这个男孩写了许多色情信件。当席勒意识到元首暴力且有时精神失常时，他变得害怕起来；他逃往瑞士，并将信件存入保险箱。他勉强保住了性命；希特勒正准备“清除”他，因为担心信件会落入敌人手中。尽管成为“同性恋”是一种时尚，但拥有一位男娘领袖会让德国公众舆论难以接受。

《我的奋斗》中最色情的章节之一是关于梅毒的：希特勒说犹太人将这种疾病传给了德国。他在书的这一部分变得异常兴奋：可以想象他在抨击肉欲和淫荡时，嘴里反复咀嚼着这些词语。他忘记了自己在讨论梅毒，而在整个性话题上肆意妄为。这种态度是典型的无能、扭曲、异常人类的特征。

他不止一次遭到勒索，尽管纳粹党财务主管弗朗茨·施瓦茨（Franz Schwarz）通常 rescue

pages.en:
59
him. There was bad blood between these two officials
because of Hitler's extravagance, particularly after he
leased an enormous flat and decorated it just when
party funds were getting low. He took the entire floor
beneath for his bodyguard. Schwarz, knowing that
the party must also pay for rallies, parades, uniforms
and arms for the SS men, quarrelled openly with the
Fuehrer. Hitler almost blew up with rage; he whipped
Schwarz with the dog-whip he always carries, and
Schwarz threatened to shoot him. Hitler of course
carried his point in the end, but his excesses and those
of his men went too far at last.

The SA bodyguard grew so noisy and wild that
Goebbels, as propaganda chief, grew worried about
the approaching 1932 election. Even though most of
the press was favourable, the editors could not cover
up the parties that went on in the bodyguards' quarters
--the men dressed as women with their faces made up
and their wigs and corsets, and women dressed as men.

Hitler himself saw the danger, and ordered that
all party-members keep quiet for the fortnight preced-
ing the election. Even Roehm was being a good boy.
pages.zh:
59
他。由于希特勒的挥霍无度，这两名官员之间产生了嫌隙，特别是在党资金紧张之际，他租下一套巨大的公寓并进行装修。他将楼下整层留给他的保镖使用。施瓦茨知道党还必须支付集会、游行、制服以及党卫队队员武器的费用，因此公开与元首争吵。希特勒几乎气得爆炸；他用随身携带的狗鞭抽打施瓦茨，施瓦茨则威胁要开枪打死他。当然，希特勒最终达到了目的，但他及其手下的过分行为最终还是做得太过了。

冲锋队保镖变得如此喧闹和狂野，以至于宣传主管戈培尔对即将到来的1932年选举感到担忧。尽管大多数媒体持赞成态度，但编辑们无法掩盖保镖宿舍里发生的派对——男人们穿着女装，化着妆，戴着假发和束腰，而女人们则穿着男装。

希特勒本人也看到了危险，命令所有党员在选举前的两周内保持安静。就连罗姆也在表现得像个乖孩子。

pages.en:
60
One night during this period the Fuehrer came home
early, unexpectedly, and found a party going on in the
bodyguard's flat. He ordered his chauffeur and
favorite, Schreck, to break down the door, drew his gun,
and stepped in.

He was disgusted, even he, with the spectacle.
On a couch lay two of the bodyguard, caught in the act.

Hitler's voice was raised to an insane pitch. "Ach,
you're not men, you're beasts!" Then he beckoned to
Schreck, who obediently shot each man through the
temple.

Hitler then went racing down the street shaking his
whip as if he were beating somebody nobody else could
see. Hess found him hours later, asleep in a country ditch.
He brought home the Leader of the German nation,
put him to bed, applied sedatives, and nursed him back
to composure.

The bodies of the guards were sneaked out of the
house and buried outside Munich. It was a prophecy
of June 30, 1934.

在此期间的一天晚上，元首意外地提前回家，发现保镖的公寓里正在举行派对。他命令他的司机兼宠儿施雷克（Schreck）撞开门，拔出手枪，走了进去。

即使是他也对眼前的景象感到厌恶。沙发上躺着两名保镖，正在行苟且之事时被当场抓获。

希特勒的声音提高到了疯狂的音调。“啊，你们不是男人，你们是野兽！”然后他向施雷克示意，后者顺从地向每个人的太阳穴开了一枪。

随后，希特勒沿着街道狂奔，挥舞着鞭子，仿佛在鞭打别人看不见的某人。几小时后，赫斯发现他睡在乡间的一条沟渠里。赫斯将这位德国民族领袖带回家，让他上床休息，服用镇静剂，并护理他恢复平静。

保镖的尸体被偷偷运出房屋，埋葬在慕尼黑郊外。这是1934年6月30日的预兆。

pages.en:
61

MUTINY

There was some reason for Hitler's tantrums:
he had many worries. The SA men were getting
out of hand in Berlin. They claimed they had not
enough food, nor enough recreation; they said that
their officers had funds and time to play at whatever
dirty pleasure they liked while their men were starving.
In Berlin a crowd of the Social Democrat opposition
raided Goebbels' office and smashed it up. Sometimes
they overturned and burned officers' cars. Also, in
North Germany there were Storm Troopers who refused
to do duty at Nazi meetings.

The Stallheim, counter-revolutionary monarchist
organization, similar to the SA, numbered about 100,000
—they were Hugenberg's own army, and a dangerous
weapon. Hitler was losing some of his numbers since
the 1930 election. Could he maintain the 107 Nazi
posts in the Reichstag?

He became jittery, and egged Streicher on to even
greater anti-Jewish obscenity in Der Sturmer. He also
bought himself an art collection and a huge library.
Other prominent Nazis too began to feather their nests.
pages.zh:
61

兵变

希特勒发脾气是有原因的：他有许多烦恼。柏林的冲锋队队员变得难以控制。他们声称没有足够的食物，也没有足够的娱乐活动；他们说，当他们的士兵挨饿时，他们的军官却有资金和时间去享受任何他们喜欢的肮脏乐趣。在柏林，一群社会民主党反对派袭击了戈培尔的办公室并将其砸烂。有时他们会掀翻并烧毁军官的汽车。此外，在德国北部，有一些冲锋队员拒绝在纳粹集会上执勤。

斯塔海姆（Stallheim）是一个反革命君主主义组织，类似于冲锋队，人数约为10万——他们是胡根贝格自己的军队，也是一件危险的武器。自1930年选举以来，希特勒的支持者人数有所减少。他能维持国会中的107个纳粹席位吗？

他变得神经质，并怂恿施特莱歇尔在《冲锋报》（Der Sturmer）上发表更加恶毒的反犹言论。他还为自己购买了一批艺术收藏品和一个巨大的图书馆。其他著名的纳粹分子也开始为自己谋取私利。

pages.en:
62
Max Amann, Robert Ley. Heinrich Hoffman, Heinrich
Himmler, Rudolf Hess, William Frick, Julius Streicher,
Lutze —they all did themselves extremly well; many
of them are now millionaires from grabbing at that time
all the workers' funds they could get.

As the elections approached, Hitler moved to Berlin,
to the Kaiserhof Hotel near the Reich Chancellor's
offices. When General von Schleicher's cabinet fell, it
looked as if he would have power. but old Hindenburg
called in Von Papen to form a government instead.

The 1932 elections brought Hitler two-fifths of the
seats in the Reichstag, and he demanded the chancellor-
ship of Hindenburg, then 84 years old. Hindenburg
told his son, "I'm damned if I let that madman head
the government," and he said to Hitler himself, "I
recommend that you at least conduct the opposition like
a gentleman."

Hitler never forgot the insult.

In August, 1932, he called in his SS and SA men
from all parts of Germany and encircled the capital,
prepared to seize the government by force if necessary.
His men were armed and he was sure the Reichswehr
pages.zh:
62
马克斯·阿曼（Max Amann）、罗伯特·莱伊（Robert Ley）、海因里希·霍夫曼（Heinrich Hoffman）、海因里希·希姆莱（Heinrich Himmler）、鲁道夫·赫斯（Rudolf Hess）、威廉·弗里克（William Frick）、朱利叶斯·施特莱歇尔（Julius Streicher）、卢策（Lutze）——他们都过得极好；其中许多人现在都是百万富翁，因为他们在那时攫取了所有能得到的工人基金。

随着选举临近，希特勒搬到了柏林，住进靠近帝国总理办公室的凯撒霍夫酒店（Kaiserhof Hotel）。当冯·施莱谢尔将军（General von Schleicher）的内阁倒台时，看起来他将掌握权力。但老兴登堡却召见冯·帕彭（Von Papen）组建政府。

1932年的选举为希特勒带来了国会五分之一的席位，他向当时已84岁高龄的兴登堡要求总理职位。兴登堡告诉他的儿子：“如果我让那个疯子领导政府，我就该死，”他对希特勒本人说：“我建议你们至少像绅士一样进行反对派活动。”

希特勒从未忘记这一侮辱。

1932年8月，他从德国各地召集党卫队和冲锋队队员，包围了首都，准备在必要时武力夺取政府。他的人武装齐全，他确信国防军
