would not fire on former soldiers—though the SA con-
tained many hoodlums who had never been soldiers,
this fact was kept quiet. Both he and Goebbels began
to make fantastic promises. Goebbels screamed that
the day Hitler moved into the Chancellery, unemploy-
ment would cease. Hitler promised land to every
farmer. The industrialists were promised reduced
taxes. All the peasants would be free of their debts
and would immediately receive 20,000 marks in cash
apiece. And the public believed them!

Early in 1933 the cabinet fell and the dying
Hindenburg unwillingly summoned Hitler.

The dope addict Goering was made minister without
portfolio. The sexmad Goebbels was made head of the
new Propaganda ministry.

Hitler had “arrived”, after trampling on every
friend and betraying everybody he knew.

Goebbels counselled a way to bring the nation under
fear of the Bolsheviks; Goering wanted military law.
Hitler voted for Goebbels. In four weeks they had
burned the Reichstag, blamed it on the Bolsheviks, and
started a reign of terror which must have satisfied even

不会向退伍军人开火——尽管冲锋队（SA）中包含许多从未当过兵的流氓，但这一事实被刻意隐瞒。他和戈培尔开始做出荒诞的承诺。戈培尔叫嚣说，希特勒入主总理府之日，失业现象就会终结。希特勒承诺给每个农民土地。工业家们被许诺减税。所有农民将免除债务，并立即每人获得2万马克现金。而公众竟然相信了他们！

1933年初，内阁垮台，垂死的兴登堡不情愿地召见了希特勒。

吸毒成瘾的戈林被任命为无 portfolio 部长（注：即不管部部长）。好色成性的戈培尔被任命为新成立的宣传部部长。

希特勒“得势”了，这是在他践踏每一位朋友、背叛每一个认识的人之后实现的。

戈培尔建议利用对布尔什维克的恐惧来控制国家；戈林则希望实行军法管制。希特勒支持了戈培尔的提议。在四周内，他们制造了国会纵火案，将其归咎于布尔什维克，并开始了恐怖统治，这一定甚至满足了

pages.en:
64
the diseased cravings of the new Chancellor. Germany
wallowed in blood.

Marinus van der Lubbe, a homosexual idiot who had
been a boy-friend of Roehm as well as many other Nazi
leaders, was selected as scapegoat for this move. Goeb-
bels and Goering had planted a lot of faked seditious
literature in the Berlin Communist quarters. Goering
quickly arrested all Communist members of the
Reichstag, van der Lubbe "confessed" to an act of in-
cendiarism, and the powers of the inferior courts were
suspended as under military law.

A huge number of concentration camps were hastily
constructed. Thousands of prisoners were put into
Columbus House, questioned and tortured. Foreign
newspaperman quickly accused the Nazis of the obvious
fact that they had set the Reichstag fire themselves.
The incendiaries had reached the Reichstag by an
underground passage leading from the official home of
Goering. The actual fire had been set by Goering,
several SA men, and Count Helldorf, the police chief
of Postdam, an intimate of Roehm's. They had poured
benzine and gasoline throughout the building first.
pages.zh:
64
这位新总理病态的欲望。德国陷入血泊之中。

马里努斯·范·德·卢贝（Marinus van der Lubbe），一个同性恋白痴，曾是罗姆以及许多其他纳粹领导人的男友，被选为此次行动的替罪羊。戈培尔和戈林在柏林共产党社区安插了大量伪造的煽动性文献。戈林迅速逮捕了国会中所有的共产党成员，范·德·卢贝“供认”了纵火行为，下级法院的权力被暂停，如同处于军法管制之下。

大量集中营被匆忙建立。数千名囚犯被关进哥伦布大楼（Columbus House），遭受审问和酷刑。外国记者迅速指责纳粹犯下了显而易见的事实，即他们自己点燃了国会大厦。纵火者通过一条从戈林官邸通出的地下通道到达国会大厦。实际点火的是戈林、几名冲锋队员以及波茨坦警察局长赫尔道夫伯爵（Count Helldorf），他是罗姆的亲信。他们事先在整个建筑物内泼洒了苯和汽油。

pages.en:
65

Hitler nevertheless made a long, elaborate speech
of lies about this “disclosure of a Bolshevist world
plot” from which “all of Germany cried for help by
telephone, telegram and wireless.” He promised judicial
proceedings to punish the offenders. “Bend or Break
is my watchword,” he said.

The “judicial proceedings” were the most obvious
farce. Von der Lubbe when he was brought in had
been tortured and doped. Having been promised im-
munity if he would “confess”, the simple-minded
Hollander did his little duty, and then to his astonish-
ment he was condemned to be executed.

As he approached the block he screamed, “Where
are Hitler and Goering and Goebbels! Where is
Roehm? They should all be here instead of me! They
forced me to help them fire the building; they promised
to get me out of the country. They——”

The axe cut him short.

POGROMS

Von Papen, as vice-chancellor, solemnly declared
that “Jewish citizens in Germany may rest assured

尽管如此，希特勒就这一“揭露布尔什维克世界阴谋”的事件发表了一篇长篇大论、精心编造的谎言演讲，声称“全德国都通过电话、电报和无线电呼救”。他承诺进行司法程序以惩罚罪犯。“不屈服就毁灭是我的座右铭，”他说。

所谓的“司法程序”是一场最明显的闹剧。范·德·卢贝被带进来时已遭受酷刑并被注射毒品。由于被告知如果“招供”即可获得豁免，这位头脑简单的荷兰人履行了他的小小义务，随后令他惊讶的是，他被判处死刑。

当他走向断头台时，他尖叫道：“希特勒、戈林和戈培尔在哪里！罗姆在哪里？他们都应该在这里而不是我！他们强迫我帮他们烧毁大楼；他们答应把我送出国外。他们——”

斧头落下，截断了他的声音。

大屠杀（POGROMS）

副总理冯·巴本庄严宣布，“德国的犹太公民可以放心

that they will enjoy exactly the same treatment as all
good citizens."
Meanwhile the first batches of Jews were arriving
at the concentration camps and subjected to torture
devices which Goering had borrowed from the days of
the Spanish Inquisition. One of these was a small
wooden clamp placed on the testicles. The Nazis by
such means obtained whatever confessions they wanted.
Goebbels prohibited German newspapers, the radio, the
theatre and the movies from showing anything his
department did not approve, so the gangsters were per-
fectly safe.
To keep the Germans from realizing that the
absurd pre-election promises were not being kept,
Goebbels realized that the Nazis must divert the people.
He used two "divertissements" --the Aryan movement,
and the blood-purge of 1933.
Six weeks after Von Papen's announcement, Hitler
ordered Goebbels to open a six weeks' propaganda
movement against the Jews. Goebbels launched his
campaign with a speech; "We have been very lenient
with the Jews. But if they think because of this they
pages.zh:
66
他们将享受与所有良好公民完全相同的待遇。”
与此同时，第一批犹太人抵达集中营，并遭受戈林从西班牙宗教裁判所时期借来的酷刑装置的折磨。其中一种装置是夹在睾丸上的小木夹。纳粹通过此类手段获得了他们想要的任何供词。戈培尔禁止德国报纸、广播、剧院和电影展示任何未经其部门批准的内容，因此这些暴徒绝对安全。
为了让德国人意识不到那些荒谬的选前承诺并未兑现，戈培尔意识到纳粹必须转移民众的注意力。他使用了两种“消遣”——雅利安人运动，以及1933年的血腥清洗。
在冯·巴本发表声明六周后，希特勒命令戈培尔开展为期六周的反犹宣传运动。戈培尔以一篇演讲 launched 他的竞选活动；“我们对犹太人一直非常宽容。但如果他们因此认为

pages.en:

can still be allowed on German stages, offering art to
the German people; if they think they can still sneak
into editorial offices and write for German newspapers:
if they still strut across the Kurfurstendamm as though
nothing had happened, let them take this warning. Jewry
can rest assured that we will leave them alone as long as
they retire quietly and modestly behind their four walls,
as long as they are not provocative, and do not affront
the German people with the claim to be treated as
equals. If the Jews do not listen to these warnings they

Next day in an article in his own newspaper he
said, "We do not sing the praise of pogroms, we do not
call for the persecution of the Jews, but we do want
to show how once again the Jew dares to behave and
how he ought to behave. We hereby ask all our readers,
party members, Storm Troopers and workers, to draw
our attention to any case of Jewish insolence which has
come to their notice during the last months and weeks,
so that we can give it due publicity."

Goebbels' wife's stepfather was a Jew, living in
Berlin.

仍然可以允许他们登上德国舞台，向德国人民提供艺术；如果他们认为自己仍然可以潜入编辑部并为德国报纸撰稿：如果他们仍然像什么都没发生一样在库弗斯坦达姆大街（Kurfurstendamm）大摇大摆，那就让他们接受这个警告。犹太人可以放心，只要他们安静且谦逊地退居四壁之内，只要他们不具挑衅性，不以要求平等待遇来冒犯德国人民，我们就不会打扰他们。如果犹太人不听从这些警告，后果将由他们自己负责。”

第二天，在他自己的报纸上发表的一篇文章中，他说：“我们不歌颂大屠杀，我们不呼吁迫害犹太人，但我们确实想展示犹太人再次如何胆大妄为，以及他们应该如何表现。我们在此请求所有读者、党员、冲锋队员和工人，提请注意他们在过去几个月和几周内注意到的任何犹太人傲慢无礼的案例，以便我们可以给予适当的公开曝光。”

戈培尔妻子的继父是犹太人，住在柏林。

The majority of the German press began publishing
the same stuff. Jews began to try to get some of their
money and property out of the country; they were im-
mediately thrown into concentration camps.
The campaign had results. People forgot their
hardships, their poverty and lack of food and education
for their children; they talked of the Jewish menace,
the international plot of world Jewry, etc. etc. But
Hitler wanted more definite action.
First he promulgated the Nuremberg "Aryan"
laws. Jews were deprived of all citizenship rights and
reduced to the status of pariah. Marriages between
"Aryans" and Jews were forbidden. Jewesses less
than 45 could not enter domestic service. Later, Jews
were forbidden all professional and other employment,
and since then, as we know the entire Jewish wealth in
the Reich has been confiscated.
When the Jews abroad, against the tortures and
restrictions placed on innocent people, organized a
boycott of German goods, the Nazis replied with more
brutal persecutions and a complete boycott of Jewish
enterprise within Germany. Thousands of Jews were
pages.zh:

德国大多数媒体开始发布相同的内容。犹太人开始试图将他们的一些金钱和财产转移出该国；他们随即被投入集中营。
这场运动产生了效果。人们忘记了他们的苦难、贫困以及子女缺乏食物和教育的情况；他们谈论犹太人的威胁、世界犹太人的国际阴谋等等。但希特勒想要更明确的行动。
首先，他颁布了纽伦堡“雅利安”法案。犹太人被剥夺了所有公民权利，沦为贱民地位。“雅利安人”与犹太人之间的婚姻被禁止。45岁以下的犹太女性不得从事家政服务。后来，犹太人被禁止从事所有专业和其他工作，此后，众所周知，帝国境内的全部犹太财富已被没收。
当海外犹太人针对施加在无辜人身上的酷刑和限制组织抵制德国货时，纳粹以更残酷的迫害和对德国境内犹太企业的全面抵制作为回应。数千名犹太人

pages.en:
69
herded together by the SA and forced to stand for
hours with arms uplifted. They were beaten in public,
or put on the rack in concentration camps.

Throughout the nation posters like this were put up:

Men and women of Germany! The people respon-
sible for this mad crime (the foreign boycott), this
base agitation by atrocity-mongering and boycott, are
the Jews in Germany. They have asked their brethren
abroad to fight the Germans. They have spread lies
and calumny. That is why the Reich leadership for
German freedom has decided, in defense against these
criminal slanders, to boycott all Jewish shops, depart-
ment stores, etc. We ask you, German men and women,
to fall in with this boycott. Do not buy in Jewish
shops! Do not go to Jewish lawyers! Avoid Jewish
physicians, who are all diseased! Show the Jews they
cannot drag Germany's honour in the mud without be-
ing punished! Whoever does not comply with this
demand proves himself an enemy to Germany!

These and more violent attacks were published
everywhere, but even this was not enough to keep all
the people busy and forgetful of their own troubles.
pages.zh:

被冲锋队驱赶在一起，被迫举臂站立数小时。他们在公共场合遭到殴打，或在集中营里遭受拉肢刑。

全国各地张贴着如下海报：

德国的男男女女！造成这一疯狂罪行（外国抵制）、这一基于散布暴行谣言和抵制的卑鄙煽动的责任人，是德国的犹太人。他们请求海外的同胞对抗德国人。他们散布谎言和诽谤。因此，为了防御这些犯罪性的诽谤，德国自由帝国领导层决定抵制所有犹太商店、百货公司等。我们请求德国男男女女配合这一抵制。不要在犹太商店购物！不要去找犹太律师！避开犹太医生，他们都患有疾病！向犹太人表明，他们不能在不受惩罚的情况下将德国的荣誉拖入泥潭！任何不遵守这一要求的人证明自己是德国的敌人！

这些以及更激烈的攻击随处可见，但即便如此，仍不足以让所有人忙碌并忘记自己的麻烦。

pages.en:
70

The three Nazi leaders now decided to smash the local
governments within the Reich. When the ministers of
Bavaria heard of this conspiracy they were loud in defy
ing Hitler to interfere with their legislative privileges.

Roehm told Hitler he could deal with the Munich
“bastards” with his SA army, and Hitler, though doubt-
ful, told him to go ahead. Roehm flew to Munich with
General Franz von Epp, and with less than fifty SA
men and one machine-gun they occupied all the govern-
ment buildings. Then he appointed Esser, anti Semitic
sex maniac, as Bavarian minister, and made Streicher
dictator of Franconia. Elsewhere the same sort of
thing happened; homosexuals and clowns placed in the
high positions. The old Prussian government quietly
disappeared, as did Hessen and Lubeck.

MASS MURDERS

Hitler was drunk with power, and determined upon
a really sensational coup. By this time he had become
more respectable, to all outward appearances. He wore
conventional dress; tailcoat and top hat; he was less
hysterical; he tried to improve his voice, making it less
pages.zh:
70

三位纳粹领导人现在决定粉碎帝国内部的地方政府。当巴伐利亚的部长们听到这一阴谋时，他们大声挑战希特勒，反对他干涉其立法特权。

罗姆告诉希特勒，他可以用他的冲锋队军队对付慕尼黑的“混蛋”，希特勒虽然怀疑，但还是让他 proceeded。罗姆与弗朗茨·冯·埃普将军（General Franz von Epp）飞往慕尼黑，带着不到五十名冲锋队员和一挺机枪，占领了所有政府大楼。随后，他任命反犹性狂躁者埃塞尔（Esser）为巴伐利亚部长，并任命施特莱歇尔（Streicher）为弗兰肯地区的独裁者。其他地方也发生了类似的事情；同性恋者和小丑被安置在高职位上。旧的普鲁士政府悄然消失，黑森（Hessen）和吕贝克（Lubeck）也是如此。

大规模谋杀

希特勒因权力而陶醉，决心进行一次真正轰动的政变。此时，他在外表上变得更加体面。他穿着传统服装；燕尾服和高顶礼帽；他不那么歇斯底里了；他试图改善自己的嗓音，使其不那么

pages.en:
71
strident. He took lessons in elocution. And he had a
change of heart in regard to the old officer caste he had
pretended to despise. The SA rank and file were so
disgusting to the country that he determined to do away
with these men. Also, Captain Roehm was becoming too
powerful for his taste. The pervert knew too much
about Hitler's wilder days. He determined to eliminate
him.

Now, whatever may be said of Roehm, and that is
plenty, he was always loyal to his Fuehrer, at least.
Roehm had first introduced Hitler to the powerful peo-
ple who advanced him. Roehm bought him his first news-
paper. Roehm, at constant risk to his life, provided
the early SA men with arms. Roehm alone had been
courageous during the beer-hall putsch, when the others
deserted. When Hitler, in jail, discharged him without
reason, Roehm went away without a word of reproach.

All of this meant nothing to Hitler. Roehm must
go.

He also decided to rid himself of Hugenberg. He
had brought Hugenberg into the cabinet as "Crisis
Minister", but he found the industrialist too wily, and
pages.zh:
71
刺耳。他上了发声课。而且他对曾经假装鄙视的旧军官阶层改变了态度。冲锋队的普通士兵令全国如此厌恶，以至于他决定除掉这些人。此外，罗姆上尉变得过于强大，不合他的心意。这个变态者知道太多关于希特勒狂野时期的事情。他决定除掉他。

现在，无论人们对罗姆有何评价，而且很多，但他至少始终忠于他的元首。罗姆最初将希特勒介绍给那些提拔他的有权势的人。罗姆为他购买了第一份报纸。罗姆冒着生命危险，为早期的冲锋队员提供武器。在啤酒馆暴动期间，当其他人逃跑时，只有罗姆表现出勇气。当希特勒在狱中毫无理由地解雇他时，罗姆一言不发地离开了，没有任何责备之词。

所有这些对希特勒来说毫无意义。罗姆必须走人。

他还决定摆脱胡根伯格（Hugenberg）。他曾将胡根伯格带入内阁担任“危机部长”，但他发现这位工业家过于狡猾，并且

pages.en:
72
over reluctant to give him taxes just as the Fuehrer
wished. Hugenberg, then, the one man who had done
more for Hitler than even Roehm, was rudely dismissed.

As for Roehm, he first wrote the homosexual an
affectionate letter, calling him "my dear friend and
fellow fighter." He said, "I feel a deep urge to thank
thee (du, the most loving and familiar term), my dearest
Ernst Roehm, for the immortal services thou hast
rendered to the National Socialist Movement and to the
German people. Wouldst thou come and see me?"

It was a positively love sick note. Roehm, un-
suspecting what lay behind all this love and tenderness,
went to Hitler's flat on June 5, 1934. Hitler kept him
there for five hours, pleading with the Captain to go on
leave and give the SA a holiday. Hindenburg, he ex-
plained, was objecting to the Storm Troopers being so
much more numerous than the regulars. But, he said,
the silly old fool was dying and would not last more
than two or three weeks more. And so, if Roehm would
get out of the way for a little while, they could disband
the SA for that time, after which they would incorporate
the Reichswehr into the SA and put Roehm in command.
pages.zh:
72
极不情愿按照元首的愿望向他缴税。因此，胡根伯格，这个甚至比罗姆为希特勒做得更多的人，被粗鲁地解职了。

至于罗姆，他首先给这位同性恋者写了一封充满深情的信，称他为“我亲爱的朋友和战友”。他说，“我感到一种强烈的冲动，要感谢你（du，最亲爱和熟悉的称呼），我最亲爱的恩斯特·罗姆，感谢你对国家社会主义运动和德国人民做出的不朽贡献。你能来见我吗？”

这绝对是一封相思病般的便条。罗姆没有察觉到这一切爱与温柔背后的真相，于1934年6月5日前往希特勒的公寓。希特勒将他留在那里五个小时，恳求这位上尉去休假，让冲锋队放假。他解释说，兴登堡反对冲锋队人数远超正规军。但是，他说，那个愚蠢的老傻瓜快要死了，活不过两三个星期了。因此，如果罗姆暂时退到一边，他们可以在此期间解散冲锋队，之后他们将把国防军并入冲锋队，并由罗姆指挥。

pages.en:
73

Röhm swallowed this pretty promise, though
Goering and Goebbels knew what was going to happen.
He left Hitler as affectionately as possible. His only
precaution after ordering the SA on a month's leave of
absence was to publish a short message for the benefit
of his enemies, among which he never for a moment
numbered Hitler

If the enemies of the SA lull themselves in hopes
the SA will not return from its leave or return
only in part, we shall allow them to enjoy this
short and pleasant hope. At the time and in the
form we think advisable these enemies will receive
their proper answer. The SA is and remains
Germany's destiny.

Quite at ease in his mind, Röhm took a plane to
Munich and then went to the Heinzelbauer Inn, in the
village of Wiessee, near Munich. Here he kept a suite
where he staged his orgies. Here staff members of the
SA enjoyed themselves, eating and drinking and play-
ing in their own peculiar ways among themselves. They
needed no women; their adjutants and orderlies were
attractive enough for them. It was all in the best
pages.zh:
73

罗姆吞下了这个美好的承诺，尽管戈林和戈培尔知道即将发生什么。他尽可能深情地离开了希特勒。他在命令冲锋队休假一个月后，唯一的预防措施是发布一条简短的信息，旨在给他的敌人看，而他从未片刻将希特勒列为敌人之一

如果冲锋队的敌人沉浸在冲锋队不会从假期中返回或仅部分返回的希望中，我们将让他们享受这短暂而愉快的希望。在我们认为合适的时间和形式下，这些敌人将得到他们应有的回答。冲锋队是且仍然是德国的命运。

罗姆心情轻松，乘飞机前往慕尼黑，然后去了位于慕尼黑附近维塞村（Wiessee）的海因策尔鲍尔旅馆（Heinzelbauer Inn）。他在那里保留了一套套房，用于举办他的狂欢活动。冲锋队的参谋人员在那里享乐，吃喝并以他们特有的方式互相玩耍。他们不需要女人；他们的副官和勤务兵对他们来说已经足够有吸引力了。这一切都是最好的

pages.en:
74

German tradition of the period. With him were
Edmund Heines, a convicted murderer on parole; Count
Spreti, police chief of Breslau and a famous Jew baiter;
Rochm's young chauffeur, usual "little friend" of
Heines, and several others, among them Rochm's
favourite of the time, a young poet.

A few weeks later the newspapers announced that
Hitler was driving to the Rhineland to attend the
wedding of one of his SA leaders. Through Goebbels,
he had the day before called a meeting of all chief staff
officers of the SA at Rochm's home that is, the Heinzel
bauer Inn. Rochm was flattered, and looked forward
to the meeting; he had not the slightest suspicion. Yet
Goebbels told Goering, "if Rochm escapes, it means he
will have jumped from an express train running a hun-
dred miles an hour, and without getting hurt!"

Hitler left Berlin with Goering on June 28. They
attended the wedding and then Goering went back to
Berlin, to be on hand for the forthcoming massacre.
Goebbels now joined the Dictator and they visited Herr
Krupp, inspected labour camps, made speeches about
pages.zh:
74

那个时期的德国传统。与他在一起的有
埃德蒙·海因斯（Edmund Heines），一名假释的已定罪谋杀犯；
斯普雷蒂伯爵（Count Spreti），布雷斯劳警察局长，著名的反犹煽动者；
罗姆的年轻司机，海因斯惯常的“小朋友”，
以及其他几人，其中包括罗姆当时的宠儿，一位年轻诗人。

几周后，报纸宣布希特勒正驱车前往莱茵兰，
参加其一名冲锋队领导人的婚礼。通过戈培尔，
他在前一天于罗姆的住所——即海因策尔鲍尔旅馆（Heinzelbauer Inn）——
召集了所有冲锋队主要参谋官员开会。罗姆受宠若惊，
期待着这次会议；他毫无怀疑。然而戈培尔告诉戈林：
“如果罗姆逃脱，那就意味着他从一列时速一百英里的特快列车上跳下，
而且毫发无伤！”

6月28日，希特勒与戈林离开柏林。他们参加了婚礼，
随后戈林返回柏林，以便为即将到来的大屠杀做好准备。
戈培尔此时加入了独裁者行列，他们拜访了克鲁伯先生（Herr Krupp），
视察了劳工营，并发表了关于

pages.en:
75

the lovely Rhine scenery, just as if he were not on an
errand of butchery.

At two o'clock in the morning of the 30th the two
men took a plane at Essen and flew to Munich. The
Nazis explained that this peculiar time was chosen for
the trip because Hitler had learned at Essen the details
of a plot by Roehm to call out the SA, seize the govern-
ment, disarm the Reichswehr, and assassinate Hitler
when he should arrive at the Inn. This, of course, is
a tissue of lies, bolstered up by Goebbels' sub-story of
Hitler's "unexampled determination during this
nocturnal flight into the unknown."

At the Munich airport Hitler was joined by a
cavalcade of cars, a detachment of SS men, an armoured
tanks, and all his personal bodyguard. At six A.M. just
before dawn in the Bavarian Alps, this cavalcade drew
up at the Heinzelbauer Inn.

Roehm and all his companions were asleep.

With a score of his bodyguard, and carrying only
his whip, Hitler with Goebbels raced into the hotel, up
the stairs to the bedroom. He told his guards to break
down Roehm's door, and dashed past to confront his
pages.zh:
75

美丽的莱茵河风光的演讲，仿佛他并非在执行一场屠宰任务。

30日凌晨两点，这两人在埃森乘飞机飞往慕尼黑。
纳粹分子解释说，选择这个特殊时间出行是因为希特勒在埃森获悉了
罗姆阴谋的细节：罗姆计划动员冲锋队，夺取政府权力，
解除国防军武装，并在希特勒抵达旅馆时将其刺杀。
当然，这是一堆谎言，由戈培尔编造的副故事加以支撑，
称希特勒在这次“夜间飞向未知”的过程中表现出“前所未有的决心”。

在慕尼黑机场，一队汽车、一支党卫队分队、
一辆装甲坦克以及他的所有贴身保镖加入了希特勒的行列。
清晨六点，就在巴伐利亚阿尔卑斯山黎明前夕，
这支车队抵达了海因策尔鲍尔旅馆。

罗姆及其所有同伴都在熟睡中。

希特勒带着大约二十名保镖，仅手持鞭子，
与戈培尔一起冲进酒店，跑上楼梯进入卧室。
他命令警卫撞开罗姆的房门，冲过去面对他的

pages.en:
56
oldest friend, upon whose shoulders he had risen to
power a bewildered, fat and sloppy creature in
pajamas.

Hitler had worked himself into one of his furies.
He reviled Roehm for the "plot"; the words poured
forth, a torrent of obscenity. Surrounded by his
guards, the noble Fuehrer flogged the captain, hitting
him over and over in the face with his whip. He
screamed at him that he would allow Roehm to execute
himself, and then strode from the room.

In the room opposite slept Heines with a youth, the
chauffeur; they were murdered in their bed. Down-
stairs, Hitler encountered Spreti; he thrashed him in
the face until the chief of police collapsed Others in
the party who were not shot were bundled with Roehm
into cars and take to Munich. On the way the cavalcade
intercepted some hundred other SA leaders who had
been summoned to the Inn; they were captured and
put under arrest.

The blood purge began. Goering was given a free
hand. For three days murder ran rampant; twelve hun-
pages.zh:
56
老朋友，正是踩着这位朋友的肩膀他才登上权力之巅——
一个穿着睡衣、困惑、肥胖且邋遢的生物。

希特勒让自己陷入狂怒之中。
他因“阴谋”一事辱骂罗姆；污言秽语如洪流般涌出。
在警卫的包围下，这位高贵的元首鞭打这位队长，
用鞭子一次又一次地抽打他的脸。
他对着罗姆尖叫，说允许罗姆自杀，然后大步走出房间。

在对面的房间里，海因斯与那名青年司机同睡；
他们在床上被杀害。在楼下，希特勒遇到了斯普雷蒂；
他猛击斯普雷蒂的脸部，直到这位警察局长倒地。
随行人员中未被枪杀的其他人与罗姆一起被塞进汽车，
带往慕尼黑。途中，车队拦截了约一百名其他被召至旅馆的
冲锋队领导人；他们被捕获并逮捕。

血腥清洗开始了。戈林被赋予全权。
三天内，谋杀肆虐；一千二百

pages.en:
77

dred were slain. Roehm, in the execution yard, three times
refused to kill himself, demanding that Hitler murder
him personally. The firing squad finally did the job,
and Roehm fell cursing his leader.

General Schleicher and his elderly wife, almost all
the SA commanders, the Munich chief of police Schneid-
huber, Karl Ernst, who helped Hitler fire the Reichstag,
Strasser who helped in the Munich putsch--Hitler was
god father to his two sons--and scores of others, includ-
ing everybody disliked by Goering and Goebbels, the
heavenly twins, were shot in cold blood.

Hitler, when he heard of the butchery, burst into
tears and was hysterical for three hours. Two weeks
later he summoned the dummy Reichstag to explain:
"Mutiny has been broken by iron laws which cannot be
changed. In that terrible hour. . . I was responsible
for the fate of the German people, and . . . the supreme
court of justice was embodied in me."

Hitler added a promise to investigate the murders
of men and women who had not the slightest connection
with the SA and that was the last that was done
about it.
pages.zh:
77

人被杀害。罗姆在行刑场上三次拒绝自杀，
要求希特勒亲自杀害他。行刑队最终执行了任务，
罗姆倒在地上，诅咒着他的领袖。

施莱谢尔将军（General Schleicher）及其年迈的妻子、
几乎所有的冲锋队指挥官、慕尼黑警察局长施奈德胡贝尔（Schneidhuber）、
协助希特勒焚烧国会大厦的卡尔·恩斯特（Karl Ernst）、
协助慕尼黑暴动的斯特拉瑟（Strasser）——希特勒是他两个儿子的教父——
以及数十名其他人，包括所有被戈林和戈培尔这对“天堂双生子”所厌恶的人，
都被冷血枪杀。

希特勒听到大屠杀的消息后，泪流满面，
歇斯底里了三个小时。两周后，他召集傀儡国会进行解释：
“叛乱已被不可更改的铁律粉碎。在那可怕的时刻……
我对德国人民的命运负责，而且……最高司法法庭体现于我身。”

希特勒补充承诺调查那些与冲锋队毫无关系的男女被谋杀案，
但这便是此事的最后下文。

pages.en:
78

He then dissolved the SA, incorporating thousands
of its men in the Reichswehr. He was safer than ever.

THE CONCENTRATION CAMPS

The "blood bath" of June 30, 1934, marked the
beginning of the open reign of terror, but even in
Germany, oppressed with poverty and uncertainty and
tyranny, there were many people who still dared to
protest, and to protest openly. Not only Jews, but
others mostly from the professional classes professors,
doctors, lawyers etc. came out flatly against the
torture of innocent Jews and the murders of SA leaders,
government officials, and anybody else who displeased
or frightened the head maniac, Hitler. He quickly saw
the danger and organized the Gestapo, the dread secret
police, under Goering and Heinrich Himmler.

Himmler is at the moment a prized servant of
Hitler, because of his lust for cruelty and evident lack
of ambition save to serve his master monster. He has
a real passion for brutality, so they put him at the head
of the concentration camps. These camps were to re-
ceive people who had not been tried and their length of
pages.zh:
78

随后他解散了冲锋队，将其数千名成员并入国防军。
他比以往任何时候都更安全。

集中营

1934年6月30日的“血浴”标志着公开恐怖统治的开始，
但即使在德国，尽管受到贫困、不确定性和暴政的压迫，
仍有许多人敢于抗议，并且是公开抗议。
不仅是犹太人，还有其他人，大多来自专业阶层——教授、
医生、律师等——坚决反对对无辜犹太人的折磨以及对
冲锋队领导人、政府官员和任何令头号疯子希特勒不悦或恐惧之人的谋杀。
他迅速看到了危险，并在戈林和海因里希·希姆莱的组织下建立了盖世太保，
即令人畏惧的秘密警察。

希姆莱此刻是希特勒珍视的仆人，因为他渴望残忍，
且显然除了服务于其主人怪物外别无野心。
他对残暴有着真正的热情，因此让他负责集中营。
这些营地将接收未经审判的人，他们的停留期限

pages.en:
79

stay was indefinite Their purpose was to break the
morale of the opposition, and they were well suited to
this end.

Himmler set to work with relish. For the camp
guards he selected men with tastes similar to his own,
as far as possible; most of them were the cruelest and
most bestial of the former SA gangsters, well hardened
and lustful for blood. He then seized on seventy
thousand persons, half of them Jews, and threw them
into twenty new concentration camps in Bavaria,
Saxony, Baden, the Rhineland, Prussia, Westphalia,
and Thuringia. They were surrounded with high-
voltage wires so that escape was impossible. The
barracks were rude and completely comfortless; the
only care was taken in preparing facilities for torture
.... All of this, in case you have forgotten, is hap-
pening NOW, in our own world, in our own civilization,
and on an immense scale. .....

Today there are 73 camps with at least 450,000
prisoners, and less than 25% of them are Jews, for the
Jews have been kicked out of Germany and Austria and
the other nations which Hitler has grabbed. Nobody
pages.zh:
79

是不确定的。其目的是摧毁反对派的士气，
而它们非常适合达到这一目的。

希姆莱兴致勃勃地开始工作。对于营地警卫，
他尽可能挑选与其品味相似的人；
其中大多数是前冲锋队暴徒中最残忍、最兽性的人，
 hardened （ hardened 此处指变得冷酷无情/ hardened criminals 惯犯之意，结合语境译为 hardened ）且嗜血。
随后他抓捕了七万人，其中一半是犹太人，
并将他们投入巴伐利亚、萨克森、巴登、莱茵兰、普鲁士、
威斯特法伦和图林根的新建二十个集中营中。
营地周围环绕着高压电线，使得逃跑成为不可能。
营房简陋且完全不适人居；唯一的用心在于准备酷刑设施……
如果你忘记了，这一切都发生在此时此刻，
在我们自己的世界，在我们自己的文明中，
而且规模巨大。……

如今有73个营地，囚犯至少45万人，
其中犹太人不到25%，因为犹太人已被赶出德国、奥地利
以及希特勒攫取的其他国家。没有人

pages.en:
so
knows how many people have died in camp, but news-
papermen from abroad once calculated Hitler's murders
as at the very least one hundred and twenty-five thou-
sand, which is a pretty good record for mere corporal.
There has never been such a slaughter in peace-time,
within man's memory.

Prisoners usually wonder why they are imprisoned,
since most of them are ignorant and innocent of their
supposed crimes. To ask such a question is to be
smashed in the face with a guard's fist After that the
punishment does not wait for more provocation, and the
method is more refined. . . . .

Those Jews who have got away are usually silent as
to what goes on in the hell from which they have
escaped. This is because they have been warned that
exposure will call down a lot more of the same on their

Upon arrival, the prisoner's head is shaved and he
is assigned a sleeping place, a pile of straw in some hut
corner if he is lucky. For toilets they use ditches.
Usually there is one pump for 600 prisoners. Anybody
attempting to open a window or to get a breath of air,
after trying to sleep in a room with a hundred filthy,
sweating other prisoners is shot or beaten. A lot of
new prisoners are usually killed in this way, because
they don't know. "Herr X was shot while attempting
to escape", says the report. Actual escape is an im-
possibility; if the prisoner, or rather the protected man
attempts it he must first face Storm Troopers with
rubber truncheons, then scale high walls topped with
high-voltage cables, and then sneak past more Storm
Troopers with machine guns. And then he must
penetrate an impenetrable forest of barbed wire.
A better aid to the Nazi program is the disease
which of course carries off thousands of people dwelling
under these filthy conditions. Herr Himmler was once
asked by journalists why so many deaths were reported
from Dachau; he replied quite truthfully, "Well, gentle-

到达时，囚犯的头部被剃光，并被分配一个睡觉的地方，

厕所使用的是沟渠。通常600名囚犯共用一个水泵。
任何试图打开窗户或在挤满一百名肮脏、

实际逃跑是不可能的；如果囚犯，或者更确切地说是“受保护的人”
试图逃跑，他必须首先面对手持橡胶警棍的突击队员，

对纳粹计划更有利的辅助因素是疾病，

He recently promoted one of his Storm Trooper
guards because the man invented the system of forcing
"unreformable" prisoners to clean out the latrines with

Other corrective measures are to make a prisoner
stand with upraised arms for hours on end. When at
last he begs permission to sit down, the guard beats
him down with a rubber truncheon until he is indeed
at rest. Other prisoners are thrown into dungheaps
and forced to stay there for hours.

These are minor tortures, though they often lead
to suicide. People Hitler really dislikes are emasculat
ed; the only "remains" sent their families for burial
are their sexual organs.

Once every fortnight a letter is allowed to be sent
out, heavily censored of course; if an unwary prisoner
asks permission to write more often he is granted it,
but as he starts to write the guard smashes and fractures
his fingers with a truncheon.

One of Hitler’s strongest supporters and closest
companions during his early struggles in Munich was
Kurt Ludecke. He knew a lot about Hitler. It was his
mission to spread Nazi propaganda in America; by the
time he returned for funds, Hitler was Chancellor.
Ludecke was immediately thrown into the Brandenburg
concentration camp.

RELIGIOUS PERSECUTION

Although Hitler's chief attacks have been against
Jewry, he has also unleashed his forces of insane hatred
and brutality against the Catholics, the Protestants—
anybody, in fact, who might oppose him. Pastors have
been thrown into the dread camps; the best known is
Niemoller, for whom Lord Cecil interceded. Hitler,
author of "Mein Kampf", is jealous of the Bible, and
anybody who prefers the older book enrages him.

MONEY SMUGGLING

Germany, on the brink of bankruptcy in spite of
fantastic inflation and rigid control of her marks, not
to mention barter schemes, has made death the penalty
for smuggling money out of the country. It is im-
possible to check it, however. Many tricks are used, and
the smugglers cannot be frightened, even though

宗教迫害

虽然希特勒的主要攻击目标是犹太人，
但他也释放了其疯狂仇恨和暴力的力量来对付天主教徒、新教徒——
事实上，任何可能反对他的人。牧师被投入可怕的营地；
最著名的是尼莫勒（Niemoller），塞西尔勋爵（Lord Cecil）曾为其求情。
《我的奋斗》的作者希特勒嫉妒《圣经》，
任何偏爱这本古老书籍的人都会激怒他。

资金走私

德国处于破产边缘，尽管有惊人的通货膨胀和对马克的严格控制，
更不用说易货计划，已将走私资金出境定为死罪。
然而，这是无法遏制的。人们使用许多伎俩，
走私者无法被吓倒，即使

bing more territory does not help the situation, and the

the Jews did not provide the panacea to all ills promised
by Hitler.

NOVEMBER POGROMS

Herschel Grynszpan was the Jewish son of a Polish
tailor of Hanover, whose business had been “Arianized”
and who had been ordered back to Poland by the gov-
ernment. His brother had been murdered by Nazis.

Grynszpan, seventeen years old, made his way at
last to Paris with a forged passport. The Paris police
ordered him back to Germany; the German Embassy
refused him a visa. On top of this he had received
word that his father and mother were dying of cold
and hunger at the German-Polish frontier. He went
nearly insane with grief and fury.

His uncle, who had sheltered him in Paris, gave him
fifty francs with which to flee into the country. He
bought a revolver instead. Then he went back to the

十一月大迫害

赫舍尔·格林斯潘（Herschel Grynszpan）是汉诺威一名波兰犹太裁缝的儿子，其父亲的生意已被“雅利安化”，且被政府勒令返回波兰。他的兄弟已被纳粹分子杀害。

时年十七岁的格林斯潘持伪造护照最终抵达巴黎。巴黎警方命令他返回德国；德国大使馆则拒绝向他发放签证。加之他又收到消息，称其父母在德波边境因寒冷和饥饿而垂死。悲痛与愤怒使他几近疯狂。

他在巴黎的叔叔收留了他，并给了他五十法郎让他逃往乡下。但他却用这笔钱买了一支左轮手枪。随后他回到

German Embassy and asked to see some minor official
about the business. He was directed to the Third
Secretary, Herr Vom Rath. His brain snapped, and
he fired five bullets, all but two going wild. But the
two killed Vom Rath within a few hours. This was
November 7, 1938.

Goebbels pounced on this affair and the terror in
Germany began. "Kill the Jews!" "Revenge for
Vom Rath!" screamed the papers and posters. The
Storm Troopers with such civilians as wished to began
the slaughter; the police were ordered not to interfere. All
the remaining Jewish stores in Germany were sacked.
Synagogues were burned. The streets were filled with

and children were not spared. The Storm Troopers
had more fun in the concentration camps, where the
Jews could be herded together and shot all at once
less exciting, of course, but much more bloody. At the
Buchenwald camp 200 Jews were lined up and simply
machine-gunned: two guns swept their ranks till they
were all dead. Twenty Jews had been killed the night
before, before Grynszpan had killed the secretary, and

戈培尔抓住这一事件，德国的恐怖统治随之开始。“杀死犹太人！”“为冯·拉特报仇！”报纸和海报上如此嘶吼。冲锋队以及那些愿意参与的平民开始了屠杀；警察奉命不得干涉。德国境内所有剩余的犹太商店均遭洗劫。犹太会堂被焚毁。街道上挤满了逃亡的犹太人，他们遭到殴打或枪击。婴儿和儿童也未能幸免。冲锋队在集中营里更是乐在其中，在那里犹太人可以被驱赶在一起一次性射杀：当然，这没那么刺激，但血腥得多。在布痕瓦尔德（Buchenwald）集中营，200名犹太人被排成一列，直接遭到机枪扫射：两挺机枪扫过队列，直至所有人死亡。在格林斯潘刺杀秘书的前一晚，已有二十名犹太人被杀，其他

EXPIATION OF THE JEWS

On November 12th, Goering promulgated a decree
which fined Jews four hundred million dollars as a
"stern defensive measure of expiation." All Jewish
bank accounts, warehouse stock, factory equipment,
etc., was confiscated to make certain the fine was paid.

Throughout Germany Protestant churches were
filled with thousands who uttered prayers for the suffer

“在纳粹党管理下，德国对法律怀有最深刻的尊重，”戈培尔在一条仍血流成河的街道上发表演讲时高呼，“过去二十小时的骚乱构成了德国人民正当且可理解的愤慨！”

这或许是文明唯一的希望之光，因为这一次没有人欢呼回应他。即使是最顽固的暴徒也感到满足后的惊恐。

犹太人的赎罪

11月12日，戈林颁布了一项法令，作为“严厉的赎罪防御措施”，对犹太人罚款四亿美元。所有犹太人的银行账户、仓库库存、工厂设备等均被没收，以确保罚款得以支付。

在整个德国，新教教堂里挤满了成千上万为受苦者

ers. Even the "Aryans" who had supported Hitler now
turned against him, after the pogrom.

When Hitler learned the full extent of the carnage
he wept, just as he had wept after the 1934 "blood
bath". During the time of riot he had been listening
to a string quartet, with Foreign Minister Von Ribben-
trop. His first reaction now was to break all the string
ed instruments and to boot Von Ribbentrop from his
drawing room. Von Ribbentrop later told one of his
family:

"His expression was that of a man gone completely
mad. He may have been trying to persuade me that
he hadn't known anything of what was going to happen,
but I fully believed that after I left him weeping with
rage he would commit suicide."

Unfortunately he didn't. But anyway he wouldn't
make the funeral oration at Vom Rath's obsequies.

Goering announced that foreign Jews would not be
permitted to pay the enormous fine; the Government
would collect, he said, from the German Jews. Im-
mediately Jews in England and France, with the aid of

祈祷的人。甚至那些曾支持希特勒的“雅利安人”，在大迫害之后也转而反对他。

当希特勒得知屠杀的全部规模时，他哭了，就像他在1934年“血浴”之后哭泣一样。在骚乱期间，他一直与外交部长冯·里宾特洛甫（Von Ribbentrop）一起听弦乐四重奏演奏。他现在的第一个反应是砸碎所有的弦乐器，并将冯·里宾特洛甫踢出他的客厅。冯·里宾特洛甫后来告诉他的一个家人：

“他的表情就像一个完全疯掉的人。他可能试图让我相信他对即将发生的事情一无所知，但我完全相信，在我离开后，当他因愤怒而哭泣时，他会自杀。”

不幸的是，他没有自杀。但无论如何，他不会在冯·拉特的葬礼上发表悼词。

戈林宣布，不允许外国犹太人支付这笔巨额罚款；他说，政府将从德国犹太人那里收取。立即地，英国和法国的犹太人在非犹太朋友的帮助下，一夜之间筹集了数百万美元以援助犹太人；然而，这笔钱被政府挪用，汇款人至今仍未得知其下落。

In some respects this pogrom, the largest yet, has
acted as a boomerang against the government, for they
were faced with the necessity of housing thousands of
people, and of hospitalizing thousands more. The
dying and injured could not be left in the streets with-
out further injuring the party's reputation; even they
realized the danger of too much brutality. For once
their own public was completely appalled. It was too
much.

One relatively minor torture, in Vienna, for ex-
ample, disgusted many people who turned from their
former fidelity to the party. This was the practise of
deliberately breaking the noses of Jews two thousand
of them!

Hundreds of Jews lay in the Vienna streets moan-
ing, begging to be put out of their misery. Nazis mere-
ly laughed at them, or kicked them in the head or
stomach.

在某些方面，这场迄今为止规模最大的大迫害像回旋镖一样反噬了政府，因为他们面临着安置数千人和收容数千伤员的必要性。死者和伤者不能被弃置街头，以免进一步损害党的声誉；就连他们也意识到了过度残暴的危险。他们的公众这一次彻底震惊了。这太过分了。

例如，在维也纳，一种相对轻微的酷刑让许多曾经忠于党派的人感到厌恶并转身离去。这种做法是故意打断犹太人的鼻子——多达两千人！

数百名犹太人躺在维也纳的街道上呻吟，乞求结束他们的痛苦。纳粹分子只是嘲笑他们，或者踢他们的头部或腹部。

Many more cases of insanity, also, resulted twelve

ATROCITY CASES

It would be necessary to fill a hundred books if we
were to review all the cases of atrocities committed by
Hitler and his henchmen. Let us take a typical story
then, as a sample. Ludwig Schmidt (the name is
fictitious to protect those of his family who still remain
within reach of the Nazis) was a Berlin shopkeeper, a
veteran of the German Imperial Army with four years
of service in the trenches during the World War. He
was one of the 10,000 non-aryans rounded up in Berlin
early in November, 1938, and sent to Buchenwald con-
centration camp, six miles from Weimar, the town of
Goethe and the late German Constitution. After the Vom
Rath assassination in Paris, when the terrorist gangs
began their "round up", even the very poorest houses
were sacked and the people driven into the streets.
Children were ousted from orphanages; sick people
trundled from hospitals, which were set afire. Jewish
mothers went begging in the streets for food, for shop-
pages.zh:
此外，还导致了更多的精神失常病例，自11月以来新增一万两千例。

暴行案例

如果要回顾希特勒及其爪牙犯下的所有暴行案例，需要写满一百本书。因此，让我们选取一个典型故事作为样本。路德维希·施密特（Ludwig Schmidt）（此名为虚构，以保护仍处在纳粹势力范围内的其家人）是一名柏林店主，也是德意志帝国陆军的老兵，在世界大战期间曾在战壕服役四年。他是19歌8年11月初在柏林被捕的一万名非雅利安人之一，并被送往位于魏玛（Goethe之城及前德国宪法所在地）六英里外的布痕瓦尔德集中营。巴黎发生冯·拉特刺杀案后，当恐怖团伙开始“围捕”时，即使是最贫穷的房屋也遭到洗劫，人们被驱赶到街上。儿童被赶出孤儿院；病人被从医院推出来，医院也被纵火焚烧。犹太母亲在街上乞讨食物，因为店

pages.en:
91

keepers were not allowed to sell food to Jews and the
children were starving

A number of people flocked to Herr Schmidt's
house, mistakenly believing that his war record would
protect it. Earlier in the evening his shop had been
looted and burnt, but they still hoped for his house.
They were mistaken. His house was broken into,
ruined, looted and smashed. He was torn from his
family and thrown into a truck and driven away to the
camp, on the night of November 10.

Assigned to a special Jew company, he was put into
a wooden hut accommodating several hundred men, in-
cluding many of his acquaintances, some over 70 and
many over 60 years old; friends of his father's and
many people who had once been influential. The camp
was, of course, surrounded as usual with high-voltage
barbed wire, armed guards, etc. There were several
machine-gun towers from which the guards were in the
playful habit of taking pot-shots at people for nothing
in particular.

The Jews were there for a special reason, to put the

主不被允许向犹太人出售食物，孩子们正在挨饿

许多人涌向施密特先生的家，错误地认为他的战争履历能保护这里。当天早些时候，他的店铺已被抢劫并烧毁，但他们仍对他的住所抱有希望。他们错了。他的房子被闯入、毁坏、抢劫和打砸。他在11月10日晚被从家人身边撕扯开来，扔进一辆卡车，运往集中营。

他被编入一个专门的犹太人连队，住进一间容纳数百人的木屋，其中包括许多他的熟人，有些超过70岁，许多超过60岁；有他父亲的朋友，也有许多曾经有权势的人。当然，营地像往常一样被高压铁丝网、武装警卫等包围。还有几座机枪塔，守卫们习惯性地从中随意向人们开枪取乐。

犹太人在那里有一个特殊原因，即让

4
nearly time for roll call. He was publicly stripped and
horsewhipped five lashes a day for four days. At an
other time he was forced to stand up for hours, tied to
a tree. The prisoners most feared solitary confinement
in the dark in a small cell for 23 hours a day. All
severe breaches of discipline were punishable by death.
A prisoner who attempted to escape, killing his guard,
was strung up on a special gallows and left three days
for all prisoners to see. But Herr Schmidt, as a result
of letter writing finally arranged to emigrate his entire
family and was released in January. As he left a
Storm Trooper kicked him in the head with a steel-
pointed boot. The hair will probably grow again.
Schmidt is lucky to be alive at all, at his age.

MURDER BY SUICIDE

“A man living in a bungalow on the Honer Moor
has committed suicide by a terrible method. He went
into the toolhouse built on to his bungalow where there
was a barrel of tar; after taking off some of his clothes
he smeared himself with tar and set fire to the barrel.

点名时间临近。他被公开剥光衣服，每天遭受马鞭抽打五下，持续四天。另一次，他被绑在树上站立数小时。囚犯们最害怕的是每天23小时被单独关押在黑暗的小牢房里。所有严重违反纪律的行为均可判处死刑。一名试图逃跑并杀死守卫的囚犯被吊在一个特殊的绞刑架上，示众三天。但施密特先生通过写信，最终安排全家移民，并于一月获释。在他离开时，一名冲锋队员用带钢头的靴子踢了他的头。头发大概还会长出来。施密特在这个年纪还能活着，已是幸运。

“杜塞尔多夫的共产党领导人巴斯勒（Bassler），已躲避逮捕相当长一段时间，今早被辅助警察 locate。在押送途中，被捕者试图逃跑。尽管多次警告他停下，但他拒不听从，警官遂使用武器。”（实际上，他是穿着睡衣被从家里拖出来并枪杀的）

escape. Frau Bloch, 70, Berlin, suicide. Unidentified

(From Manchester Guardian) "My German cousin
said there was a feeling of disaster over the whole town
where she lives. Rich Aryans, men and women, were
doing what they could, going from Jewish house to
house with food and clothing. She says that Aryans,
after the pogrom, were seen openly weeping in the
streets."

Also from the Guardian: "My reception by the
SA men in Vienna. . . We were forced with hundreds
of other Jews in a yard to crawl on all fours in the
mud. We were stood facing one another in pairs and
forced to strike each other in the face--anyone who
didn't strike hard enough had a lesson from an SA man
on his own face. All this was accompanied by the
brutal shouting of the SA men and the beaten men's
cries of pain. Then there was drill under SA
orders, consisting of unending stretching and knee
bending, although among the prisoners there were
many old people. Those who could not keep it up
were beaten on the head. For good measure then we
pages.zh:
96

逃跑时被枪杀。布洛赫夫人（Frau Bloch），70岁，柏林，自杀。柏林，身份不明的社会党人，在医院死于不明原因。”

（摘自《曼彻斯特卫报》）“我在德国的表妹说，她居住的整个城镇弥漫着灾难感。富有的雅利安人，无论男女，都在尽其所能，带着食物和衣物逐户拜访犹太人家庭。她说，大迫害之后，人们看到雅利安人在街头公然哭泣。”

同样来自《卫报》：“我在维也纳受到冲锋队成员的‘接待’……我们与其他数百名犹太人一起被迫在院子里四肢着地在泥地里爬行。我们两人一组面对面站立，被迫互相扇耳光——任何下手不够重的人都会从冲锋队员那里亲自‘受教’。这一切伴随着冲锋队员残忍的叫喊声和被殴打者的痛苦哭喊声。随后是在冲锋队命令下的操练，包括无休止的伸展运动和屈膝运动，尽管囚犯中有许多老人。那些坚持不下来的人会被击打头部。为了‘加餐’，我们

pages.en:
97

were beaten with the leather belts of the SA. Because
I didn't hit man opposite me hard enough in the face
- he was a close friend of mine - I received a black eye.
Then we had to lie down and get up again for two hours
without stopping, in the course of which dozens of men
and women collapsed and were revived by a pail of
dirty water in their faces. . ."

Another: "Elderly men and women were forced
to crawl along the streets on their stomachs, wearing
nothing (in the case of the men) but their pants.
Refined Jewish women were forced to clean the latrines
of the SA and SS."

AN ARYAN'S STORY

(This story is authentic)

Until I was 42 I was an average middle class
Hamburg citizen with a happy family, a pleasant home,
and a good business which had been built up through
generations.

I am German, all my ancestors were of pure German
blood, many of my forefathers died fighting for the
pages.zh:
97

还被用冲锋队的皮带殴打。因为我打对面那个人脸打得不够重——他是我的密友——我被打成了黑眼圈。然后我们不得不连续两个小时不停地躺下再起身，在此期间，数十名男女昏倒，并被泼在脸上的一桶脏水唤醒……”

另一则报道：“老年男女被迫仅穿内裤（男性）趴在街上爬行。受过良好教育的犹太妇女被迫清洗冲锋队和党卫军的厕所。”

一个雅利安人的故事

（这个故事是真实的）

直到42岁，我一直是一个普通的汉堡中产阶级市民，拥有幸福的家庭、舒适的住所，以及一份经过几代人积累的良好事业。

我是德国人，我的祖先都是纯种德国血统，我的许多先辈在为

pages.en:
98

fatherland. I am Protestant. I am Aryan. I am
law abiding. My children were raised to believe in
God, obey the law, and love our Germany.

In my employ was a lazy and inefficient young man.
I discharged him. A couple of days later the leader of
the Nazi cell to which he belonged came and wanted
him re-instated. I refused, naturally.

A few days later two uniformed youths entered my
store and started a collection. It was a common
occurrence. With heel-clicking and crying of 'Heil,
Hitler!' they made the rounds. I gave them some small
change, as did my clerks and customers; finally they
stationed themselves at either side of the entrance
where they could accost each newcomer. There was
nothing I could do: I shrugged my shoulders.

An old lady I had known for years started to enter.
She refused to contribute her meager change to the
Nazi striplings. They kept pestering her, she became
excited, and a crowd collected. I rushed over and told
the boys, "Take it easy. You've had your share; now
leave my customers alone."
pages.zh:
98

祖国。我是新教徒。我是雅利安人。我
遵纪守法。我的孩子们从小被教导要信仰
上帝，遵守法律，并热爱我们的德意志。

我雇用过一个懒惰且无能的年轻人。
我解雇了他。几天后，他所属的纳粹小组
的头目前来，要求让他复职。我自然拒绝
了。

几天后，两名身穿制服的年轻人走进我
的商店，开始募捐。这是常见的情形。他
们一边跺脚行礼，一边高呼“希特勒万
岁！”，四处走动。我和店员及顾客一样，
给了他们一些零钱；最后，他们守在入口
两侧，以便拦截每一位新进来的顾客。我
无能为力：只好耸耸肩。

一位我认识多年的老妇人正要进来。她
拒绝向那些纳粹毛头小子捐献微薄的零
钱。他们不断纠缠她，她变得激动起来，
人群也聚集了起来。我冲过去对那几个年
轻人说：“放轻松点。你们已经拿够了；现
在别打扰我的顾客。”

pages.en:
99

One of the boys turned on me. "You should be
ashamed of yourself! taking sides with this old hag
against the Nazi party." I was furious, and said,

"Listen, my boy; I was in the war when you were
wearing diapers. Now beat it!"

The crowd had increased, and several uniformed
Storm Troopers arrived. The leader had been janitor
in our business building until the new regime gave him
rank and uniform. He shoved the crowd aside and
investigated.

"This is outrageous!" he shouted. "This old cow
has insulted Der Fuehrer and you sided with her.
You'll be sorry for this!"

I was dumbfounded. This former janitor had
been a decent man for years; taken his Christmas bonus
like the others, and his children wore my boys' out-
grown clothing. Once I had arranged a little loan for
him which he had paid back promptly and to the
cent. . . . . Well, I gave up.

That night I took my wife to a movie, to relax and
forget. I had not told her of the incident. When we

其中一个年轻人转而对付我。“你应该
感到羞耻！竟然站在一个老巫婆一边，对
抗纳粹党。”我勃然大怒，说道：

“听着，小子；当你还穿尿布的时候，我
就已经在打仗了。现在滚开！”

人群越来越多，几名身穿制服的冲锋队
员赶到了。那个头目直到新政权授予他军
衔和制服之前，一直是我们商业大楼的门
卫。他推开人群，进行调查。

“这太 outrageous（原文不清/过分）了！”他吼道。“这个老母牛
侮辱了元首，而你竟然站在她那边。你会
为此后悔的！”

我目瞪口呆。这位前门卫多年来一直是
个体面人；像其他人一样领取圣诞奖金，
他的孩子们还穿我儿子们淘汰下来的衣
服。有一次我还为他安排了一笔小额贷款，
他迅速且分文不少地还清了……好吧，我
放弃了。

那天晚上，我带妻子去看电影，以放松
心情并忘却此事。我没有告诉她这起事
件。当我们

pages.en:
100
left the theatre I heard my name called; I turned and
saw my older son. He whispered, "Papa . . . you
can't go home. You've got to leave town you've got to
hide!" Storm Troopers and police were waiting at
the house, he said. My wife pleaded with me when I
told her to take Otto and go to her sister's, but I in-
sisted, "I have done nothing!" Hurriedly I bundled
wife and son in a cab and sent them on their way.
Then I got into another cab and started home.

In my own house, the hall was crowded with uni-
forms Storm Troopers, special officers in black,
policemen. The leader snarled, "You're under arrest!"
I was taken to the district office, before the district
leader, and stood before his desk like a criminal while
the Storm Trooper made his report. I demanded to
know on what grounds I had been brought there. The
man behind the desk glared at me. "So you want to
know that, really? . . ."

He got up slowly, then suddenly grabbed a riding
whip that lay on the desk and slashed me in the face.

They dragged me from the room. I struggled and
was kicked with heavy boots. Heels cracked against

离开剧院时，我听到有人叫我的名字；我
转过身，看到了我的大儿子。他低声说：
“爸爸……你不能回家。你必须离开这个
城镇，你必须躲起来！”他说，冲锋队员和
警察正在家里等候。当我告诉妻子带着奥
托（Otto）去她姐姐家时，她向我哀求，但
我坚持说：“我什么也没做！”我匆忙将妻
子和儿子塞进一辆出租车，送他们离开。
然后我坐上另一辆出租车，开始回家。

在我自己家里，大厅里挤满了身穿制服
的冲锋队员、黑衣特别警官和警察。那个
头目咆哮道：“你被捕了！”我被带到区办
公室，面对区头目，像罪犯一样站在他的
办公桌前，而那名冲锋队员则在作报告。
我要求知道我被带到这里的原因。办公桌
后的那个人怒视着我。“所以你真的想知
道？……”

他慢慢站起来，突然抓起桌上放着的一
根马鞭，抽打在我的脸上。

pages.en:
101

my knee caps. I was trampled in the back, and beaten
with fists. I was hauled into the cellar and forced to
strip; then grabbed and placed on a table. Again I
was beaten with riding whips and black-jacks.

A man leaned against the cellar wall, quietly suck-
ing an empty pipe, just looking on.

Finally they stopped beating me and ordered me
to get up. I could hardly stand. My very heart felt
bruised and swollen.

“Now stand up straight, will you!” I tried to
obey.

“Now raise your right arm and say Heil Hitler!”

I obeyed. They made me repeat, again and again,
until my arm felt heavy as lead. At last they shoved
me into a filthy cell.

I was kept there for three days, then brought
before several officials and confronted with the young
man I had dismissed for laziness. He now wore the
uniform of a Storm Trooper. His testimony stunned
me.
pages.zh:
101

他们把我拖出房间。我挣扎着，被穿着
重靴的脚踢踹。鞋跟猛烈撞击

我的膝盖骨。我的背部遭到践踏，并被拳
头殴打。我被拖进地下室，被迫脱光衣服；
随后被抓住并按在桌子上。再次遭到马鞭
和指节铜套（black-jacks）的殴打。

一个人靠在地下室的墙上，静静地吸着
一只空烟斗，只是在一旁观看。

最后他们停止殴打我，命令我站起来。
我几乎站不稳。我的心感觉像是受了淤伤
并肿胀起来。

“现在站直了，听见没有！”我试图照
做。

“现在举起你的右臂，说‘希特勒万岁’！”

我照做了。他们让我一遍又一遍地重复，
直到我的手臂感觉像铅一样沉重。最后他
们把我推进一间肮脏的牢房。

我被关在那里三天，然后被带到几名官
员面前，并与我之前因懒惰而解雇的那个
年轻人对质。他现在穿着冲锋队的制服。
他的证词令我震惊。

pages.en:
102

According to him I was a traitor to my Fatherland,
a hinderer to the Nazi cause, an anarchist, and a con
spirator. I favored Jewish employees and abused
Aryan salesgirls.

I wasn't given a chance to reply, but was ordered
back to the cell. As yet I had no word from my family.
I could hear the screams and shrieks of other victims:
the sounds of whips lashing, the thud of bodies slumping
to the floor. I could heard the laughter and cursing of
the Nazi guards.

Days later I was taken out, lined up with half a
dozen others, handcuffed together and led to a truck.
Our destination was Fuelsbuettel. On our arrival we
were lined up, face to the wall, and forced to stand at
attention for three hours!

When we fell the guards jumped at us, kicking us
where we had been bruised before. An old gentleman
with irongrey hair next to me couldn't stand it; he
went down, with a groan.

The guard, two of them, seized him and banged
his head on the floor. His false teeth fell out and one
pages.zh:
102

据他说，我是祖国的叛徒，是纳粹事业
的阻碍者，是无政府主义者，也是阴谋家。
我偏袒犹太雇员，并虐待雅利安女售货
员。

我没得到任何辩解的机会，就被命令回
到牢房。至此我仍未收到家人的任何消
息。我能听到其他受害者的尖叫和哀嚎：
鞭打的声音，身体瘫倒在地板上的闷响。
我能听到纳粹看守的笑声和咒骂声。

几天后，我被带出去，与其他半打人排
成一列，手铐连在一起，被带上卡车。我
们的目的地是 Fuhlsbuettel（富尔斯比特尔）。到达后，我
们面朝墙壁排成一列，被迫立正站立三个
小时！

当我们倒下时，看守扑向我们，踢打我
们之前受过伤的部位。我身边一位头发铁
灰的老绅士无法忍受；他呻吟着倒了下去。

两名看守抓住他，将他的头撞向地板。
他的假牙掉了下来，其中一名

pages.en:
103

of the troopers ground them to bits with his heel. A
guard drew his pistol and commanded, “Get up, you
swine!” The poor fellow tried to scramble to his feet.

“Cry Heil Hitler!”

The contorted mouth without teeth moaned some-
thing like the sigh of a dying beast.

The pistol butt smacked viciously against the blue-
veined temples.

“Teach him the Nazi salute!”

Again and again the butt rose and fell. Blood
spurted from his face. Once the gun hit an eye and
almost knocked it out.

When the prisoner went down for the second time
his head banged the stone floor near my feet, and he
didn’t rise again.

Finally they dragged his body out by the heels,
his head striking against stool legs, against a table,
against the doorway.

He died two days later in one of the dungeons.

103

队员用脚后跟将其碾碎。一名看守拔出
手枪，命令道：“起来，你这猪猡！”那个可
怜的家伙试图挣扎着站起来。

“喊‘希特勒万岁’！”

那张没有牙齿的扭曲嘴巴发出某种类似
垂死野兽叹息的声音。

枪托凶狠地砸在他青筋暴起的太阳穴
上。

“教他行纳粹礼！”

枪托一次次举起又落下。鲜血从他的脸
上喷涌而出。有一次枪托击中了一只眼
睛，差点把它打出来。

当这名囚犯第二次倒下时，他的头撞在
我脚边的石地板上，再也没有起来。

最后，他们抓住他的脚后跟将尸体拖出
去，他的头撞在凳子腿上、桌子上以及门
框上。

两天后，他死在其中一间地牢里。

pages.en:
104

After hours of waiting we were called by name and
led into another office for questioning. The officer in
charge eyed me sharply.

“Where did you get those bruises, man?”

I said truthfully, “In the district office.”

He lunged at me with his riding whip, striking my
face until the old cuts opened and the blood streamed
into my mouth.

“You dirty liar! Tell me again, where did you
get those bruises? The Communists did it because you
refused to murder Nazi comrades, isn’t that it?”

I nodded dumbly. It was no use.

I was given my number and assigned my place in
barracks.

The Jewish prisoners were segregated from our
barracks. They perished in underground dungeons; we
heard their moans. But we Aryans were not much
better off. There were tortures impossible to describe,
physical and mental. Beatings, workouts, unbearably
hard labour, uneatable food, solitary confinement. And
pages.zh:
104

经过数小时的等待，我们被点名叫到另
一间办公室接受审问。负责的官员严厉地
盯着我。

“你身上的淤青是怎么来的，伙计？”

我如实回答：“在区办公室。”

他用马鞭向我猛扑过来，抽打我的脸，
直到旧伤口裂开，鲜血流进我的嘴里。

“你这个肮脏的骗子！再告诉我一次，
这些淤青是怎么来的？是因为你拒绝谋杀
纳粹同志，所以共产党人打的，对吧？”

我麻木地点点头。这没用。

他们给了我编号，并分配了我在营房的
位置。

犹太囚犯与我们的营房隔离。他们在地
下地牢中死去；我们听到了他们的呻吟。
但我们雅利安人的处境也好不到哪里去。
有着难以描述的折磨，包括身体和精神两
方面。殴打、体能训练、难以忍受的重体
力劳动、难以下咽的食物、单独监禁。以及

pages.en:
105

the mental abasement! We were made to drink from
spittoons and toilets. We were given “cures”; the
mud cure; the pine cone cure; so obscene and disgusting
they cannot be printed.

I hereby state that I, Ernest Gunther Peterson
(fictional name), was kept a prisoner in the Fuehls-
buettel camp for nearly two years, part of which time I
was forced to spend in solitary confinement, chained to an
iron stool, fed with bread and water. I still don’t know
on what charge I have been imprisoned. I have never
been brought before a court, never been given a chance
to defend myself against my possible or impossible
charges.

I have been beaten. I have been kicked with heavy
boots. I have been lashed with riding whips. I have
been spat at, forced to crawl in the mud, made to drink
the contents of spittoons.

I have been forced to lie, to say things of which I
don’t believe a word. I have been forced by the threat
of death to raise my right arm and cry “Heil Hitler!”

I have been ruined. The honour of my family has
pages.zh:
105

精神上的羞辱！我们被迫从痰盂和马桶
中饮水。我们被给予“疗法”；泥疗；松果
疗法；其淫秽和令人作呕的程度无法付印。

我在此声明，我，恩斯特·冈瑟·彼得森
（Ernest Gunther Peterson，虚构姓名），在 Fuhlsbuettel（富尔斯比特尔）
集中营被囚禁近两年，期间部分时间被强
迫单独监禁，被铁链锁在铁凳上，仅靠面
包和水维持生命。我至今仍不知道因何罪
名被囚禁。我从未被带上法庭，也从未获
得机会针对可能或不可能存在的指控为自
己辩护。

我遭到殴打。我被穿着重靴的脚踢踹。
我被马鞭抽打。我被吐口水，被迫在泥泞
中爬行，被迫喝下痰盂里的东西。

我被迫撒谎，说出我自己一个字都不相
信的话。在死亡的威胁下，我被迫举起右
臂高呼“希特勒万岁！”

我被毁了。我家人的荣誉已

pages.en:
106

been besmirched. My relatives have been threatened
and persecuted beyond human endurance.

And on what grounds — on what substantiated charges
has all this been done?

There are no grounds — there were no grounds —
there never have been grounds. There was never a
trial never a direct accusation never a prosecutor —
never a defendant.

There was nothing but sheer, beastly brutality, so
help me God!

A GERMAN JEW'S STORY

I keep reminding myself, "Franz, you have nothing
more to fear. You are in America, where everyone is
free."

My mind understands, but my body and soul are
another matter. My flesh still cringes; my soul is sick.
Hundreds of thousands of my fellowmen are suffering
in Germany as I suffered, with no chance of escape.
There is an ocean between that blood-crazed madman
pages.zh:
106

受到玷污。我的亲属受到的威胁和迫害超
过了人类承受的极限。

而这所有的一切是基于什么理由——基
于什么确凿的指控？

没有理由——从来没有理由——从来就
没有过理由。从来没有审判，从来没有直
接的指控，从来没有检察官——从来没有
被告。

除了纯粹的、兽性的残暴之外，什么都
没有，上帝作证！

一个德国犹太人的故事

我不断提醒自己，“弗朗茨，你没什么好
怕的了。你在美国，这里每个人都是自由
的。”

我的理智明白这一点，但我的身体和灵
魂却是另一回事。我的肉体仍然畏缩；我
的灵魂病了。成千上万的同胞在德国遭受
着我曾遭受的苦难，且无处可逃。在那位
嗜血疯狂的疯子

pages.en:
107

and my wife, my son and myself, but no ocean can
separate my heart from my people. Nothing can erase
my memory of other Jews who suffer under the obscene
sadism of Hitler's henchmen.

I was born in Hamburg in 1897, of Jewish parents.
It is rumoured that my father was murdered outside
Hamburg during the terrible week of November 8; I know
nothing of my mother, who was 70 last spring. During
the World War I lost an eye, and a grateful government
gave me the Iron Cross, second class. In 1934 my little
boy dropped that decoration down the toilet by accident
one day, playing with it; I did not reprimand him.

After a few years of starvation in post-war
Germany I got a job in a Berlin bank; in 1928, in spite
of many attempts by "Aryans" to get me fired, I became teller. At night I studied banking and finance,
and attended courses in the Hochschule für Politik. In
1929 I was earning $35 a week, a good deal for a man
of 32 without college training. Enough to marry on.

Erika Grunberg was the sister of my closest companion in the war. Fritz was killed at Verdun, and I
pages.zh:
107

与我的妻子、儿子和我之间隔着一片海
洋，但没有任何海洋能将我的心与我的民
族分开。没有什么能抹去我对其他在希特
勒爪牙的淫秽施虐下受苦的犹太人的记
忆。

我于1897年出生在汉堡，父母是犹太人。
有传言说我父亲在11月8日那可怕的一周
期间在汉堡郊外被谋杀；对我去年春天已
满70岁的母亲，我一无所知。在第一次世
界大战中，我失去了一只眼睛，感激的政
府授予我二级铁十字勋章。1934年，我的小
男孩有一天玩耍时不小心把那枚勋章掉进
了马桶；我没有责备他。

在战后德国的几年饥荒之后，我在柏林
的一家银行找到了一份工作；1928年，尽管
“雅利安人”多次试图解雇我，我还是成
为了出纳员。晚上我学习银行和金融，并
在政治高等学院（Hochschule für Politik）上课。1929
年，我每周收入35美元，对于一个32岁且
没有大学学历的人来说，这是一笔不错的
收入。足够结婚用了。

埃丽卡·格伦伯格（Erika Grunberg）是我战时最亲密
伙伴的妹妹。弗里茨（Fritz）在凡尔登阵亡，我

pages.en:
108
married his sister, a golden-haired girl with the bluest
eyes in the world, and went to live in a tiny apartment
in the Kuntstrasse. We scraped and saved and put
our money in my bank, for it became more and more
likely that I would be fired for being a Jew. Even then
Hitler was Jew-baiting, and Mein Kampf was selling
widely.
On a Saturday night in October, Erika and I had
gone out to Potsdam to walk along the canal banks, our
last outing before our child should be born. About nine
o'clock we sat down on one of the benches. Four men
walked toward us, talking and shouting boisterously.
Two of them sat down heavily beside me and crowd-
ed me against my wife. Then a third pushed them.
Erika was knocked off and fell to the ground.
They began yelling in unison, "Dirty Jew! Dirty
Jew!"
I swung blindly at the nearest man. I felt my fist
crunch against his face, then went down under an as-
sault of kicks and blows. I cried, "Run, Erika!"
Then a boot landed in my stomach and I had no breath
left. I heard Erika cry out, then a splash.
pages.zh:
108
娶了他的妹妹，一个拥有世界上最蓝眼睛
的金发女孩，并搬进了昆特街（Kuntstrasse）的一间小公
寓。我们省吃俭用，把钱存在我的银行
里，因为我因是犹太人而被解雇的可能性
越来越大。即使在那时，希特勒也在煽动
反犹情绪，《我的奋斗》销量广泛。
十月的一个周六晚上，埃丽卡和我去波
茨坦沿着运河堤岸散步，这是孩子出生前
我们最后一次外出。大约九点钟，我们坐
在一条长椅上。四个男人朝我们走来，谈
笑着，大声喧哗。其中两人重重地坐在我
身边，将我挤向妻子。接着第三个人推搡
他们。埃丽卡被撞倒，摔在地上。
他们开始齐声大喊：“肮脏的犹太人！肮
脏的犹太人！”
我盲目地向最近的那个人挥拳。我感觉
拳头砸在他的脸上，随后在一阵拳打脚踢
下倒地。我喊道：“快跑，埃丽卡！”
接着一只靴子踢中了我的胃部，我喘不
过气来。我听到埃丽卡大叫一声，然后是
落水声。

pages.en:
109

With a final barrage of kicks the men turned and
ran, screaming over their shoulders, “Dirty Jews!”

Painfully I crawled to my feet. From the canal
behind me I heard a moan. There was my Erika,
struggling in the shallow water. . .

At the hospital they called it a miscarriage, but it
was six weeks before Erika could come home, and the
Polizei laughed at me when I made a complaint.

After the Austrian house-painter moved into the
Wilhelmstrasse and set the Reichstag afire, none of us
were safe. I never knew when I would return from the
bank to find Erika raped and murdered. This is not
an exaggeration, as you would know if you had lived
three years in Germany.

In 1933, in April, I was fired without warning. My
first son had been born five months before. For two
weeks, eight hours a day, I went jobhunting. I tried
all the banks, I applied at all the department stores,
but it was no use. Jews were being shoved about on
the streets, and spat on in the gutters. In the second
month I arrived home to find my door placarded with
pages.zh:
109

随着最后一阵猛踢，那些人转身跑开，
回头尖叫着：“肮脏的犹太人！”

我痛苦地爬起身来。从我身后的运河里
传来一声呻吟。那是我的埃丽卡，在浅水
中挣扎……

在医院里，他们称其为流产，但埃丽卡
六周后才能回家，当我提出投诉时，警察
嘲笑我。

在那位奥地利油漆工搬进威廉街
（Wilhelmstrasse）并纵火焚烧国会大厦后，我们谁都
不安全。我永远不知道何时从银行回来会
发现埃丽卡被强奸并杀害。这并不是夸
张，如果你在德国生活过三年就会知道。

1933年4月，我在毫无预警的情况下被解
雇。我的第一个儿子在五个月前出生。在
接下来的两周里，我每天花八个小时找工
作。我试遍了所有银行，申请了所有百货
公司，但都无济于事。犹太人在街上被推
搡，在沟渠里被吐口水。第二个月，我回
到家，发现门上贴满了

pages.en:
110
the "Yellow Spot". This meant that Aryan trades
people could not deal with us; Erika had to walk half
a mile to get milk until three months later, when a Jew
was permitted to set up a dairy store near us.

The Yellow Spot was not mere mockery for other
reasons also. Today in the Third Reich Jews are
blamed for all venereal diseases as well as for tuber-
culosis; scores of Jews have been beaten to death for
being consumptive, and when a Jewish name is reported
by a doctor as having contracted gonorrhea or syphilis
the word is passed along to the Lokal of the Brown
Shirts. . . . Hans Schmidt, a young mechanic who
lived near me, went for tubercular treatment to a Jewish
doctor. The Nazis broke into the doctor's office, stole
his records, and rounded up, stripped and whipped
twelve anaemic men and two young girls whose names
they found in the physician's files. The police did
nothing. Hans died two months afterward of blood
poisoning from beating with rubber truncheons. He
was too terrified to go to another doctor.

In 1934 they posted outside our door one of those
dread bright-red "Sturmer" boxes, or bulletin boards,
pages.zh:
110
“黄点区”。这意味着雅利安裔商人不能与我们做生意；埃丽卡不得不步行半英里去买牛奶，直到三个月后，一名犹太人被允许在我们附近开设一家乳品店。

出于其他原因，“黄点区”也不仅仅是侮辱。如今在第三帝国，犹太人不仅被指责传播所有性病，还被指责传播结核病；数十名犹太人因患有肺结核而被殴打致死，当医生报告某位犹太姓名者感染淋病或梅毒时，消息便会传达到褐衫军的地方分部（Lokal）……汉斯·施密特（Hans Schmidt），一位住在我附近的年轻技工，去找一位犹太医生治疗结核病。纳粹分子闯入医生的诊所，偷走了他的病历，并根据医生档案中找到的名字，围捕、剥光并鞭打了十二名贫血男子和两名年轻女孩。警察对此无动于衷。汉斯在两个月后因被橡胶警棍殴打导致的败血症而死亡。他因极度恐惧而不敢去看其他医生。

1934年，他们在我们门外张贴了那些可怕的鲜红色“冲锋队”信箱或公告板之一，

pages.en:
111
on which was recounted all the fictional sins of Jews
in our neighbourhood. The “biographical note” about
me stated that I had been arrested as a juvenile delin-
quent in Hamburg for attempting to rape my aunt—
(I didn’t have an aunt). I had shown cowardice at the
front—where I had lost an eye and part of my right
leg—and was known to participate in “ritualistic
murders of Gentile infants, after which this sodden
Gluckstein drinks their blood with other Jewish sows.”

They were scarcely kinder to my wife. As a
revenge on “pure, manly Aryans” she had infected
hundreds of them in a Magdeburg brothel.

We were expecting another child, and in despera-
tion I wrote to my father for help, although his small
business had shrunk. He sent me 2000 marks, a
sacrifice I hate to think of, and urged me to open a
small stationery and tobacco shop where Jews could
purchase papers.

By 1936 all of us in Charlottenburg were resigned
to death and destruction. One night after closing my
shop I went for a cup of coffee with a friend, an under-
pages.zh:
111
上面罗列了我们邻里间犹太人的所有虚构罪行。关于我的“生平简介”声称，我曾在汉堡因企图强奸我的姨妈而作为少年犯被捕——（我根本没有姨妈）。我在前线表现出怯懦——在那里我失去了一只眼睛和部分右腿——并且已知参与“仪式性谋杀非犹太婴儿，此后这个醉醺醺的格卢克斯坦（Gluckstein）与其他犹太母猪一起饮用他们的血液。”

他们对我也妻子也毫不留情。作为对“纯洁、阳刚的雅利安人”的报复，她在马格德堡的一家妓院里感染了数百人。

我们正期待另一个孩子的降生，在绝望中，我写信向父亲求助，尽管他的小生意已经萎缩。他寄给我2000马克，这是一笔让我不忍回想的牺牲，并敦促我开一家小型文具烟草店，以便犹太人能够购买报纸。

到1936年，我们夏洛滕堡（Charlottenburg）的所有人都已听天由命，准备迎接死亡与毁灭。一天晚上，关店后，我和一位朋友去喝杯咖啡，那是一位身材矮小的犹太裁缝。

pages.en:
112

sized Jewish tailor. The waiter had just brought out
coffee when an SA man purposely banged against our
table and upset the coffee in our laps. I got up,
trembling and white with rage, and saw 30 more of them
coming at us, laughing and shouting insults.

Ten of them literally lifted us off the ground and
carried us to a truck across the sidewalk; we were
tossed in and driven about 15 minutes while they all sat
on us. I never recovered from the injury to my spine
that night.

We were pushed into one of the Brown Shirt
Lokals, and stripped of our clothes. Two youths went
through our coats and took all our money and papers.
Then we were kicked and beaten over the head and
shoulders with rubber truncheons. Blood ran into my
own eye and I couldn't see. I stumbled around with
outstretched arms.

The sport for these Nazis was immense! A Jew,
naked, blinded, covered with blood, was as good if not
better than a cartoon in Der Stürmer.

They made me denounce Judea in obscene terms.
pages.zh:
112

服务员刚端出咖啡，一名冲锋队（SA）成员故意撞向我们的桌子，将咖啡打翻在我们腿上。我站起身，因愤怒而颤抖且面色苍白，看到又有三十名这样的人向我们走来，笑着并高声辱骂。

他们中的十个人 literally 将我们抬离地面，穿过人行道把我们塞进一辆卡车；我们被扔进车里，在他们全都坐在我们身上的情况下被驱车兜风约15分钟。我那晚遭受的脊柱损伤从未痊愈。

我们被推进一个褐衫军的地方分部（Lokal），衣服被剥光。两个年轻人搜遍我们的外套，拿走了所有的钱和证件。然后他们用橡胶警棍踢打我们的头部和肩膀。鲜血流进我自己的眼睛，使我无法视物。我伸出双臂，踉跄徘徊。

这些纳粹分子的娱乐兴致极高！一个赤身裸体、双目失明、浑身是血的犹太人，即便不比《冲锋报》（Der Stürmer）上的漫画更好，至少也与之相当。

他们迫使我用淫秽的语言谴责犹太民族。

pages.en:
113
repeating ten times over such phrases: "The Jew's big
nose belongs in a bucket of excrement. So does that
of his wife. So does that of his filthy Jew-brats."

I fainted in the middle of this; they threw water
over me, dragged me to my feet, and in unison Paul and
I were made to read selected sentences from "Mein
Kampf". Blood dripped from my forehead on the copy
in my hands: for this "sacrilege" I was knocked down.

At last they were finished. We were kicked out
into the back yard; made to shout Heil, Hitler! ten
times, standing naked in the snow, and then they left.
Paul and I helped each other on with our clothes.
The poor little tailor's left wrist was broken; the bones
stuck out of his skin. Every few moments he screamed
with pain.

Somehow we got over the fence; an American news
paper correspondent picked us up and took us to a
doctor, who, in spite of the sign on his door, "Beware,
a Jew! Consultation Forbidden!" took us in and
took care of us.

My second son, Richard, was born early in 1937.
pages.zh:
113
重复十遍这样的短语：“犹太人的大鼻子该放进一桶粪便里。他妻子的鼻子也是。他那肮脏的犹太小鬼们的鼻子也是。”

我在此过程中昏厥过去；他们向我泼水，将我拖起站立，并让保罗和我齐声朗读《我的奋斗》中的选段。鲜血从我额头滴落在我手中的副本上：因这一“亵渎”行为，我被击倒在地。

最后他们终于结束了。我们被踢进后院；被迫在雪地中赤身裸体站立，高喊十次“希特勒万岁！”，然后他们离开了。保罗和我互相帮对方穿上衣服。那位可怜的小裁缝左手腕骨折；骨头刺穿了皮肤。他每隔片刻便因疼痛而尖叫。

不知怎的，我们翻过了围栏；一位美国报社通讯员发现了我们，并将我们带到一位医生那里。尽管他门上挂着“当心，是犹太人！禁止问诊！”的牌子，他还是收治并照顾了我们。

我的第二个儿子理查德于1937年初出生。

pages.en:
114

He was constantly ill; his birth was not normal because
Erika had for months been nervous, given to spells of
depression, and without the right food. She was un-
able to nurse the baby, but he seemed determined to
live, although at the age of six months he weighed only
11 pounds.

I was arranging newspapers in my shop in April,
1937, and saw a headline in Hitler's paper, announcing
"The Modest Beginnings of a Modest Purge of the
Jews." Three days later a little boy came running into
the shop, screaming that the Brown Shirts were in my
apartment, maltreating Erika. I ran out of the place,
leaving it unguarded. I found Erika in the living-room
of the wrecked apartment building, sprawled on the
floor. There was blood all over her face. She was
blood all over her face. She was unconscious. Her
clothes were torn half off. . . . .

At last her eyes opened. She began to scream
hysterically until she recognized me. Four-months-old
Richard was crying loudly in the crib I had made of
old boxes.
pages.zh:
114

他经常生病；他的出生并不正常，因为埃丽卡在数月间一直神经紧张，时有抑郁发作，且缺乏适当的食物。她无法哺乳婴儿，但他似乎决心活下去，尽管在六个月大时体重仅11磅。

1937年4月，我正在店里整理报纸，看到希特勒的报纸上有一则标题，宣布“对犹太人进行适度清洗的 modest 开端”。三天后，一个小男孩跑进店里，尖叫着说褐衫军正在我的公寓里虐待埃丽卡。我跑出店铺， leaving it unguarded。我在被毁坏的公寓楼的客厅里找到了埃丽卡，她瘫倒在地板上。她满脸是血。她满脸是血。她失去了知觉。她的衣服被撕掉了一半……

最后她睁开了眼睛。她开始歇斯底里地尖叫，直到认出是我。四个月大的理查德在我用旧箱子做的摇篮里大声哭泣。

pages.en:
115

Erika, screaming, told me that SA men had broken
in, demanding to see my police papers (which had been
stolen that night at the Lokal). They told her I was a
Communist and that the Gestapo had ordered my arrest.
They had ransacked the place and a couple of them
spat on Richard. To terrify Erika they got knives in
the kitchen and said they would slit the baby's throat
if she wouldn't show them where I kept my money.
She rushed over and clawed at one of the men.

The Brown Shirts knocked her down.

Two of them held her and the other two attacked
her. Then she lost consciousness.

Late in 1937, four days before Chanukah, Storm
Troopers burst into my shop and wrecked it. I was
under arrest for selling Communist literature. The
Nazis, of course, had planted Soviet propaganda on the
shelves; no sane Jew would have dared sell such pam-
phlets, or possess them!

Without semblance of a trial I was sent to the
concentration camp of Oranienburg-Sachsenhausen on
an indeterminate sentence. The brutalities of that cess-
pages.zh:
115

埃丽卡尖叫着告诉我，冲锋队（SA）成员破门而入，要求查看我的警察证件（那些证件当晚在地方分部已被盗走）。他们告诉她我是共产党人，盖世太保已下令逮捕我。他们洗劫了住所，其中几人还朝理查德吐口水。为了恐吓埃丽卡，他们从厨房拿来刀具，说如果她不指出我把钱藏在哪里，他们就割断婴儿的喉咙。她冲过去抓挠其中一人。

褐衫军将她击倒。

两人按住她，另外两人攻击她。随后她失去了知觉。

1937年末，光明节（Chanukah）前四天，突击队员冲进我的店铺并将其砸毁。我因出售共产主义文献而被捕。当然，是纳粹分子将苏联宣传品放置在货架上的；没有哪个神志正常的犹太人敢出售或拥有此类小册子！

未经任何类似审判的程序，我便以不定刑期被送往奥拉宁堡-萨克森豪森（Oranienburg-Sachsenhausen）集中营。那个污秽之地的暴行

pages.en:
116
pool are well known and I do not suppose my ex-
periences were better or worse than those of others.
For three months I was there, unable to get word from
Erika. One outstanding refinement was always on
Saturday, the Jewish Sabbath: they collected those of
us who wished to hear the rabbi preach, and followed
him into the yard to a small mountain of manure.
Here he was made to stand in the center, naked, waist
high while he read, and we were placed in a circle round
him and forced to shovel manure on top of him.

Near the end of my imprisonment at one of these
rabbinical services, two newcomers turned on the guards
and struck them with their shovels. They were shot
down, riddled with bullets.

When at last I was released I learned that my
second son Richard, the baby, had been murdered.

The Nazis had again “purged” our apartment-
building. . . .

I lost all self-respect after that. I used to hang
round the Freidrichstrasse Banhof until the last
wagon-lit had left for Paris with the well-to-do tourists.
pages.zh:
116
众所周知，我想我的经历并不会比其他人更好或更糟。我在那里待了三个月，无法得到埃丽卡的任何消息。有一个特别“精致”的做法总是在星期六，即犹太安息日进行：他们召集我们这些想听拉布比讲道的人，跟着他走进院子，来到一小堆粪肥前。在这里，他被强迫站在中心，赤裸上身至腰部，一边朗读，而我们被安排围成一圈，被迫将粪肥铲到他身上。

在我囚禁接近尾声的一次此类拉比服务中，两名新来者转向警卫，用铁锹击打他们。他们随即被枪杀，身中数弹。

当我最终获释时，我得知我的第二个儿子理查德，那个婴儿，已被谋杀。

纳粹分子再次“清洗”了我们的公寓楼……

从那以后，我失去了所有的自尊。我常常在弗里德里希大街车站（Friedrichstrasse Bahnhof）徘徊，直到最后一班载着富裕游客前往巴黎的卧铺车厢离开。

pages.en:
117

then I would sleep in a corner of the baggage-room,
because the overnight timekeeper had pity on me. My
father guessed something was wrong because he did
not hear from me; and Erika had been afraid to write,
knowing the mail was opened and read. Through a
friend in the Czech consulate in Berlin he located me
in September. His friend let me use his office phone.

My father didn't recognize my voice. He thought
someone was talking from a prison, trying to get in-
formation. He told me in Yiddish, as obliquely as he
could, to try for the Dutch frontier at Emden, and he
would have Erika there if it was humanly possible.

"Your Mother's and my life is finished," he told
me, "I am sending you money. Now go as soon as
you can, and we'll get Erika up to Emden."

The following morning at the GPO I got 5000
marks, after my friends had identified me, for I had
no papers. My father had of course sold his business
at a pawn-shop price.

I met Erika at Emden, but I scarcely recognized
her. She was a middle-aged woman, with gray, stringy
pages.zh:
117

然后我便睡在行李房的一个角落里，因为夜班计时员对我心存怜悯。我父亲猜到出了事，因为他没有收到我的音讯；而埃丽卡因知道邮件会被开封阅读，不敢写信。通过他在柏林捷克领事馆的一位朋友，他在九月找到了我。他的朋友让我使用其办公室的电话。

我父亲没听出我的声音。他以为有人从监狱打电话，试图获取信息。他用意第绪语尽可能含蓄地告诉我，尝试前往埃姆登（Emden）的荷兰边境，如果人力所能及，他会把埃丽卡送到那里。

“你母亲和我的生命已经完结，”他告诉我，“我给你寄钱。现在尽快离开，我们会把埃丽卡送到埃姆登。”

第二天早上在中央邮局（GPO），在朋友们证实我的身份后，我拿到了5000马克，因为我没有任何证件。我父亲当然是以典当般的低价卖掉了他的生意。

我在埃姆登见到了埃丽卡，但我几乎认不出她。她像个中年妇女，头发灰白、枯槁，

pages.en:
118

hair and a rigid face.

It took us three weeks to get across the frontier;
our marks outside Germany were valueless. At last the
U.S. consul at Rotterdam granted us a visitors' visa.

I still cannot realize I am in America. But just
yesterday, as I was coming out of the subway, somebody
shoved a pamphlet into my hands. I stared blankly at
these words:

"Awake, White Christian Americans."

Yes, I am in America; I am free. Over and over
I remind myself of that. I am free. I am in America.

But I am afraid, still. I feel in the air the fetid
breath of that vicious, unreasoning hatred I knew so
well in Germany. And I am sick and desolate from
wounds which can never heal.

WHOM THE GODS WOULD DESTROY
THEY FIRST MAKE MAD.
pages.zh:
118

面容僵硬。

我们花了三周时间才越过边境；我们在德国境外的马克毫无价值。最后，美国驻鹿特丹领事授予我们访客签证。

我仍然无法意识到自己身在美国。但就在昨天，当我走出地铁时，有人将一本小册子塞进我手中。我茫然地盯着这些文字：

“觉醒吧，白人基督教美国人。”

是的，我在美国；我是自由的。我一遍又一遍地提醒自己这一点。我是自由的。我在美国。

但我仍然感到恐惧。我在空气中感受到了那种恶毒、非理性的仇恨气息，这种气息我在德国如此熟悉。而且，因那些永远无法愈合的创伤，我感到病痛缠身且孤寂凄凉。

神欲使其灭亡，必先使其疯狂。

Subject "A Nightmare Comes True" Anti-Nazi booklet distributed in the

"A Nightmare Comes True", a booklet containing
violent anti-Nazi sentiments is being distributed to
foreign homes in the Settlement and French Concession,
copies being placed in the letter boxes.

The authorship is anonymous but a study
of the contents indicates that it is probably the
work of a Jewish organization.

A copy of the booklet which was placed in
all letter boxes in Avenue Apartments, Avenue and
Hardoon Roads on the night of September 30th/October
1st is attached herewith.

R.W. Mac Adie.

Subject Communist pamphlet in German distributed through the

Made by D.J. Pitts. Forwarded by Thorne D.S.I

Forwarded herewith is a copy of "Deutsche Schanghai
VOLKSFRONT - 1936-G," (SHANGHAI GERMAN POPULAR FRONT), which
was distributed through the mails to certain local Germans
who are not members of the Nazi organisation. Translation
is also attached.
This particular pamphlet, which is communist in
nature, is one of a series of this type, which have been
sent through the mails on several occasions. This copy
was received by a certain German on January 27, 1937.
The contents of the pamphlet are similar to articles
which have appeared from time to time in the International
Press Correspondence, but the actual matter is several
months old, many of the trials mentioned having taken place
last summer or in the early autumn.
Attempts are now being made to ascertain the source
of this pamphlet.

DER BRAUNE SCHRECKEN ZIEHT DURCHS LAND

Wir haben nie einem Gegner von uns etwas
zu Leide getan. Nie wurde einem Juden ein
Haar gekrümmt. Auf unserem Weg liegt kein er-
schlagener Gegner, erfolgte kein Attentat.
                                        Hitler
    Wir fühlen uns mit allen verbunden, die in Deutschland für
den Frieden kämpfen oder im Kampf für Freiheit und Recht den Faschisten
in die Hände fallen.
    Wir sehen immer mehr, wie unlösbar das terroristische Wüten
des Faschismus mit seinen kriegerischen Abenteuern verknüpft ist. In
einem Lande wo durch Reichsgesetz selbst die zehnjährigen Buben und
Mädchen in die Kandare der Zwangsmilitarisierung gepresst werden, muss
der Faschismus jeden als seinen Todfeind ansehen, der das Banner des
Friedens und Völkerversöhnung erhöht.
    Nach unvollständigen Angaben der I.A.H. (amtliche Zahlen
gibt es wohlweislich nicht) wurden von März 1933 bis Anfangs 1936 in
Deutschland rund 5000 Menschen ermordet und 61 wegen politischen Vergeh-
en durch das Handbeil hingerichtet. In 5500 Prozessen wurden 21.000
Menschen zu rund 40.000 Jahren Zuchthaus verurteilt. Wollte man den Frei-
heitsentzug durch die Vorhängung der Haft in Konzentrationslagern be-
rechnen, dann kämen für die genannte Zeit ungefähr 300.000 eingekerkerte
Menschen mit über 100.000 Jahren Zuchthaus heraus.
    Folterungen und Tod sind tägliche Gäste in den Gefängnissen
Hitlers, Görings und Göbbels. Denkt an die Schreie der Gequälten und Ge-
marterten. Denkt an die blutige Agonie von Richard Claus und John Scheer
Scheer wurde noch kurz vor seiner Hinrichtung gefoltert, er wurde an
einen glühenden Ofen gestossen, bis der Raum von den penetranten Geruch
verbrannten Fleisches erfüllt war. Oskar Hoffmann, Redakteur aus Elberfeldt.
wurde von den Wecke-Garden verhaftet. Um ein Geständnis zu erzwingen
wurden ihm Bart und Kopfhaare ausgerissen und der Sechziger musste drei
extra mit Salz dick überschüttete Salzheringe essen, die vorher mit einem
Schmieröl eingeschmiert wurden. Der alte Mann bricht sofort darauf mit
Magenkrämpfen zusammen. Grund genug ihn mit Knüppeln blutig zu schlagen
und in ein metallenes, viel zu kleines Kleiderspind zu sperren.
    Der Herzschlag stockt bei den grauenhaften und vorsätzlichen
Morden, die täglich von den Beamten des dritten Reiches im Auftrag der
Regierung verübt werden. In Sachsen kommen nach der Aufdeckung des Mas-
sackers an achtzehn Antifaschisten im Konzentrationslager Hohenstein
neue viehische Verbrechen an den Tag: Der Arbeiter Engelhardt in Nieder-
hasslau; von der S.S. in der Haft erschlagen! Der Arbeiter Liepold aus
Liebersdorf; von der Gestapo zu Tode getreten! Der Redakteur Sachs von
der "Dresdener Volkszeitung"; im Konzentrationslager Sachsenburg neun
Tage nach der Einlieferung zu Tode geprügelt! Helmut Walter aus Reichen-
bach und Arbeiter Lorenz aus Planitz; im Krankenhaus an den Folgen der
Haftmisshandlungen gestorben! Paul Schraps; in Sachsenburg verblutet!
Hans Seidel aus Kramm bei Neustadt; Brustkorb eingestampft.

德意志
上海
1936-6
人民阵线

褐色的恐怖席卷全国

我们从未伤害过我们的任何敌人。从未有一根犹太人的头发被弯曲。在我们的道路上没有倒下的敌人，也没有发生过暗杀事件。
                                        希特勒
    我们与所有在德国为和平而战，或在为自由和正义的斗争中落入法西斯分子手中的人感同身受。
    我们越来越清楚地看到，法西斯主义的恐怖暴行与其战争冒险密不可分。在一个连十岁的男孩和女孩都被帝国法律强行纳入强制军事化笼头的国家，法西斯主义必须将每一个高举和平与民族和解旗帜的人视为其死敌。
    根据国际工人救济会（I.A.H.）的不完整数据（显然没有官方数据），从1933年3月到1936年初，德国约有5000人被谋杀，61人因政治犯罪被断头台处决。在5500起诉讼中，21,000人被判处约40,000年的监禁。如果要计算因被关押在集中营而剥夺的自由，那么在这段时间内，大约有30万人被监禁，相当于超过10万年的监禁刑期。
    酷刑和死亡是希特勒、戈林和戈培尔监狱里的日常常客。想想那些受折磨者和受难者的尖叫。想想理查德·克劳斯（Richard Claus）和约翰·谢尔（John Scheer）的血腥痛苦。谢尔在处决前不久还遭受了酷刑，他被推到一个炽热的炉子上，直到房间里充满了烧焦肉体的刺鼻气味。奥skar·霍夫曼（Oskar Hoffmann），来自埃尔伯费尔德（Elberfeldt）的编辑。被韦克卫队（Wecke-Garden）逮捕。为了逼供，他的胡须和头发被拔掉，这位六十多岁的老人被迫吃下三条额外撒满厚盐、并事先涂有润滑油的咸鲱鱼。老人随即因胃痉挛而倒下。这足以成为用棍棒将他打得鲜血淋漓，并将他锁进一个金属制的、太小而不合适的衣柜里的理由。
    面对第三帝国官员奉政府之命每天实施的可怕且蓄意的谋杀，心脏几乎停止跳动。在萨克森，在霍恩施泰因（Hohenstein）集中营十八名反法西斯主义者遭到屠杀的真相被揭露后，新的兽行罪行又暴露出来： Niederhasslau 的工人恩格尔哈特（Engelhardt）；在拘留期间被党卫军（S.S.）殴打致死！来自 Liebersdorf 的工人利波尔德（Liepold）；被盖世太保（Gestapo）踩踏致死！《德累斯顿人民报》（"Dresdener Volkszeitung"）的编辑萨克斯（Sachs）；在萨克森堡（Sachsenburg）集中营，入狱九天后被殴打致死！来自赖兴巴赫（Reichenbach）的赫尔穆特·沃尔特（Helmut Walter）和来自普拉尼茨（Planitz）的工人洛伦茨（Lorenz）；在医院死于拘留期间虐待造成的后果！保罗·施拉普斯（Paul Schraps）；在萨克森堡流血而死！来自诺伊施塔特附近克拉姆（Kramm bei Neustadt）的汉斯·赛德尔（Hans Seidel）；胸腔被踩塌。
